objects.description: Primary parameter aggregate for creating/loading a torrent in a libtorrent session. Holds metadata (torrent_info or info hashes), storage and path options, initial priorities, trackers, web seeds, peers, and various resume/scrape/time counters. Constructors and destructor are declared here; definitions are elsewhere. Many fields are ABI-conditional. Use to add torrents via session::add_torrent() or async_add_torrent().

Alias of either boost::asio::ip::address or sim::asio::ip::address, depending on build flags. This header does not define the type itself; it brings it into the libtorrent namespace via using-declaration.
Alias of either boost::asio::ip::address_v4 or sim::asio::ip::address_v4. Introduced into libtorrent namespace via using-declaration.
Alias of either boost::asio::ip::address_v6 or sim::asio::ip::address_v6. Introduced into libtorrent namespace via using-declaration.
Alias of boost::asio::ip::network_v4. Introduced into libtorrent namespace via using-declaration.

Abstract base class for all libtorrent alert messages. Non-copyable, movable. Provides timestamp and virtual interface for type identification, description, and category. Also exposes per-category static bitflag constants. Constructed internally only.

objects.definition: using alert_category_t = flags::bitfield_flag<std::uint32_t, struct alert_category_tag>;
objects.description: Strongly-typed bitmask representing alert categories, backed by uint32_t, tagged by alert_category_tag. Used to enable/disable groups of alerts.
Priority levels used internally to rank alerts when the alert queue overflows. Lower numeric value has lower priority and will be dropped first.
Holds stats for a single DHT routing table bucket: number of nodes, replacements and seconds since last activity.
Base alert carrying a torrent_handle. Many derived alerts for torrent-specific events inherit from this.
Base alert for peer-specific events. Includes endpoint and peer_id.
Base alert for tracker-related events. Adds tracker URL and local listen endpoint used for the announce.
Posted when a torrent is removed. Carries info-hashes and client userdata; handle may soon become invalid.
Completion of torrent_handle::read_piece(). On success carries buffer/size for the piece; on failure error set and buffer null.
Emitted when an individual file completes (all overlapping pieces verified). Contains file index.
Success result of torrent_handle::rename_file(). Provides new and old names and file index.
Failure result of torrent_handle::rename_file(). Holds file index and filesystem error.
Warns about conditions that may hurt performance (disk queue limits, request queue, rate limits, etc.).
Emitted when a torrent changes state; carries new and previous state.
Tracker announce failure. Includes error, times in a row failed, operation and optional failure reason string.
Tracker announce success with a warning message. Provides warning string and announced protocol version.
Tracker scrape succeeded. Carries complete/incomplete counts and protocol version.
Tracker scrape failed. Contains error and possibly an error string from the tracker.
Tracker announce succeeded. Contains number of peers and protocol version.
DHT get_peers reply delivering peers for a torrent. Carries count.
Posted when a tracker announce is sent (or attempted). Includes event and protocol version.
Piece failed hash check. Contains piece index.
Peer was banned due to corrupt data. Peer endpoint in base class.
Peer previously snubbed has resumed sending data.
Peer is snubbed due to stalling or not sending data.
Peer disconnected due to protocol error. Contains low-level op and error.
Peer connection established (incoming or outgoing). Includes socket_type and direction.
Peer connection closed. Provides socket type, operation, error and optional close reason.
Debug alert for invalid piece request from a peer. Includes request and related flags.
Torrent switched to seed state (finished downloading).
A piece finished downloading and passed hash check.
Peer rejected or ignored a block request.
A requested block timed out without response.
A requested block was received.
A block request was sent to a peer (placed for download).
Received a block that was not requested (or request timed out).
Files successfully moved after torrent_handle::move_storage(). Provides new and old paths.
move_storage() failed. Contains error, file path (if applicable) and operation.
Files of a torrent were deleted successfully. Includes info-hashes.
Deleting a torrent's files failed. Carries error and info-hashes.
Result of torrent_handle::save_resume_data(). On success carries populated add_torrent_params.
Failed to generate resume data for a torrent. Contains error.
Torrent paused and all files closed (I/O synchronized).
Torrent resumed from paused state.
Torrent finished initial file checking and is ready to start.
Web seed error or message. Contains URL and either error code or textual message.
Storage read/write error caused the torrent to be paused. Includes operation and filename.
Failure to verify or parse fetched metadata for a magnet torrent.
Magnet torrent received full metadata and can start downloading.
Error on a UDP socket (used by uTP, DHT, UDP trackers).
Emitted when libtorrent learns its external IP address.
Listening on a specified interface/port failed. Contains operation, error, socket_type, attempted address/port and interface string.
Listening succeeded on given address/port and socket type.
UPnP/NAT-PMP mapping failed on a router. Includes mapping index, transport, local address and error.
UPnP/NAT-PMP mapping succeeded. Carries mapping id, external port, protocol, transport and local network.
Informational log line for UPnP/NAT-PMP operations (requires port_mapping_log category).
Provided fast-resume data was rejected; includes error, file (if any) and operation.
Peer was blocked (by IP/port filter, i2p rules, privileged ports, protocol disabled, invalid local interface or SSRF mitigation).
A DHT node announced to our DHT for a specific info-hash.
A DHT node sent a get_peers query to our node for the specified info-hash.
Disk cache flush for a torrent completed (e.g., after flush_cache() or removal).
Received a Local Service Discovery peer for a torrent.
Tracker replied with a trackerid. Stored and repeated in later announces.
Initial DHT bootstrap completed.
Torrent transitioned into error state. Contains error and optional filename/object.
SSL torrent needs certificate set via set_ssl_certificate() before it can work.
Accepted an incoming connection (TCP/uTP/SSL/SOCKS/i2p).
Result of adding a torrent. On success, handle valid and params contains key fields; on failure, error set.
Posted on request via post_torrent_updates(). Contains torrent_status for torrents that changed.
Posted in response to post_session_stats(). Carries session counters sequence; not filtered by alert mask.
Error occurred in DHT subsystem. Includes operation and error.
Response to get of immutable DHT item. Carries target hash and decoded entry.
Response to get of mutable DHT item. Includes public key, signature, salt, sequence number and authoritative flag.
Completion of a DHT put operation (immutable or mutable). Includes number of successful stores.
Reports errors in the i2p SAM connection.
Posted when we send a DHT get_peers query. Includes destination and (possibly obfuscated) target.
Session-wide debug/information log line (requires session_log category and build support).
Torrent-specific logging line (requires torrent_log category and build support).
Peer-specific logging. Includes direction, event type and formatted message.
Local Service Discovery socket failed to start on a local network. Contains network and error.
Snapshot of a DHT traversal (lookup) operation: counters and target ID.
Posted in response to post_dht_stats(). Contains routing table buckets, active lookups, local node ID and socket.
Posted whenever an incoming peer request is queued to be serviced.
Debug log line from DHT (module-qualified). Requires dht_log category.
Verbatim DHT packet sent or received (for debugging). Buffer valid while alert is alive.
Response to a DHT get_peers with the peers returned.
Posted once per dht_direct_request(), with the response if any (or empty on timeout).
Verbose piece picker logging. Indicates strategy flags and the list of picked piece_blocks.
Serious, potentially fatal, session-wide error with optional message.
Response to dht_live_nodes(). Lists nodes currently in the routing table.
First-time header corresponding to session stats values, printed for alignment with session_stats_alert.
Response to dht_sample_infohashes(). Provides sample keys, more nodes and interval hint.
A block was queued in the send buffer to be uploaded to a peer (may not have actually been sent yet).
Indicates some alerts were dropped before delivery. Contains a bitset by alert type id for which were dropped.
SOCKS5 proxy-related error. Includes proxy endpoint, operation and error.
Completion of prioritize_files() / file_priority() round-trip to disk thread. If it fails, file_error_alert is posted instead.
During initial file/resume check, a file on disk was larger than expected. Client may truncate or handle conflict.
Two magnet links resolved to the same torrent (duplicate). Carries conflicting handle and received metadata.
Response to torrent_handle::post_peer_info(). Contains the list of peer_info objects.
Response to torrent_handle::post_file_progress(). Carries per-file progress values.
Response to torrent_handle::post_download_queue(). Contains partial_piece_info list and backing block_info storage.
Response to torrent_handle::post_piece_availability(). Contains availability per piece.
Response to torrent_handle::post_trackers(). Contains list of trackers and their status.

Per-infohash tracker-announce state for a single tracker endpoint. Tracks scheduling, failure counts/flags, last error, optional scrape stats, and whether start/complete events have been sent. Used by announce_endpoint to manage announcements for v1/v2 info hashes. Construction is internal; users typically access instances via announce_endpoint::info_hashes.

Holds per-listen-socket tracker state for a single tracker, including the local TCP endpoint and an array of announce_infohash objects (one per supported protocol version). Controls whether this endpoint participates in announces.

Represents a single tracker entry for a torrent. Stores the tracker URL, trackerid parameter, per-endpoint announce state, tier, failure limit, and a bitmask of sources it came from. Provides deprecated helpers and an enum tracker_source bitmask.

Standard library string class referenced by this header when assertions and debugging utilities are enabled. It is not defined in this header (comes from <string>), so it should be ignored per instructions.

objects.definition: extern TORRENT_EXPORT char const* libtorrent_assert_log;
objects.description: External C-style string pointer used to direct libtorrent production assert logging. Declaration only; the definition is elsewhere. Not a custom type; included here only as a declaration note. Per instructions, this should generally be ignored since it is not a user-defined type.

Enumeration of bdecode parser error codes used with libtorrent's bdecode_category. Values cover common parse failures and limits. Suitable for constructing boost::system::error_code via make_error_code().

Internal token structure used by the bdecoder to represent parsed items compactly. Stores type, relative links to next items, and offsets/headers into the source buffer. Not intended for public API use; owned and managed by bdecode_node for parsed trees.

Public node type representing parsed bencoded data. Instances are either owning roots (manage token storage and buffer pointer) or non-owning child views into the root's token array. Provides typed accessors for dict/list/string/int nodes and utilities to manage/inspect the parse tree.
direct_api_constructors: libtorrent::bdecode(char const*, char const*, libtorrent::bdecode_node&, libtorrent::error_code&, int*, int, int)
libtorrent::bdecode(libtorrent::span<char const>, libtorrent::error_code&, int*, int, int)

objects.description: Type alias to boost::system::error_code used throughout the API for reporting errors. This header defines the alias only; construction follows boost::system semantics.

Resizable heap-backed bitset type for libtorrent. Stores bit count and 32-bit word array, supports querying, setting/clearing bits, counting, searching, iteration (const_iterator), resizing, and bulk operations. Size is stored in m_buf[0]; bits follow in network-bit-order per word. Some methods are only declared here (all_set, count, find_first_set, find_last_clear) and defined elsewhere.

Forward iterator over bits in a libtorrent::bitfield. Holds a pointer to current 32-bit word and a mask bit; supports pre/post increment/decrement and equality. Constructible only by bitfield via private constructor; used with bitfield::begin/end.

Peer Exchange (ut_pex) peer store for a single remote peer. It tracks limited-size lists of IPv4 and IPv6 peers (address bytes + port) that the remote peer reported via PEX, used for provenance/lookup such as holepunch introductions. Provides a query to check if an endpoint was an introducer. Lifetime managed externally; virtual destructor allows polymorphic deletion.

BitTorrent wire-protocol peer connection. Implements message parsing/dispatch, feature negotiation (extensions, FAST, DHT port), optional message-stream encryption (RC4/Plaintext), and construction of outgoing protocol messages. It derives from peer_connection and manages handshake state, message queues, and optional ut_pex integration. Includes nested enums for message ids and holepunch message/error types. Construction requires peer_connection_args; destruction handled via virtual destructor.
Holepunch submessage type identifiers used within extension messaging for NAT traversal: rendezvous, connect, and failed.
Holepunch error codes communicated in holepunch extension messages: no_error, no_such_peer, not_connected, no_support, and no_self.

objects.definition:
enum message_type
		{
			// standard messages
			msg_choke = 0,
			msg_unchoke,
			msg_interested,
			msg_not_interested,
			msg_have,
			msg_bitfield,
			msg_request,
			msg_piece,
			msg_cancel,
			// DHT extension
			msg_dht_port,
			// FAST extension
			msg_suggest_piece = 0xd,
			msg_have_all,
			msg_have_none,
			msg_reject_request,
			msg_allowed_fast,

			// extension protocol message
			msg_extended = 20,

			msg_hash_request = 21,
			msg_hashes,
			msg_hash_reject,

			num_supported_messages
		};
objects.description: Enumeration of BitTorrent protocol message IDs used by this connection, including standard, FAST, DHT port, extended, and merkle tree hash exchange messages.
Forward declaration of the aux::session_settings type within libtorrent::aux. Only an incomplete type is declared here; its members and layout are not defined in this header.
Forward declaration of the peer_connection type in the libtorrent namespace. Only an incomplete type is declared here; its members and layout are not defined in this header.

Type-safe opaque user-data holder for libtorrent. Wraps a raw void* but records a unique per-type token so that retrieval via get<T>() or explicit pointer conversion is only successful when T matches the originally assigned pointer type (including cv-qualifiers). Default-constructs to null, can be constructed or assigned from any pointer type. When TORRENT_ABI_VERSION > 2, implicit conversion/assignment to/from void* is disabled to enforce type safety. Does not own the pointed-to object; lifetime must be managed externally.

Strongly-typed enum (16-bit underlying type) enumerating all internal reasons a libtorrent peer connection may be closed, grouped with general reasons starting at 0 and protocol/peer-error reasons starting at 256. Values are used for diagnostics/telemetry and policy decisions when disconnecting peers.

No custom data types are defined in this header. It only declares two free functions (crc32c_32 and crc32c) returning std::uint32_t. std::uint32_t is a standard type alias from <cstdint>, not defined here.

Bitfield of flags controlling torrent creation behavior. It wraps a 32-bit bitfield_flag with tag create_flags_tag. Members such as modification_time, symlinks, v2_only, v1_only, canonical_files, etc. are defined as specific bits in create_torrent and are of this type.

Stateful builder for .torrent metadata. Construct with a file_storage or a torrent_info to seed the info dictionary, set properties and piece/file hashes, then call generate()/generate_buf() to obtain the bencoded metadata. Offers flags (create_flags_t) to control v1/v2 behavior, symlinks, canonical layout, etc. Requires that the referenced file_storage/torrent_info outlive the builder. Throws on generation errors such as missing hashes or empty storage.

Type alias defined in the libtorrent namespace that resolves to a high-resolution timer implementation. When TORRENT_BUILD_SIMULATOR is defined, it aliases sim::asio::high_resolution_timer (simulator environment); otherwise it aliases boost::asio::high_resolution_timer (real Boost.Asio). The alias itself is defined here; underlying types are external and not defined in this header.
Utility mixin to assert single-threaded access. In assert-enabled builds, it records the first caller thread id and checks subsequent calls originate from the same thread; otherwise it is a no-op.

Abstract interface used to free disk buffers that were allocated by the disk subsystem. Implementers must provide free_disk_buffer to return a previously allocated buffer. The destructor is protected and virtual-by-implication via vtable, preventing deletion through this interface unless derived, and ensuring lifetime is managed elsewhere.

RAII holder similar to unique_ptr for a disk buffer allocated via a buffer_allocator_interface. On destruction or reset, it returns the buffer to the allocator via free_disk_buffer. Non-copyable, movable. data() exposes the raw buffer, size() returns its size in bytes, and operator bool indicates ownership. is_mutable() is hardcoded to false, implying callers should not modify the buffer in place. Requires a valid allocator reference in the constructor along with the buffer pointer and size. If default-constructed or moved-from, holds no buffer.
direct_api_constructors: libtorrent::disk_buffer_holder::disk_buffer_holder(libtorrent::buffer_allocator_interface& alloc, char* buf, int sz) noexcept

objects.definition: using file_open_mode_t = flags::bitfield_flag<std::uint8_t, struct file_open_mode_tag>;
objects.description: A strongly-typed bitfield flag over std::uint8_t used to specify file open modes for libtorrent's disk I/O (read/write, sparse, no_atime, random_access, mmapped, etc.). Values are defined in the file_open_mode namespace. Construction and usage follow flags::bitfield_flag semantics.
Represents a single file currently open by the disk I/O subsystem for a given torrent, including its file index, open mode flags, and last-use timestamp. Returned by disk_interface::get_status().

objects.definition: using disk_job_flags_t = flags::bitfield_flag<std::uint8_t, struct disk_job_flags_tag>;
objects.description: A strongly-typed bitfield flag over std::uint8_t used to tweak behavior of read/write/hash disk jobs (e.g. force_copy, sequential_access, volatile_read, v1_hash, flush_piece). Constants are provided as static constexpr members of disk_interface.

The abstract customization point for libtorrent’s disk I/O backends. Implementations own and operate per-torrent storage, perform async-read/write, hashing, file management, prioritization, and shutdown coordination. All methods are invoked from libtorrent’s network thread; implementations may manage their own worker threads and must post completions back to the network thread.

A small RAII handle that uniquely owns a storage instance (identified by storage_index_t) within the disk_interface backend. On destruction or reset, it notifies the disk backend via disk_interface::remove_torrent(). Movable, non-copyable.

Abstract interface (struct) used to observe disk/cache backpressure changes. Implementers receive a callback via on_disk() when the disk cache drops below a low watermark and downloading can resume. The destructor is protected and non-virtual beyond the implicit one from the vtable; instances are intended to be deleted through derived classes (do not delete through disk_observer*).

Strong typedef representing a download priority value for files or pieces in libtorrent. It wraps a std::uint8_t via aux::strong_typedef to provide type safety. Constants define typical priority levels (dont_download, low_priority, default_priority, top_priority). Details of aux::strong_typedef are not present in this header.

Variant-like class representing a node in a bencoded structure. It can hold an integer, string, list, dictionary, or preformatted bytes. Provides typed accessors, map-style access for dictionaries, and pretty-printing. Construction is via specific-type constructors or by specifying a data_type. Proper type must be observed when accessing or modifying; otherwise functions may throw system_error/assert in debug builds.

objects.definition: using dictionary_type = std::map<std::string, entry, aux::strview_less>;
objects.description: Type alias for the dictionary/map representation of a bencoded dictionary, mapping string keys to entry values with a custom comparator for string_view ordering.

objects.definition: using string_type = std::string;
objects.description: Alias for the string type used by entry to represent bencoded strings.

objects.definition: using list_type = std::vector<entry>;
objects.description: Alias for the list type used by entry to represent bencoded lists (arrays of entry).

objects.definition: using integer_type = std::int64_t;
objects.description: Alias for the integer type used by entry to represent bencoded integers.

objects.definition: using preformatted_type = std::vector<char>;
objects.description: Alias for a byte buffer used to store already-bencoded data blobs for efficient re-emission without parsing.
Enumeration of the concrete type currently held by an entry instance. Used to construct or query the active variant alternative.

Enumeration of all libtorrent-specific error codes used with boost::system::error_code under the libtorrent_category. Values cover torrent parsing, peer protocol, networking, HTTP, resume data, and v2 torrent-specific errors. Used to create error_code via make_error_code.

enum http_errors
	{
		cont = 100,
		ok = 200,
		created = 201,
		accepted = 202,
		no_content = 204,
		multiple_choices = 300,
		moved_permanently = 301,
		moved_temporarily = 302,

	};
objects.description: Enumeration of a subset of HTTP status codes used as error codes within libtorrent's http_category for reporting HTTP-related errors.

Represents an error from storage (disk I/O) along with context of which file index and what operation failed. Holds a boost::system::error_code (aliased as libtorrent::error_code), a 24-bit file index, and an operation_t identifying the file operation.

objects.definition: using feature_flags_t = flags::bitfield_flag<std::uint8_t, struct feature_flags_tag>;
objects.description: Bitfield of feature flags indicating which plugin callbacks are implemented/desired by a session plugin. Backed by an 8-bit flag field.
Base class for a session-wide plugin. Receives session-level events and can spawn torrent-specific plugins. Exposes feature flags to declare interested callbacks.

objects.definition: using add_peer_flags_t = flags::bitfield_flag<std::uint8_t, struct add_peer_flags_tag>;
objects.description: Bitfield flags used when reporting newly discovered peers to torrent plugins. Indicates metadata like first-time and IP-filtered.
Per-torrent plugin interface. Can attach peer plugins to new connections and intercept/override torrent-level events such as pause/resume, state changes, and peer discovery.
Per-peer plugin interface. Receives and can intercept BT protocol events/messages for an individual peer connection, including handshakes, bitfield, piece transfer, and outgoing message hooks.

Abstract interface for stream crypto adapters used by encrypted peer connections. Provides key setup and buffer-oriented encrypt/decrypt operations with explicit ownership and lifetime rules for extra head data.

Platform-dependent alias for an OS file handle: HANDLE on Windows, int (file descriptor) on POSIX. The associated invalid value is INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE on Windows and -1 on POSIX. This is a type alias, not an owning wrapper.

RAII wrapper around a platform file handle. Opens a file in the constructor taking path, size, and open mode; prohibits copy, supports move; closes the handle in destructor. Provides size query and access to the raw OS handle via fd(). On Windows stores open mode for use in close/dup semantics.

Type alias in the libtorrent namespace mapping file_layout to file_storage. It introduces no new storage or behavior; it is a pure alias meant to present the file_storage API under the name file_layout. Details of file_storage are not defined in this header.
Deprecated ABI v1 struct describing a file within a torrent: path, size, offset, times, hash and attribute flags. Only available when TORRENT_ABI_VERSION == 1.
Internal compact representation of a file’s metadata used by file_storage: sizes, offsets, attributes, name handling, symlink/root info, and path indexing.
Represents a window (offset, size) into a specific file within a torrent.
Owns and manages the list of files in a torrent, piece layout, attributes, and related queries/mappings. Provides APIs to add files, map between pieces and file ranges, and query per-file metadata.

objects.definition: using file_flags_t = flags::bitfield_flag<std::uint8_t, struct file_flags_tag>;
objects.description: Strongly-typed bitfield flag type used for per-file attribute flags (pad, hidden, executable, symlink).
Strong typedef wrapping a 32-bit index used to reference entries in file_storage path tables. Values include sentinels like no_path and path_is_absolute in aux::file_entry.

Represents a client fingerprint (client ID and version components) used to encode and generate a BitTorrent peer_id string for libtorrent-based clients. Stores a two-character client code and four integer version fields. Constructor initializes fields; to_string is available only when TORRENT_ABI_VERSION == 1. No ownership or special destruction semantics beyond POD-like struct; details about range checking are not provided here.

Small strong type that wraps a bit index. It converts explicitly to int and is intended to be used to create single-bit flags (e.g. for constructing bitfield_flag with a specific bit set). There is also a user-defined literal "_bit" to construct it from an integer literal. No dynamic resources; trivially copyable.

Enumeration of gzip-specific error codes used by libtorrent. These correspond to conditions encountered during gzip decompression and are associated with libtorrent's gzip_category error category.

Template specialization marking libtorrent::gzip_errors::error_code_enum as a valid error_condition enum for Boost.System. This trait enables implicit conversions to error_condition.
Result holder returned when setting/adding a single block hash. Encodes status (verified/unknown/failure), and the first verified block index and count to help map to piece ranges.
Aggregated result from adding a batch of hashes for one or more pieces. Indicates overall validity and which pieces/blocks failed or passed verification.
Lightweight identifier for a node within a file’s Merkle tree, pairing a file index with a node index.
Describes a request for a contiguous range of Merkle hashes for a specific file, including tree level (base), start index, count, and number of proof layers required.

Coordinator for selecting, requesting, and verifying Merkle hashes for pieces and files in a torrent. Maintains per-file Merkle trees, tracks pending piece/block hash requests, and exposes methods to add hashes, set block hashes, and query verification state.

HTTP client connection object that performs async resolve, connect, read/write, and invokes user-provided handlers. Supports proxies, SSL, I2P, bandwidth limiting, and optional "bottled" buffering of the entire response before callback.
Value type describing an outbound bind preference: network device name and IP address to bind the socket to. Equality compares both fields.

objects.description: Forward declaration of a visitor/helper used by http_connection for closing sockets. Definition not present in this header.

using http_handler = std::function<void(error_code const&
	, http_parser const&, span<char const> data, http_connection&)>;
objects.description: Callback type invoked on HTTP events or received data. Parameters: error code, parsed HTTP headers, data chunk (or empty when bottled), and the http_connection.

objects.definition: using http_connect_handler = std::function<void(http_connection&)>;
objects.description: Callback type invoked when the TCP/SSL connection is established, before request/response processing.

objects.description: Callback type to filter or reorder candidate endpoints before connecting.

objects.definition: using hostname_filter_handler = std::function<bool(http_connection&, string_view)>;
objects.description: Callback type to filter/validate a hostname before resolving; returns true to allow, false to block.

HTTP message parser for requests/responses. Parses status line, headers, and body, with support for chunked transfer-encoding and content-range. Provides accessors for method, path, protocol, status code, headers, body, and chunk metadata. Construction accepts flags_t to tweak behavior (e.g., dont_parse_chunks). Lifetime managed by caller; no explicit destroy function is required beyond destructor. Some behavior depends on received buffers fed via incoming().

objects.definition: enum flags_t { dont_parse_chunks = 1 };
objects.description: Bitflag enum controlling parser behavior. Currently defines dont_parse_chunks=1 to disable parsing of chunked encoding details.

HTTP web-seed peer connection implementation used by libtorrent to download pieces over HTTP(S). It derives from web_connection_base and manages HTTP requests/responses, chunked transfer parsing, and progress tracking for a specific web seed URL. Construction requires peer_connection_args and a web_seed_t reference. Destruction and other lifecycle details are managed by the owning torrent/connection machinery in libtorrent; details not present here.

objects.definition: struct torrent;
objects.description: Forward declaration only. Represents a torrent object in libtorrent. No definition in this header.

objects.definition: struct peer_request;
objects.description: Forward declaration only. Represents a request for a block/piece from a peer. No definition in this header.

An HTTP CONNECT-capable stream wrapper in namespace libtorrent that derives from proxy_base. It resolves and connects to an HTTP proxy and performs the CONNECT handshake to reach a target endpoint. It supports optional basic authentication (username/password), an optional Host header override, and a mode (no_connect) to skip issuing CONNECT and talk to the proxy directly. Construction requires an io_context and it uses asynchronous operations via Boost.Asio-style handlers. Destruction/closure is delegated to proxy_base::close(). Details of proxy_base, socket types, and resolver are defined elsewhere.

Concrete tracker_connection implementation that communicates with HTTP/HTTPS trackers. Manages an underlying http_connection, performs connect/response handling, filters endpoints/hostnames, and parses tracker responses. Lifecycle is controlled by tracker_manager; constructed with IO context, tracker_manager, a tracker_request, and a request_callback weak_ptr.

Enumeration of error codes used with the I2P error category for SAM bridge interactions. Values map to responses like RESULT=OK, CANT_REACH_PEER, etc. Intended for forming/inspecting boost::system::error_code instances with i2p_category().
Holds tunable I2P SAM session options (tunnel quantities, lengths, and variances) used when creating an I2P STREAM session.

Asynchronous SAM (I2P) stream helper derived from proxy_base. Manages the SAM handshake and commands (HELLO, SESSION CREATE, STREAM CONNECT/ACCEPT, NAMING LOOKUP) over a TCP socket, parsing responses and surfacing completion via handlers. Holds buffer, destination, local endpoint, session options, and internal command/state enums.
Command selector for i2p_stream to decide which SAM action to send after HELLO, including session creation, connect, accept, name lookup, or handling incoming notification.

High-level manager for a SAM session to an I2P router. Owns an i2p_stream, opens the session (SESSION CREATE), tracks session ID and local endpoint, and provides queued async name lookup support. Maintains its own state machine distinct from i2p_stream.
Standard library string type referenced by declarations. Not defined in this header. Ignored per instructions.
Type referenced but not defined in this header (declared in libtorrent/peer_id.hpp). Per instructions, it should be ignored.
Type referenced but not defined in this header (declared in libtorrent/fingerprint.hpp). Per instructions, it should be ignored.
Template instantiation referenced but not defined here. Should be ignored per instructions.

Alias introduced in namespace libtorrent for io_context. When TORRENT_BUILD_SIMULATOR is defined, it aliases sim::asio::io_context; otherwise it aliases boost::asio::io_context. It is not a new type definition with storage; it’s a using-alias to an external type.

Public IP address filter managing IPv4 and IPv6 rules. Provides adding rules, querying access flags, and exporting consolidated IPv4/IPv6 ranges. Uses two aux::filter_impl instances internally. access_flags::blocked marks disallowed ranges. Default-constructed instance allows all addresses.

Public port-range filter mapping 16-bit port ranges to flags. Provides adding rules, querying access flags, and uses aux::filter_impl<uint16_t> internally. access_flags::blocked marks disallowed destination ports. Default-constructed instance allows all ports.

Tracks votes from peers/sources to determine the most likely external IP address of the current node. Maintains per-address vote counts, source bitmask, and bloom filters to avoid duplicate/abusive voting, and can rotate/reset its state when necessary. Construction/destruction are default; usage centers around cast_vote() and querying external_address(). Internal nested struct external_ip_t encapsulates per-address vote state.

Stores one local and one global address per IP family (IPv4/IPv6) and can return the external address as observed from a given IP. Provides default and four-address constructor plus a query method. Internals are an address[2][2] matrix indexed by locality and family.

objects.definition: using torrent_list_index_t = aux::strong_typedef<int, struct torrent_list_tag>;
objects.description: Strong typedef wrapping an int to represent an index into a torrent-related list. Provides type safety distinct from raw int. The underlying value is an index; valid values are implementation-defined. No constructors or methods are shown here beyond what strong_typedef provides in its own definition (not part of this header).

Intrusive list-link helper storing the position of an owning object within an external aux::vector<T*>. index is -1 when not in a list; otherwise it is the element's position. insert() appends the owning object to a vector and records its index. unlink() removes the owning object by swapping with the last element and shrinking the vector, updating the moved element's link index. Requires that T has a member m_links indexed by torrent_list_index_t that exposes .index. Thread-safety and lifetime management are not provided here.

Local Service Discovery (LSD) manager for libtorrent. Provides UDP-based multicast/broadcast announcements of torrents on the local network and listens for peers. Holds network resources (UDP socket, timer) and a callback interface to report discovered peers/events. Construction requires an io_context, an lsd_callback, and local addressing info. Supports start(), announce() of info-hashes with a listen port, and close() to tear down. Internals include retry/broadcast logic, unique cookie to ignore self-announcements, and optional logging. Destruction likely stops timers and closes the socket. Further behavioral details depend on libtorrent’s aux::lsd implementation.
direct_api_constructors: libtorrent::lsd::lsd(io_context& ios, aux::lsd_callback& cb, address listen_address, address netmask)

objects.definition: struct torrent_handle;

objects.definition: struct session;
objects.description: Forward declaration of the session type from libtorrent. Only referenced in deprecated add_magnet_uri overloads; not defined in this header.

objects.definition: struct counters;

objects.definition: struct settings_interface;
objects.description: Forward declaration of libtorrent::settings_interface. Incomplete type; definition is not provided in this header. Represents an interface to query configuration settings used by disk I/O construction.

Concrete storage backend that uses memory-mapped files to read, write, hash, and manage torrent data on disk. It shares file mappings via aux::file_view_pool, supports part files for skipped files, renaming, moving, and initialization. It derives from aux::disk_job_fence to coordinate concurrent disk jobs and uses enable_shared_from_this for shared ownership. Destruction and resource lifetimes are tied to torrent/file_storage objects; copy is disabled. Some operational details (e.g., exact semantics of flags) are defined elsewhere in libtorrent; this header declares the interface and members.

Enum of PCP (Port Control Protocol) error codes per RFC 6887 section 7.4, used to classify PCP result statuses into a boost::system error_code. Intended for mapping network/NAT traversal errors when using PCP.

NAT-PMP/PCP port mapping manager. Manages UDP communication with the router to create, refresh, and delete NAT-PMP or PCP mappings for a listening socket. Provides start, add_mapping, delete_mapping, get_mapping, and close APIs and handles retries, timers, and parsing replies. Final, shared_from_this-enabled, single-threaded component.
direct_api_constructors: libtorrent::natpmp::natpmp(io_context& ios, aux::portmap_callback& cb, aux::listen_socket_handle ls)

objects.description: Template specialization marking libtorrent::errors::pcp_errors as a Boost.System error_code enum. Enables implicit conversion to error_code. Not an instantiable runtime type but a compile-time trait.

Protocol type for Boost.Asio representing a Linux netlink socket. Provides family(), type(), and protocol() for Asio integration. Default constructs to NETLINK_ROUTE; can be constructed with another netlink family. Defines associated endpoint and socket types.

Strongly-typed enumeration of operation identifiers used by libtorrent to tag the source of an error or disconnect (e.g., file I/O, socket operations, DNS, timers). Stored as uint8_t for compactness and used in alerts like peer_error_alert and peer_disconnected_alert. Values cover a wide range of network and filesystem operations.

Legacy, non-scoped enum used in ABI version 1 builds to represent a subset of operation identifiers. Marked deprecated via TORRENT_DEPRECATED_ENUM; superseded by operation_t. Only available when TORRENT_ABI_VERSION == 1.
Return type of parse_url_components: a 5-tuple consisting of protocol, auth, hostname, port, and path. Standard library type; included here only as the function’s return, not defined in this header.
Return type of split_url: a 2-tuple consisting of base and path components of a URL. Standard library type; included here only as the function’s return, not defined in this header.

objects.definition: using slot_index_t = aux::strong_typedef<int, struct slot_index_tag_t>;
objects.description: Strong typedef over int used to represent an index of an allocated slot inside the part file. Provides type safety compared to raw int when indexing slots.

Manages a sparse on-disk part file storing selected torrent pieces. Provides read/write of piece ranges, hashing, exporting ranges, moving the backing file, and flushing metadata. Thread-safe internal bookkeeping via mutex. Slots map pieces to storage offsets within the part file.

objects.definition: using key_t = mp::number<mp::cpp_int_backend<768, 768, mp::unsigned_magnitude, mp::unchecked, void>>;
objects.description: Alias for a 768-bit unsigned big-integer type (Boost.Multiprecision cpp_int_backend) used as Diffie-Hellman keys and secrets.

Represents a peer with an optional DNS hostname, BitTorrent peer_id, and TCP port. Comparison operators compare only the peer_id (equality) and order by peer_id, not by hostname/port. Construction is aggregate; no special constructors are provided. Be aware that the header references external types peer_id and std::string; semantics for peer_id are defined elsewhere.
Compact IPv4 peer representation storing the raw IPv4 address bytes (network order as provided by address_v4::bytes_type) and a TCP port. Aggregate type with no methods.
Compact IPv6 peer representation storing the raw IPv6 address bytes and a TCP port. Aggregate type with no methods.

I2P peer representation identified by an I2P destination hash. This type is conditionally defined only when TORRENT_USE_I2P is enabled. If the macro is not defined, this struct is not available in this header.

objects.definition: using peer_class_t = aux::strong_typedef<std::uint32_t, struct peer_class_tag>;
objects.description: Strong typedef around std::uint32_t used as an opaque handle/identifier for a peer_class entry in peer_class_pool. Values are not arithmetic IDs for public use; treat them as opaque tokens usable with peer_class_pool APIs.

Plain settings container describing limits and priorities for a peer class (e.g. bandwidth limits, priorities, connection limit factor, label). Intended to be passed into/returned from peer_class::set_info/get_info.

Runtime peer class object storing bandwidth channels, priorities, connection-limit factor, and flags. Provides APIs to set/query its configuration via peer_class_info and to set bandwidth limits. Lifetime and reference counting managed by peer_class_pool.

Owner/manager of peer_class instances. Allocates new classes, returns opaque peer_class_t handles, and manages reference counts. Provides accessors to retrieve peer_class by handle. Internally stores classes in an indexed deque and tracks free slots.

Concrete struct that tracks up to 15 peer classes assigned to an object (e.g., peer connections or torrents). Provides APIs to add, check, remove, count, and index peer classes. Internally stores the current size and a fixed-size array of peer_class_t identifiers. Construction initializes with zero classes. Details about peer_class_pool and peer_class_t are referenced but defined elsewhere.

A container of rules mapping socket types to peer class bitmasks. It filters (via masks) and augments (via add-bits) the peer classes assigned to new peers after the IP-based peer class filter. Provides add/remove to set bits to add, allow/disallow to mask bits off, and apply() to transform a peer class bitmask for a given socket type. Default-constructs with all classes allowed and none added. Note: peer_class_t must be <= 31 because internal masks are 32-bit. Requires libtorrent::peer_class_t from peer_class.hpp.

Enumeration of socket types used to index filter rules within peer_class_type_filter. Values correspond to libtorrent socket types; num_socket_types is a sentinel/count. Underlying type is std::uint8_t.

objects.definition:
struct min_value_t {};
static const min_value_t min_value{};
objects.description: Tag type used to construct special minimum-valued relative_time instances. The static constant min_value is a sentinel to pass to constructors.

A compact, reference-relative time holder storing an offset in milliseconds32 from an arbitrary reference time_point. Offers set() and get() to encode/decode absolute time relative to a reference. Used widely for timestamping events without storing full time_points.
Represents a piece_block requested from a peer and its send-buffer state. Tracks offset into send buffer, and flags for not_wanted, timed_out, and busy. Used in request/download queues.

Aggregate of constructor arguments required to create a peer_connection. Holds pointers/references to session, settings, disk thread, IO context, torrent reference, socket, endpoints, and initial peer info and our peer_id.

Base class containing fields that are frequently accessed (“hot”) for peer connections: piece availability bitfield, torrent reference, session/settings references, and a set of state flags. Designed to improve cache locality.
Enumeration of concrete peer connection protocol types. bittorrent for regular BT peers; url_seed and http_seed for web seeds.

Abstract base class modeling a peer transport in libtorrent. Manages socket I/O, bandwidth accounting, request/response queues, state machines for choking/interest, piece availability, and interaction with torrent/session. Derived classes implement protocol-specific behavior (e.g. BitTorrent wire, HTTP seeds). Construction uses peer_connection_args; lifecycle managed via shared_ptr and enable_shared_from_this. Many virtual hooks (write_*, on_receive/on_sent, on_connected, in_handshake, etc.).

RAII helper that temporarily marks the upload channel as having an outstanding network send to defer actual async sends (corking). Upon destruction, it clears the flag and calls setup_send(), issuing pending data. Prevents multiple small send calls.

objects.definition: using request_flags_t = flags::bitfield_flag<std::uint8_t, struct request_flags_tag>;
objects.description: Strongly-typed bitfield flag type for request options on piece requests (e.g., time_critical, busy). Underlying type is std::uint8_t.

Opaque handle class for accessing an internal libtorrent peer_connection via a weak_ptr. Exposes low-level operations and queries on a peer (state, interest/choke, metadata, logging, disconnect). Intended for plugin authors; API stability is not guaranteed. The object itself is lightweight and refers to an internal peer_connection; lifetime is managed elsewhere. Construction requires a std::weak_ptr<peer_connection>.

Derived handle specialized for BitTorrent peer connections. Provides BT-specific queries (packet completion, extension/encryption support) and the ability to swap crypto plugins for send/receive paths. Wraps the same underlying peer_connection and exposes a native_handle to bt_peer_connection.

objects.definition: using disconnect_severity_t = aux::strong_typedef<std::uint8_t, struct disconnect_severity_tag>;
objects.description: Strong typedef over std::uint8_t representing disconnect severity levels for peer connections. Values used in this header are the static constexpr instances defined in peer_connection_interface: normal{0}, failure{1}, peer_error{2}. The underlying type is an aux::strong_typedef, providing type safety over raw integers.

Abstract interface for a peer connection in libtorrent. It defines the operations and queries available on a peer connection, including endpoints, disconnect handling with severity, peer identity, statistics, and logging hooks. This type is an interface (pure virtual) with a protected virtual destructor, so it is intended to be implemented and managed via pointers or references; clients should not delete via this interface unless the destructor is accessible within the implementation. Construction is via implementing classes elsewhere; no constructors are provided here.

Alias type for libtorrent::sha1_hash representing a BitTorrent peer identifier. It is exactly the same type as sha1_hash; this header only introduces the name peer_id for semantic clarity. Details of sha1_hash (layout, size, methods) are defined elsewhere and are not present in this header.

objects.definition: using peer_flags_t = flags::bitfield_flag<std::uint32_t, struct peer_flags_tag>;
objects.description: Bitfield type representing peer state flags for libtorrent peers. Backed by a 32-bit storage type with tag peer_flags_tag. Used for peer_info::flags and its static constexpr flag constants.

objects.definition: using peer_source_flags_t = flags::bitfield_flag<std::uint8_t, struct peer_source_flags_tag>;
objects.description: Bitfield type indicating the source(s) from which a peer was learned (tracker, DHT, PEX, LSD, resume data, incoming). Backed by an 8-bit storage type with tag peer_source_flags_tag.

objects.definition: using bandwidth_state_flags_t = flags::bitfield_flag<std::uint8_t, struct bandwidth_state_flags_tag>;
objects.description: Bitfield type describing what is blocking network transfers (idle, limiter, network I/O, disk). Backed by an 8-bit storage type with tag bandwidth_state_flags_tag.

objects.definition: using connection_type_t = flags::bitfield_flag<std::uint8_t, struct connection_type_tag>;
objects.description: Bitfield type encoding the connection kind for a peer (standard BitTorrent, web seed, HTTP seed). Backed by an 8-bit storage type with tag connection_type_tag.

Holds statistics and state for a single connected peer in libtorrent. Provides numerous fields for speeds, buffers, requests, piece availability, connection type, flag bitfields for state/source/bandwidth, endpoints, and progress. Constructors/assignment are declared but defined elsewhere. Some members and aliases are ABI-version-conditional. Used as a snapshot-style info object; it is not responsible for network I/O or lifetime of underlying sockets.

Internal ABI-1-only structure representing a peer list entry with address, flags, failure count, and source bits. Contains a small enum flags_t with a banned flag. Intended for internal use; construction and semantics are minimal in this header.

Forward declaration of an allocator interface for torrent_peer objects. Only declared here; actual definition is elsewhere. Purpose is to abstract allocation and deallocation of torrent_peer instances used by peer_list.

Carries snapshot configuration and transient state shared between the torrent and peer_list. Provides limits, external IP/port for ranking, counters, and a return vector of erased peers. Used across peer_list operations; fields are set and read by peer_list methods. No special construction logic beyond aggregate initialization; destruction is trivial.
Empty tag type used to parameterize the bitfield flag type erase_peer_flags_t. Only forward-declared here; no members. It serves as a unique type token for flags::bitfield_flag.

Type alias for a small bitfield-backed flag set used by peer_list to control erasure behavior. It wraps a std::uint8_t storage with tag erase_peer_flags_tag. Notably, peer_list defines a constexpr flag value force_erase = 1_bit for immediate erasure.

Manages the set of known peers for a torrent. Responsible for adding/removing peers, tracking seeds, candidate selection and ranking, applying filters, and coordinating with peer_connection_interface. It is single-threaded (inherits single_threaded). Requires a torrent_peer_allocator_interface reference on construction; non-copyable. Provides iterators over managed torrent_peer* and stats like seeds and connect candidates. Methods modify fields in torrent_state and may erase peers, returning them via torrent_state::erased. Destruction must free peers using the provided allocator (implementation-defined elsewhere).

A POD-like struct representing a requested byte range within a torrent piece, used primarily for incoming piece requests. Fields: piece (piece index), start (byte offset within the piece), length (byte count). Equality operator compares all three fields. Construction is aggregate; no special constructors or destructors are defined. Requires piece_index_t from libtorrent/units.hpp.

objects.description: Thread-safe statistics accumulator for libtorrent sessions. Provides two dense index spaces: stats_counter_t (event counters) and stats_gauge_t (instantaneous gauges). Offers atomic increment, set, blend and read access over an internal array of num_counters elements. Storage is either lock-free atomics or a single mutex protecting a plain array depending on ATOMIC_LLONG_LOCK_FREE. Construction/destruction have no special requirements beyond default operations.

Type-safe bitfield flag type used to represent peer-exchange (PEX) feature flags within libtorrent. It is an alias of flags::bitfield_flag parametrized with std::uint8_t storage and the tag type pex_flags_tag to provide strong typing across flag domains. Constants pex_encryption, pex_seed, pex_utp, pex_holepunch, and pex_lt_v2 are individual flag values of this type.

objects.definition: struct pex_flags_tag;
objects.description: Tag type used solely to distinguish pex_flags_t from other bitfield_flag instantiations. It is an incomplete forward declaration in this header; no members are defined here.

A lightweight value-type identifying a specific block within a torrent piece. It contains a piece index (piece_index_t) and a block index (int). Provides comparison operators for ordering and equality, and exposes a static sentinel value 'invalid' (declared here, defined elsewhere). Construction can be default (both indices zero) or via explicit piece/block indices. Lifetime is trivial; no ownership semantics. Note: piece_index_t is declared in libtorrent/units.hpp and not defined here.

Represents progress information for a specific piece/block currently being downloaded in libtorrent. Holds the piece index, the block index within that piece, how many bytes of the block have been received, and the total bytes in the block. The piece_index defaults to invalid_index (-1) to denote an invalid/unset state.
Plain aggregate carrying counts for pieces and pad bytes, plus whether the last piece is included, used by piece_picker query methods (want/have/etc.).

Piece selection and state-tracking core for libtorrent. Manages availability, priorities, per-block state, and download queues with support for various picking strategies and extent affinity. Inner types define block metadata, partial piece state, piece-position metadata, stats, and helpers.
Metadata for a single block within a piece: which peer it’s associated with, number of peers queueing it, and its state (none/requested/writing/finished). Debug-only fields track invariants.
Tracks per-piece download progress and counts of blocks in each state, plus an index into the shared block_info storage. hashing indicates outstanding hash job(s).
Lightweight snapshot of a piece's availability, effective priority, and local state (have/downloading). Returned by piece_stats().
Predicate functor to find a downloading_piece with a specific piece index.

A helper struct for mutable torrents that discovers identical files across torrents and records links to them. It owns a target torrent_info to resolve and builds per-file links to matching files in other torrents. Construction requires a torrent_info to resolve. Use match() with another torrent_info and its save path to discover shared files, then read results via get_links(). Details of matching differ for v1/v2 torrents via private helpers. Note: definition is conditionally compiled out if TORRENT_DISABLE_MUTABLE_TORRENTS is defined.

Inner struct describing a discovered link between a file in the target torrent and a file in another torrent: ti points to the other torrent, save_path is its storage root, and file_idx identifies the matching file within that torrent.

Handle object that outlives a session to coordinate and synchronize asynchronous shutdown. Constructed internally by session::abort(). Copyable and movable. Holds shared pointers to the session’s io_context, worker thread, and implementation. No public operations beyond lifetime management.

Top-level session object managing libtorrent state across torrents. Runs network loop and owns the worker thread and implementation. Constructed with session_params (preferred) and optionally an external io_context and flags. Non-copyable, movable. abort() yields a session_proxy to perform asynchronous shutdown.

Non-owning handle to a libtorrent session. Wraps and forwards a subset of session APIs. It can expire if the underlying session is destroyed; check is_valid() before use. Provides methods to manage torrents, DHT, peer classes, alerts, settings, port mappings, and persistence of session state. Many members are conditional on ABI version and some are deprecated. Construction is internal; users receive a handle from session and copy/move it. No explicit destruction semantics beyond standard object lifetime; it holds a weak_ptr to aux::session_impl.

Configuration aggregate used to initialize a libtorrent session. Holds initial settings_pack, extension plugins, DHT bootstrap/state and storage factory, disk I/O backend factory, arbitrary extension state map, and an ip_filter. objects.description: A concrete settings container used to batch and apply configuration options to a libtorrent session. It implements settings_interface and defines all setting keys via nested enums (string_types, bool_types, int_types) along with several configuration enums for I/O and algorithms. Stores only explicitly set values; provides getters that fall back to defaults. Copyable and movable. Construct via default constructor and fill using set_* functions, then pass to session::apply_settings().
Abstract interface for setting storage back-ends. Defines virtual methods to set/query string, integer, and boolean settings by numeric key. settings_pack implements this interface.
Forward declaration of bdecode_node, a parse tree node for bencoded data. Only referenced here; no definition provided in this header.
Forward declarations of internal session types used by apply functions. No definitions are present in this header.
Forward-declared internal settings structure for a session. Definition is elsewhere.
Forward-declared internal single-thread settings representation. Definition not included here.

SHA-1 hashing context struct for libtorrent’s built-in SHA-1 implementation (used when no external crypto backends are enabled). Holds internal state, bit count, and input buffer. Use with SHA1_init, SHA1_update, and SHA1_final to compute SHA-1 digests. Details of lifecycle: create a sha1_ctx object (stack or heap), initialize with SHA1_init, feed data via SHA1_update, and finalize with SHA1_final to produce a 20-byte digest. After final, the context may be re-initialized for a new hash.

objects.definition: using sha1_hash = digest32<160>;
objects.description: Alias for a 160-bit digest, commonly used for SHA-1 hashes such as info-hashes, piece-hashes, peer IDs, and node IDs in libtorrent.

objects.definition: using sha256_hash = digest32<256>;
objects.description: Alias for a 256-bit digest, commonly used for SHA-256 hashes in libtorrent.

SHA-256 hashing context used by libtorrent's built-in SHA-256 implementation (adapted from LibTomCrypt). Holds the running bit count (length), the internal hash state of eight 32-bit words, the current buffer length (curlen), and a 64-byte message block buffer.

Wrapper type adapting boost::asio::ip::tcp (or sim::asio::ip::tcp when building the simulator) to libtorrent, primarily to expose a noexcept-move-only socket typedef. It behaves like the base protocol type and is used for TCP endpoints and sockets.
Wrapper type adapting boost::asio::ip::udp (or sim::asio::ip::udp in simulator builds) with a noexcept-move-only socket alias. Used for UDP endpoints and sockets.
IPv6 traffic class (TCLASS) socket option wrapper. Construct with DSCP/traffic class value and apply via asio.
IPv4 Type of Service (TOS)/DSCP socket option wrapper. Platform type differs (DWORD on Windows, int elsewhere). Use to set IP_TOS via asio.

Socket option wrapper to control the IPv4 Don't Fragment (DF) behavior. Uses IP_DONTFRAG/IP_DONTFRAGMENT when available. An alternative definition using IP_MTU_DISCOVER may be compiled instead on some platforms.
Linux netlink socket option wrapper to disable ENOBUFS notifications (NETLINK_NO_ENOBUFS). Only available when TORRENT_USE_NETLINK is enabled.
Socket option wrapper for TCP_NOTSENT_LOWAT to control when unsent data triggers sending (where supported, e.g., some Linux kernels).

Strongly-typed enum identifying the kind of socket used by libtorrent (e.g., tcp, socks5, http, utp, i2p, and their SSL variants). Backwards-compatibility alias 'udp' may map to 'utp' when TORRENT_ABI_VERSION <= 2. Underlying type is std::uint8_t.

Enumeration of SOCKS-related error codes used with the libtorrent-specific socks_category(). Values map to specific protocol failures and are used to construct boost::system::error_code instances in this header’s implementation.

Asynchronous SOCKS4/5 proxy stream that derives from proxy_base. Manages authentication, handshakes, and connect/UDP associate commands over a TCP socket to a configured proxy. Users configure version, command, credentials, and destination host, then call async_connect(endpoint, handler).

Template specialization marking libtorrent::socks_error::socks_error_code as a valid error_code enum for Boost.System. This is a trait, not a runtime type to construct. Note: This is defined here but typically used by Boost.System internals.

Lightweight handle to an allocation within stack_allocator’s internal storage. Encapsulates an index and validity checks; construction from index is restricted to stack_allocator via friendship. Used as a stable reference to retrieve pointers back to stored data.

A bump/stack-style allocator managing a contiguous char buffer for short-lived strings/buffers. Provides APIs to copy/format strings and buffers, returning allocation_slot handles. Tracks a generation counter to invalidate cached slots across resets. Non-copyable but movable.

Small helper caching an allocation_slot across stack_allocator generations. On request, it lazily (re)creates the string via a provided functor if the allocator generation changed or the slot is invalid. Provides a clear() method to drop the cached handle.

A per-channel traffic counter and rate estimator used by libtorrent. It accumulates counts, maintains a sliding average rate (5-second low-pass), and tracks the total. second_tick(int) must be called periodically (once per second) to update the rate. Provides methods to add counts, offset totals, clear, and combine with another channel.

Aggregates multiple stat_channel instances for upload and download accounting in libtorrent. Tracks payload, protocol, and IP overhead for both directions. Provides per-category totals and rates, combined rates, and utilities to account for SYN/SYN-ACK handshakes and per-packet overhead. Requires periodic second_tick(int) to update rates. The anonymous enum defines channel indexes.

Thread-safe cache of file stat results used by libtorrent to quickly retrieve file sizes or errors for files addressed by file_index_t within a file_storage. Provides APIs to reserve cache size, query file sizes (populating error_code on failure), mark entries dirty, clear the cache, and set cached values or errors. Internally tracks errors separately and encodes cache state via negative file_size values. Construction/destruction are default; users do not manage resources beyond object lifetime. Unknown specifics about get_filesize I/O behavior beyond reading filesystem metadata.

objects.definition: using storage_index_t = aux::strong_typedef<std::uint32_t, struct storage_index_tag_t>;
objects.description: Strong typedef over std::uint32_t identifying a storage instance (e.g., per-torrent storage) within libtorrent. Provides type-safety compared to using a raw integer.
Enumeration selecting storage allocation mode for a torrent’s files. storage_mode_allocate pre-allocates files fully; storage_mode_sparse uses sparse files and writes pieces in place.

Strongly-typed 8-bit status code (bitmask-capable) returned by disk operations such as check_fastresume and move_storage. Includes error/status values and a mask/flag bits; bitwise operators are provided.
Bit-style flags controlling async_move_storage behavior, selecting replacement policy and special reset behaviors.
Deprecated, legacy non-scoped enum corresponding to the move flags. Only defined when TORRENT_ABI_VERSION == 1. Prefer move_flags_t.

Parameter bundle passed to disk/storage constructors. Holds references to file layout, optional mapped file layout, save path, storage mode, per-file priorities, and the torrent info-hash. The struct stores references; lifetimes of referenced objects (files, path string, priorities vector) must outlive storage_params usage.

Represents a listen interface specification parsed from configuration strings. Fields: device (interface name or IP string), port (TCP/UDP port), ssl (whether the interface is for SSL/TLS), and local (marks a local-only binding). Equality compares all fields. No constructors beyond the implicit default; values are populated by parse_listen_interfaces.

Alias type within namespace libtorrent that names a string view type provided by Boost. Depending on Boost version, it aliases boost::string_ref (pre-1.61) or boost::string_view (>=1.61). Serves as a lightweight non-owning view of a contiguous char sequence. Construction is typically from const char* plus length or from std::string. Destruction is trivial; it does not own memory. Note: This header does not define the underlying type; it only provides the alias for compatibility. Methods and semantics come from the Boost type selected by the version check.

Alias type within namespace libtorrent that names a wide-character string view provided by Boost. Depending on Boost version, it aliases boost::wstring_ref (pre-1.61) or boost::wstring_view (>=1.61). Non-owning view of a contiguous wchar_t sequence. Lifetime of referenced data must outlive the view. Underlying methods come from the Boost type.
Internal enumeration of reasons why downloaded bytes were wasted, e.g. due to timeouts, cancels, end-game duplicates, etc.
Describes a piece marked time-critical for streaming. Tracks deadlines and request counts and sorts by deadline.
Internal representation of a web seed (HTTP/URL seed). Extends web_seed_entry with runtime state such as endpoints, retry timing, redirect map, and partial transfer buffers.
Base subobject holding frequently-accessed torrent members for cache locality. Owns picker, hash picker, torrent_info, session ref, connection list, and key torrent state flags.

Core internal class representing a torrent in a libtorrent session. Manages peers, piece picking, web seeds, trackers, state transitions, I/O, and statistics. Inherits utility bases for callbacks and peer class management. Not a public-stable API.

objects.definition: using torrent_flags_t = flags::bitfield_flag<std::uint64_t, struct torrent_flags_tag>;
objects.description: Type-safe bitfield flag wrapper over a 64-bit integer for torrent-wide flags. It is used to hold combinations of individual torrent_flags constants defined in this header.

Holds per-block download/write state within a piece, including which peer it came from, progress, size, state machine and number of peers requesting it. Also stores the source endpoint (IPv4/IPv6 + port).
Summarizes the state of a partially requested or written piece: counts of blocks by state and a pointer to per-block info for the piece. Used by torrent_handle to report the download queue.

Primary user-facing handle to control and query a torrent within a libtorrent session. Provides synchronous and asynchronous APIs for status, peers, priorities, IO actions, tracker/DHT/LSD announces, limits, SSL certs, resume data, queue position, storage operations and more. Holds a weak reference to the internal torrent object.
Helper struct (in libtorrent::aux) used to move/drain tracker URLs, web seeds and DHT nodes out of a torrent_info instance in one operation.
Represents a single web seed (URL or HTTP seed) including its URL, optional basic-auth credentials and extra HTTP headers. type indicates url_seed or http_seed.

objects.definition: class from_span_t {};
objects.description: Tag type used to disambiguate constructors taking a span buffer from those taking std::string (e.g. for torrent_info). Has no data or behavior.
Configuration object specifying safety limits used when parsing/loading .torrent metadata to prevent excessive memory usage.

Primary metadata holder for a .torrent. Provides constructors from bdecoded data, buffers, files and info-hashes; exposes file layout, piece info, trackers, web seeds, nodes, comments, creator, creation date, v1/v2 info-hashes and piece-layer hashes. Manages original vs modified file storages and supports limited mutation (rename/remap, add trackers/seeds/nodes).

objects.definition: using torrent_info_flags_t = flags::bitfield_flag<std::uint8_t, struct torrent_info_flags_tag>;
objects.description: Type alias representing a bitfield_flag used internally by torrent_info for compile-time-defined flag bits. Pointer form refers to the alias type itself.

Base peer record used by libtorrent to track a remote peer’s address/port, flags, statistics and connection state. Not a socket; it stores metadata and a pointer to the active peer_connection_interface when connected. Many fields are bitfields for compact storage. Construction requires port, connectable flag, and source flags. Copyability and destructor behavior are conditioned by TORRENT_USE_ASSERTS. Methods provide stats, addressing and ranking.
Concrete torrent_peer specialization storing an IPv4 address. Constructed from a tcp::endpoint, connectable flag, and source flags. Adds an address_v4 field.
Concrete torrent_peer specialization storing an IPv6 address as raw bytes (immutable). Constructed from a tcp::endpoint, connectable flag, and source flags.
Concrete torrent_peer specialization for I2P destinations. Stores the destination as a string_ptr. Non-copyable but movable. Only available when TORRENT_USE_I2P is enabled.

Concrete allocator implementing torrent_peer_allocator_interface. It manages pooled allocation of torrent_peer subclasses (ipv4_peer, ipv6_peer, and optionally i2p_peer) via aux::pool instances, and tracks allocation statistics. allocate_peer_entry() returns a torrent_peer* from the appropriate pool based on type; free_peer_entry() returns it to the pool. Statistics accessors expose cumulative and live counters. The exact peer concrete types and aux::pool are defined elsewhere.

Snapshot struct representing the current status of a torrent as returned by libtorrent::torrent_handle::status(). Contains metrics, state, timing, flags, errors, and availability. Includes nested enum state_t and several static constexpr sentinel file_index_t values. Ownership: used by clients; constructed by libtorrent internally. Destruction uses default destructor; fields are value types and smart pointers.
Enumeration of announce events sent to trackers (maps to HTTP &event=). Values indicate lifecycle state of a torrent session relative to a tracker.

Request object describing a single tracker announce or scrape, including URL, info-hash, stats (uploaded/downloaded/left), event, key, and addressing hints. Flags indicate scrape vs announce and I2P mode. Holds socket binding and optional SSL/I2P pointers. Used by tracker_connection/tracker_manager.
Parsed response from a tracker announce or scrape, including peer lists, optional external IP, tracker id, warning/failure messages, announce intervals, and swarm statistics.

Abstract callback interface implemented by torrent/session code to receive tracker events: warnings, scrape responses, full announce responses, and errors. Optionally provides logging hooks when enabled.
Base class providing shared timeout management for async operations (start/read time tracking, timer, cancelation, and virtual on-timeout hook). Designed to be used via shared_ptr.

Abstract base for specific tracker protocol connections (HTTP/UDP). Inherits timeout handling, owns an immutable tracker_request, references the tracker_manager, and reports bytes sent/received and failures. Derived classes implement start/close.

Final manager class orchestrating tracker connections (HTTP/UDP), queuing requests, routing incoming packets, updating transaction IDs, and accounting for bytes. Provides UDP send abstractions and integrates with session settings, resolver, and stats.

objects.description: Type alias representing a bitfield of flags for UDP send operations. Backed by an 8-bit storage and tagged with udp_send_flags_tag to create a distinct flag type. Intended to be used with constants like 0_bit, 1_bit, etc., to mark peer/tracker connections and behaviors such as dont_queue and dont_fragment.

Helper struct used by udp_socket::read() to return received UDP datagrams. It carries the payload buffer (span over caller-provided storage), the sender endpoint, an optional hostname (used when receiving via SOCKS5 proxy), and any error associated with the received packet.

High-level UDP socket wrapper that integrates with libtorrent’s IO context, proxying (SOCKS5), and listen socket handling. Provides async readiness notifications, batched reads via packet spans, and send APIs supporting explicit endpoints or hostnames through a SOCKS5 proxy. Exposes flag constants for classifying traffic and controlling queuing/fragmentation. Non-copyable; lifetime managed by user. Must be opened/bound before send/receive; close() to abort. Some behavior depends on external types (proxy_settings, alert_manager, resolver_interface).

A tracker_connection-derived class implementing the BitTorrent UDP tracker protocol. It manages resolving the tracker endpoint, establishing a UDP tracker connection, sending announce/scrape requests, parsing responses, handling timeouts, and caching connection IDs per tracker address. Constructed with IO context, tracker manager, a tracker_request, and a weak request_callback.

Compact value-type holder that stores either an IPv4 or IPv6 address in a plain union of raw byte arrays, with a 1-bit flag indicating which version. It provides assignment from and implicit conversion back to libtorrent::address, as well as equality/inequality comparisons. Useful for POD-like storage and serialization of IP addresses.

Endpoint container that unifies TCP and UDP endpoints. Stores a union_address plus a 16-bit port, and provides constructors/assignments from tcp::endpoint and udp::endpoint, as well as implicit conversion back to either. Facilitates storing endpoints in a protocol-agnostic, trivially-copyable form.

functions.name: libtorrent::demangle
functions.description: Returns a human-readable (demangled) version of a C++ symbol name. Useful for diagnostics (e.g., logging stack traces) when only mangled names are available. Only declared/available when assertions/debugging features are enabled by build flags (TORRENT_USE_ASSERTS, TORRENT_ASIO_DEBUGGING, TORRENT_PROFILE_CALLS, or TORRENT_DEBUG_BUFFERS).
requirements: name must be a valid null-terminated C string and must not be null.
Availability is conditional on build-time macros enabling it; callers should guard usage accordingly.

functions.name: libtorrent::print_backtrace
functions.signature: void libtorrent::print_backtrace(char* out, int len, int max_depth = 0, void* ctx = nullptr);
functions.description: Writes a textual backtrace into the provided output buffer. Intended for debugging/logging crash contexts or assertion failures. Availability is conditional on specific debugging/assertion build flags (same as demangle).
requirements: out must point to a writable buffer of at least len bytes; behavior is undefined if out is null when len > 0.
len must be non-negative; when len is 0, no output is written.
The output may be truncated to fit len; the function may or may not null-terminate if truncated (unspecified).
max_depth specifies the maximum number of frames to capture; 0 uses the implementation default (often unlimited or a sensible cap).
ctx is an optional platform-specific context for unwinding (e.g., ucontext_t on POSIX); when null, the current context is used.
Availability is conditional on build-time macros enabling it; callers should guard usage accordingly.
Thread-safety and signal-safety are unspecified; avoid calling from signal handlers unless documented elsewhere.

functions.name: libtorrent::assert_print
functions.description: Internal helper that performs printf-style formatted output for assertion diagnostics. Used to compose assertion messages. It is variadic and expects a standard printf format string and corresponding arguments.
requirements: fmt must be a valid null-terminated C string and must not be null.
The variadic arguments must exactly match the format specifiers in fmt (printf-style rules); mismatches result in undefined behavior.
The function may write to internal/logging sinks; thread-safety and reentrancy are unspecified.
Primarily intended for internal use; callers should avoid using it in production paths unless necessary.

functions.name: libtorrent::assert_fail
functions.signature: void libtorrent::assert_fail(char const* expr, int line, char const* file, char const* function, char const* val, int kind = 0);
functions.description: Internal assertion handler invoked by TORRENT_ASSERT and related macros. Records details about a failed assertion (expression string, source location, function, optional value/context string, and kind indicating regular assert vs. precondition). It may log diagnostics and typically terminates or breaks execution, but exact behavior is not specified here.
requirements: expr must be a valid null-terminated C string naming the failed expression (use "<unconditional>" for unconditional failures).
line should be the source line number corresponding to the assertion site (typically passed as __LINE__).
file must be a valid null-terminated C string with the source file path (typically __FILE__).
function must be a valid null-terminated C string with the function name (typically __func__).
val may be null or a valid null-terminated C string providing extra diagnostic information.
kind distinguishes assertion type; 0 for regular assert, 1 for precondition (inferred from macro usage).
Callers must not rely on the function returning; behavior after call is unspecified and may abort the process or trigger a breakpoint.
Intended for internal use via macros; do not call directly unless replicating macro behavior.
