functions.name: libtorrent::parse_int
functions.signature: char const* libtorrent::parse_int(char const* start, char const* end, char delimiter, std::int64_t& val, libtorrent::bdecode_errors::error_code_enum& ec);
functions.description: Parses a signed 64-bit integer from the character range [start, end), stopping at the specified delimiter. On success, writes the parsed value to val, returns a pointer to the delimiter (or position after the parsed number as defined by the implementation) and sets ec to no_error; on failure sets ec to an appropriate bdecode error and returns a pointer within [start, end).
requirements: start and end must delimit a valid contiguous buffer; start <= end.
delimiter specifies the character that terminates the integer text.
val is an output parameter and will be assigned on success.
ec is an output parameter and will be set to a value from libtorrent::bdecode_errors::error_code_enum.

functions.name: libtorrent::bdecode
functions.signature: int libtorrent::bdecode(char const* start, char const* end, libtorrent::bdecode_node& ret, libtorrent::error_code& ec, int* error_pos = nullptr, int depth_limit = 100, int token_limit = 2000000);
functions.description: Parses bencoded data from [start, end). On success, populates ret with an owning parse tree and returns 0; on failure, returns non-zero and sets ec and optionally error_pos to the failure offset. The underlying input buffer must remain valid while any node from ret is used.
requirements: start and end must delimit a contiguous buffer; start <= end.
ret will become an owning root node; do not destroy ret while using its child nodes.
The input buffer (start..end) must remain valid for the lifetime of any nodes referencing it.
If provided, error_pos receives the byte offset of the parse failure.
depth_limit controls maximum nesting; very high values increase stack usage.
token_limit caps the total number of parsed tokens to bound memory usage.
Call ret.reserve(...) beforehand if you can estimate token count to reduce reallocations.

functions.name: libtorrent::bencode
functions.signature:
template<class OutIt>
int libtorrent::bencode(OutIt out, const libtorrent::entry& e)
functions.description: Encodes a libtorrent::entry tree into bencoded form and writes it to the given output iterator. Returns the number of bytes written. Typical usage is with a back_insert_iterator to a std::vector<char> or an ostream_iterator<char>. The output iterator’s value_type must be char (8-bit).
requirements: OutIt must satisfy OutputIterator with value_type char (8-bit).
The output iterator 'out' must be valid and able to accept as many bytes as produced (e.g., a back-inserter to a container or a stream iterator to a writable stream).
The input entry 'e' must be a valid libtorrent::entry object; if it contains preformatted data, those bytes are copied verbatim.
Thread-safety or exception behavior is not specified in the header; callers should not assume either.

functions.name: libtorrent::bdecode
functions.signature:
template<class InIt>
TORRENT_DEPRECATED
libtorrent::entry libtorrent::bdecode(InIt start, InIt end)
functions.description: Parses a single bencoded entity from the iterator range [start, end) and returns it as a libtorrent::entry. On parse error (malformed input, excessive nesting, or premature end), returns a default-constructed libtorrent::entry. Deprecated API; available only when TORRENT_ABI_VERSION == 1.
requirements: Only available when TORRENT_ABI_VERSION == 1 at compile time.
InIt must be an InputIterator whose dereferenced value is a 1-byte char-like type (static requirement in parser).
The range [start, end) must be valid and should contain exactly one complete bencoded entity; otherwise a default-constructed entry is returned.
Maximum supported nesting depth is less than 100; deeper input is treated as an error.
Callers should detect errors by checking if the returned entry is default-constructed (empty).
The function does not modify the caller’s iterators (parameters are passed by value).

functions.name: libtorrent::bdecode
functions.signature:
template<class InIt>
TORRENT_DEPRECATED
libtorrent::entry libtorrent::bdecode(InIt start, InIt end, typename std::iterator_traits<InIt>::difference_type& len)
functions.description: Parses a bencoded entity from the iterator range [start, end), returning it as a libtorrent::entry and setting 'len' to the number of iterator steps consumed. On parse error, returns a default-constructed libtorrent::entry; 'len' is set to the distance advanced during parsing. Deprecated API; available only when TORRENT_ABI_VERSION == 1.
requirements: Only available when TORRENT_ABI_VERSION == 1 at compile time.
InIt must be an InputIterator whose dereferenced value is a 1-byte char-like type (static requirement in parser).
The range [start, end) must be valid and should begin with a complete bencoded entity; otherwise a default-constructed entry is returned.
The output parameter 'len' must be a valid lvalue of type std::iterator_traits<InIt>::difference_type; it will be assigned the consumed distance (may be zero on early error).
Maximum supported nesting depth is less than 100; deeper input is treated as an error.
Callers should detect errors by checking if the returned entry is default-constructed (empty).

functions.name: libtorrent::set_bits
functions.signature: void libtorrent::set_bits(std::uint8_t const* k, std::uint8_t* bits, int len);
functions.description: Sets a set of bloom filter bits (in the destination bit array) derived from the key k. Intended to add an entry to a bloom filter represented by the byte array bits of length len bytes. The key is expected to be a hash (e.g., SHA-1) used to determine which bits to set.
requirements: k must point to at least the key length used by the implementation (in this codebase typically 20 bytes for a SHA-1 hash).
bits must be a valid, writable buffer of at least len bytes.
len must be non-negative; if len is 0, bits may be null but the function will perform no useful work.
The bloom filter represented by bits must be initialized (e.g., zeroed) before first use if you want predictable behavior.

functions.name: libtorrent::has_bits
functions.signature: bool libtorrent::has_bits(std::uint8_t const* k, std::uint8_t const* bits, int len);
functions.description: Checks whether all bloom filter bits corresponding to key k are set in the bit array bits of length len bytes. Intended to test membership in a bloom filter (subject to false positives). Returns true if the key’s mapped bits are set, false otherwise.
requirements: k must point to at least the key length used by the implementation (in this codebase typically 20 bytes for a SHA-1 hash).
bits must be a valid, readable buffer of at least len bytes.
len must be non-negative; if len is 0, the function will always report absence (implementation-dependent).
The same len and bit layout must be used consistently with set_bits for meaningful results.

functions.name: libtorrent::count_zero_bits
functions.signature: int libtorrent::count_zero_bits(std::uint8_t const* bits, int len);
functions.description: Counts the number of zero-valued bits in the bloom filter bit array bits of length len bytes. Useful for estimating bloom filter occupancy or size of the inserted set.
requirements: bits must be a valid, readable buffer of at least len bytes.
len must be non-negative.
Returns a value in the range [0, len*8].

functions.name: libtorrent::bloom_filter::find
functions.description: Tests whether the bloom filter likely contains the given SHA-1 key k by verifying that all corresponding bits are set. This is a standard bloom-filter membership check and may yield false positives but not false negatives (assuming consistent use).
requirements: The bloom_filter instance must have been initialized (constructor or clear).
k must be a valid, initialized sha1_hash value.
Thread-safety is not guaranteed; concurrent modifications to the same filter must be synchronized.

functions.name: libtorrent::bloom_filter::set
functions.description: Adds the SHA-1 key k to the bloom filter by setting the corresponding bits in the internal bit array.
requirements: k must be a valid, initialized sha1_hash value.
Modifies internal state; callers must synchronize if used from multiple threads on the same instance.

functions.name: libtorrent::bloom_filter::to_string
functions.description: Serializes the bloom filter’s internal bit array to a binary std::string of exactly N bytes. Useful for persistence or network transmission.
requirements: The returned string contains raw binary data of size N; callers must handle embedded null bytes appropriately.
The bloom_filter instance must be in a valid state.

functions.name: libtorrent::bloom_filter::from_string
functions.description: Deserializes N bytes from str into the bloom filter’s internal bit array, replacing its current contents. Intended to restore a filter from a previously serialized representation.
requirements: str must point to at least N readable bytes. No null-termination is required or assumed.
Overwrites the current filter contents; ensure the input format matches to_string’s output (same N and layout).
Callers must ensure alignment and lifetime of str during the call. Thread-safety is not guaranteed for concurrent access.

functions.name: libtorrent::bloom_filter::clear
functions.description: Clears the bloom filter by setting all bits in the internal array to zero.
requirements: Invalidates any previous membership state; subsequent find() will return false until elements are set again.
Not thread-safe w.r.t. concurrent operations on the same instance.

functions.name: libtorrent::bloom_filter::size
functions.description: Estimates the number of inserted elements in the bloom filter based on the fraction of zero bits (using a standard estimator). Returns a floating-point estimate; accuracy depends on filter parameters and load. May return +inf when the filter is completely saturated (no zero bits).
requirements: The filter must have N>0 bytes; behavior for N==0 is not applicable for this template as N is a positive compile-time constant in typical use.
Returns a finite float in normal conditions; may return infinity when all bits are set.

functions.name: libtorrent::bloom_filter::bloom_filter
functions.description: Default constructor. Initializes the internal bit array to all zeros, creating an empty bloom filter of N bytes.
requirements: No arguments. After construction the filter is empty and ready for use.

requirements: Under encryption-enabled builds, depends on m_recv_buffer state; otherwise availability may vary with build flags.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::supports_holepunch
functions.description: Indicates whether the remote peer supports the holepunch extension (non-zero holepunch message id negotiated).
requirements: None beyond valid object state.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::set_ut_pex
functions.description: Associates a ut_pex_peer_store with this peer connection for PEX-related peer tracking and introduction lookups.
requirements: Available only when TORRENT_DISABLE_EXTENSIONS is not defined.
Argument ut_pex must be a valid weak_ptr (may be empty to clear).

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::was_introduced_by
functions.description: Queries the associated ut_pex peer store (if any) to determine if this peer was introduced by the given endpoint (for holepunch or PEX correlation).
requirements: Available only when TORRENT_DISABLE_EXTENSIONS is not defined.
Argument ep must be a valid tcp::endpoint.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::support_extensions
functions.description: Returns true if the remote peer’s handshake indicated support for the BitTorrent extension protocol.
requirements: None beyond valid object state.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::on_choke
functions.description: Message handler invoked as choke message bytes are received; processes the choke once the full message has arrived.
requirements: received should reflect how many bytes of the message have been received so far.
Intended for internal protocol processing; caller must ensure message framing/state correctness.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::on_unchoke
functions.description: Message handler for unchoke message; processes it when sufficient bytes have been received.
requirements: received must reflect bytes received for this message so far.
Internal use tied to the message parsing loop.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::on_interested
functions.description: Message handler for interested message; updates state once the message is fully read.
requirements: received must reflect bytes received for this message so far.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::on_not_interested
functions.description: Message handler for not_interested message.
requirements: received must reflect bytes received for this message so far.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::on_have
functions.description: Message handler for have message (peer announces possession of a piece).
requirements: received must reflect bytes received for this message so far.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::on_bitfield
functions.description: Message handler for bitfield message containing the peer’s piece availability bitmap.
requirements: received must reflect bytes received for this message so far.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::on_request
functions.description: Message handler for request message (peer requests a piece block).
requirements: received must reflect bytes received for this message so far.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::on_piece
functions.description: Message handler for piece message carrying a block of data.
requirements: received must reflect bytes received for this message so far.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::on_cancel
functions.description: Message handler for cancel message.
requirements: received must reflect bytes received for this message so far.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::on_hash_request
functions.description: Message handler for hash_request (merkle tree hash) message.
requirements: received must reflect bytes received for this message so far.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::on_hashes
functions.description: Message handler for hashes message (transmits merkle tree hashes).
requirements: received must reflect bytes received for this message so far.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::on_hash_reject
functions.description: Message handler for hash_reject message (rejects a hash request).
requirements: received must reflect bytes received for this message so far.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::on_dht_port
functions.description: Message handler for DHT port announcement from the peer.
requirements: received must reflect bytes received for this message so far.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::on_suggest_piece
functions.description: Message handler for FAST extension suggest_piece message.
requirements: received must reflect bytes received for this message so far.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::on_have_all
functions.description: Message handler for FAST extension have_all message (peer claims to have all pieces).
requirements: received must reflect bytes received for this message so far.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::on_have_none
functions.description: Message handler for FAST extension have_none message (peer claims to have no pieces).
requirements: received must reflect bytes received for this message so far.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::on_reject_request
functions.description: Message handler for FAST extension reject_request message.
requirements: received must reflect bytes received for this message so far.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::on_allowed_fast
functions.description: Message handler for FAST extension allowed_fast message.
requirements: received must reflect bytes received for this message so far.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::on_holepunch
functions.description: Dispatches handling of an incoming holepunch extension message.
requirements: Peer must support holepunch (negotiated message id); otherwise message will be unsupported.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::on_extended
functions.description: Message handler for the extension protocol (message id 20). Handles vendor-specific extension messages.
requirements: received must reflect bytes received for this message so far.
Peer must have indicated extension protocol support in the handshake.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::on_extended_handshake
functions.description: Processes the extension protocol handshake payload, negotiating supported extension message IDs (e.g., upload_only, holepunch, share_mode, dont_have).
requirements: Peer must support extensions.
Should be called after receiving the extension handshake payload.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::write_choke
functions.description: Queues a choke message to be sent to the peer, indicating we will not serve requests.
requirements: Connection must be in a state where sending BitTorrent messages is valid (handshake completed).

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::write_unchoke
functions.description: Queues an unchoke message to be sent to the peer, allowing it to request blocks.
requirements: Handshake should be completed before sending protocol messages.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::write_interested
functions.description: Queues an interested message indicating we are interested in the peer’s pieces.
requirements: Handshake should be completed before sending protocol messages.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::write_not_interested
functions.description: Queues a not_interested message indicating we are not interested in the peer’s pieces.
requirements: Handshake should be completed before sending protocol messages.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::write_request
functions.description: Queues a request message for a specific block (piece index, offset, length) from the peer.
requirements: r must describe a valid block within the torrent’s bounds (piece index, begin, length) consistent with protocol rules. Specific range constraints are not documented here.
Handshake should be completed before sending protocol messages.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::write_cancel
functions.description: Queues a cancel message for a previously requested block.
requirements: r must match a previously issued request to be meaningful.
Handshake should be completed before sending protocol messages.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::write_bitfield
functions.description: Queues a bitfield message advertising our current piece availability.
requirements: Number of torrent pieces must be known (magnet links may defer this until metadata is available).
Handshake should be completed before sending protocol messages.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::write_have
functions.description: Queues a have message indicating we have completed the specified piece.
requirements: index must refer to a valid piece within the torrent.
Handshake should be completed before sending protocol messages.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::write_dont_have
functions.description: Queues a dont_have extension message indicating we no longer have the specified piece.
requirements: Peer must support the dont_have extension (negotiated message id).
index must refer to a valid piece within the torrent.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::write_piece
functions.signature: void write_piece(peer_request const& r, disk_buffer_holder buffer) override;
functions.description: Queues a piece message with payload data for the requested block.
requirements: r must describe the block being sent and be consistent with buffer length.
buffer must hold the exact payload to transmit and remain valid until queued for sending.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::write_keepalive
functions.description: Queues a keepalive message to keep the connection active when no other messages are being sent.
requirements: Connection must be open.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::write_handshake
functions.description: Queues the BitTorrent handshake message to the peer, advertising protocol identifier, reserved bits, info-hash, and peer_id.
requirements: Should be called when initiating/accepting a BitTorrent connection prior to other BitTorrent messages.
Requires that the connection knows the torrent’s info-hash and our peer_id.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::write_upload_only
functions.description: Queues an extension message advertising or updating our upload-only state to the peer.
requirements: Peer must support extensions and the upload_only message id.
enabled selects whether to advertise upload-only mode.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::write_extensions
functions.description: Queues the extension protocol handshake payload describing supported extension messages and features.
requirements: Peer must support the extension protocol.
Should be sent during/after the extended handshake phase.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::write_share_mode
functions.description: Queues an extension message advertising share mode to the peer (extension-dependent).
requirements: Peer must support extensions and the share_mode message id.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::write_holepunch_msg
functions.signature: void write_holepunch_msg(hp_message type, tcp::endpoint const& ep, hp_error error = hp_error::no_error);
functions.description: Queues a holepunch extension message of the specified type, optionally including an endpoint and error code, for NAT traversal coordination.
requirements: Peer must support extensions and the holepunch message id.
Argument ep must be a valid endpoint if required by the message type.
error should be hp_error::no_error unless reporting a failure.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::write_hash_request
functions.description: Queues a merkle hash request message as part of the merkle tree (v2) data verification process.
requirements: req must be a valid hash_request structure describing the desired hashes.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::write_hashes
functions.signature: void write_hashes(hash_request const& req, span<sha256_hash> hashes);
functions.description: Queues a hashes message responding to a hash request with a span of SHA-256 hashes.
requirements: req must correspond to the request being answered.
hashes must reference a valid contiguous span of sha256_hash entries with the expected count for the request.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::write_hash_reject
functions.signature: void write_hash_reject(hash_request const& req, sha256_hash const& file_root);
functions.description: Queues a hash_reject message indicating rejection of a hash request, including the root hash for context.
requirements: req must be the request being rejected.
file_root must be the correct file root hash for the rejected request.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::maybe_send_hash_request
functions.description: Internal trigger to send a pending merkle hash request if appropriate based on current state and pending queue.
requirements: Assumes internal state tracking of m_hash_requests; intended for internal use.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::write_dht_port
functions.description: Queues a DHT port message advertising our UDP listen port to the peer (DHT extension).
requirements: listen_port must be a valid UDP port number in range [0, 65535].

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::write_have_all
functions.description: Queues a FAST extension have_all message indicating we have all pieces.
requirements: Peer should support FAST extension semantics for correct interpretation.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::write_have_none
functions.description: Queues a FAST extension have_none message indicating we have no pieces.
requirements: Peer should support FAST extension semantics for correct interpretation.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::write_reject_request
functions.description: Queues a FAST extension reject_request message to reject a specific block request.
requirements: Argument must specify the request being rejected.
Peer should support FAST extension semantics for correct interpretation.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::write_allow_fast
functions.description: Queues a FAST extension allowed_fast message granting the peer permission to request the specified piece despite choking.
requirements: piece must refer to a valid piece index.
Peer should support FAST extension semantics for correct interpretation.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::write_suggest
functions.description: Queues a FAST extension suggest_piece message suggesting the peer request the specified piece.
requirements: piece must refer to a valid piece index.
Peer should support FAST extension semantics for correct interpretation.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::on_connected
functions.description: Callback invoked when the underlying transport connection is established; used to kick off the BitTorrent handshake and initial messaging.
requirements: Should be invoked by the connection management logic; not intended for external callers.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::on_metadata
functions.description: Callback invoked when torrent metadata becomes available (e.g., after magnet link). Allows sending bitfield and other metadata-dependent messages.
requirements: Torrent metadata must have become available for the associated torrent before this is called.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::check_invariant
functions.description: Internal debug-only invariant checker for bt_peer_connection state. Used in builds with TORRENT_USE_INVARIANT_CHECKS to validate assumptions.
requirements: Available only when TORRENT_USE_INVARIANT_CHECKS is defined.
Intended for debugging; no functional effect in release builds.

functions.name: bt_peer_connection::append_const_send_buffer
functions.signature:
template <typename Holder>
void append_const_send_buffer(Holder holder, int size);
functions.description: Appends data to the send buffer. If encryption is active, makes a mutable copy of the buffer contents before queuing (since encryption mutates the data). Otherwise forwards the holder directly to append_send_buffer.
requirements: If TORRENT_DISABLE_ENCRYPTION is not defined and encryption is active, Holder’s data() must return a pointer to a contiguous memory region of at least size bytes.
Holder must be movable (it is std::move’d into append_send_buffer in the non-encrypted path).
size must be non-negative and must not exceed the actual size of the data in holder.

functions.name: libtorrent::unchoke_sort
functions.signature: int libtorrent::unchoke_sort(std::vector<libtorrent::peer_connection*>& peers, libtorrent::time_duration unchoke_interval, libtorrent::aux::session_settings const& sett)
functions.description: Sorts the given vector of peer_connection pointers in-place such that the first N entries (where N is the function’s return value) represent the peers that should be unchoked. This behaves like a partial sort: only the first N elements are ordered; elements beyond N are not sorted. Usage: pass the current peer list along with the unchoke interval and session settings; then unchoke the first N peers and do not assume any ordering for the rest. Details of the exact ranking criteria are not present in this header and are library-internal.
requirements: The peers vector is reordered in-place; callers must allow modification of the vector’s element order.
Only the first N elements (where N is the return value) are valid for unchoking; do not assume any ordering or meaning for elements beyond N.
The peers vector may be empty; handling of empty input is supported by definition of in-place sorting.
Each element of peers should be a pointer to a libtorrent::peer_connection object; behavior for null pointers is unspecified in this header.
sett must refer to a valid libtorrent::aux::session_settings object; it is read-only from the function’s perspective (passed as const&).
unchoke_interval influences the unchoke decision; acceptable range or units beyond being a time_duration are not specified in this header.

functions.name: libtorrent::client_data_t::client_data_t
functions.description: Default-constructs a client_data_t holding a null pointer. Used to initialize the wrapper before assigning a specific user pointer.
requirements: Object is initialized to hold a nullptr; no user data is stored until assigned via constructor or operator=.
Dereferencing or using the contained pointer requires callers to first assign a valid pointer of some type via the templated constructor or assignment operator.

functions.name: libtorrent::client_data_t::client_data_t
functions.description: Templated constructor that stores an opaque user pointer of type T*. The type information is recorded so the same T must be used to retrieve it later. Intended for passing a caller-owned cookie into libtorrent and retrieving it in callbacks.
requirements: Parameter v is a pointer of type T*; T is any type (including cv-qualified), except void/void const if TORRENT_ABI_VERSION > 2 where such usage is prohibited by deleted overloads.
The pointer is not owned; the caller is responsible for ensuring v remains valid for the duration of use of the associated client_data_t and any retrievals.
To retrieve the pointer later, callers must use the exact same T (including cv-qualifiers) with get<T>() or the matching conversion operator.

functions.name: libtorrent::client_data_t::operator=
functions.description: Templated assignment operator that replaces the stored user pointer with v and updates the recorded type to T. Enables reusing an existing client_data_t to point to a new object.
requirements: Parameter v is a pointer of type T*; T is any type (including cv-qualified), except void/void const if TORRENT_ABI_VERSION > 2 where such usage is prohibited by deleted overloads.
The pointer is not owned; the caller must ensure v remains valid for any subsequent retrievals.
After assignment, retrieval must use the exact same T (including cv-qualifiers) with get<T>() or the matching conversion operator.

functions.name: libtorrent::client_data_t::operator=
functions.description: Assignment from void* is explicitly deleted (when present) to prevent storing a pointer without type information, enforcing type-safe usage via the templated overload.
requirements: This function cannot be called; any attempt to assign a void* to client_data_t is ill-formed and will not compile.
This deleted declaration is only present when TORRENT_ABI_VERSION > 2; otherwise only the templated operator=(T*) participates in overload resolution.

functions.name: libtorrent::client_data_t::get
functions.description: Returns the stored pointer as type T* if and only if T exactly matches the type used when the pointer was stored (including cv-qualifiers). Otherwise returns nullptr. Used to safely recover the user data.
requirements: T must be identical to the type used when assigning/constructing the stored pointer, including cv-qualifiers; otherwise the function returns nullptr.
Callers must check for a nullptr return and handle it appropriately before dereferencing.
The underlying pointer must still be valid; this wrapper does not manage lifetime.

functions.name: libtorrent::client_data_t::operator void*
functions.description: Implicit conversion to void* is explicitly deleted (when present) to prevent type-unsafe extraction of the stored pointer.
requirements: This function cannot be called; any attempt to convert client_data_t to void* is ill-formed and will not compile.
This deleted declaration is only present when TORRENT_ABI_VERSION > 2; otherwise the conversion operator is not provided.

functions.name: libtorrent::client_data_t::operator void const*
functions.description: Implicit conversion to void const* is explicitly deleted (when present) to prevent type-unsafe extraction of the stored pointer.
requirements: This function cannot be called; any attempt to convert client_data_t to void const* is ill-formed and will not compile.
This deleted declaration is only present when TORRENT_ABI_VERSION > 2; otherwise the conversion operator is not provided.

functions.name: libtorrent::error_to_close_reason
functions.description: Converts a libtorrent::error_code to a libtorrent::close_reason_t value describing why a peer connection should be (or was) closed. Use this to translate lower-level/libtorrent error codes into a standardized close reason for logging, metrics, or disconnect decisions. The exact mapping from error codes to close reasons is implementation-defined and not documented in this header.
requirements: Argument ec must be a valid libtorrent::error_code object (value type); a default-constructed error_code is allowed.
For meaningful results, ec should represent an error originating from libtorrent operations; otherwise the mapping may be generic or unspecified.
No ownership or lifetime constraints beyond the const reference parameter exist (ec must outlive the call).
Thread-safety and exception behavior are not specified in this header; callers should not assume noexcept or thread-safe behavior without consulting implementation/documentation.

functions.name: libtorrent::copy_ptr::copy_ptr
functions.description: Default-constructs an empty copy_ptr that does not own any object.
requirements: Constructs an object in an empty state (equivalent to holding nullptr).
No type requirements on T for default construction.

functions.name: libtorrent::copy_ptr::reset
functions.description: Replaces the managed object with t, deleting the previously owned object (if any). Passing nullptr releases ownership, leaving the copy_ptr empty.
requirements: t may be nullptr to release ownership.
If t is non-null, it must point to a heap-allocated T suitable for deletion with delete.
After calling reset with a non-null t, the caller must not delete or otherwise manage t.
Any previously managed object (if any) will be deleted; callers must ensure no other owners exist for that object.

functions.name: libtorrent::copy_ptr::operator=
functions.description: Copy-assigns from p using deep copy semantics. Replaces the current managed object with a new T copy of p’s object, or releases ownership if p is empty.
requirements: This operator can only be called on an lvalue (ref-qualified with &).
T must be CopyConstructible; assignment performs new T(*p.m_ptr) when p is non-empty.
Self-assignment is handled; if both point to the same object, no change occurs.
May delete the currently managed object; callers must ensure no other owners exist.
May throw if T’s copy constructor throws.

functions.name: libtorrent::copy_ptr::operator->
functions.description: Provides pointer-like access to the managed object for non-const copy_ptr.
requirements: The copy_ptr must not be empty; dereferencing a null pointer results in undefined behavior.
Caller must ensure the returned pointer is not used after the managed object is reset or destroyed.

functions.name: libtorrent::copy_ptr::operator*
functions.description: Dereferences to the managed object, returning a reference for non-const copy_ptr.
requirements: The copy_ptr must not be empty; dereferencing when empty results in undefined behavior.
The reference becomes invalid if the copy_ptr is reset or destroyed.

functions.name: libtorrent::copy_ptr::swap
functions.description: Swaps the contents of this copy_ptr with p, exchanging ownership of the managed objects.
requirements: p must be a valid libtorrent::copy_ptr<T> reference.
After swap, both objects remain valid; no allocation or deletion is performed aside from swapping ownership.

functions.name: libtorrent::copy_ptr::operator bool
functions.description: Checks whether the copy_ptr holds a non-null managed object. Returns true if not empty, false otherwise.
requirements: Usable in boolean contexts due to explicit conversion; does not allow implicit integer conversions.
No preconditions; does not modify state.

functions.name: libtorrent::crc32c_32
functions.description: Computes a CRC-32C (Castagnoli) checksum for a single 32-bit value. Intended for fast integrity hashing of a 32-bit word. Details such as byte order, initial seed, and final XOR are not documented in this header and are therefore unknown.
requirements: Argument may be any 32-bit unsigned value (no documented range restrictions).
No error reporting is documented; the return value is the computed 32-bit checksum.
Endianness, initial CRC seed, and final XOR are not specified; callers should not rely on a particular convention without checking the implementation.

functions.name: libtorrent::crc32c
functions.description: Computes a CRC-32C (Castagnoli) checksum over a sequence of 64-bit words. The data is provided as a pointer to const std::uint64_t and a count of elements. Intended for bulk integrity hashing. Details such as byte order within words, initial seed, and final XOR are not documented and are therefore unknown.
requirements: If the element count is greater than 0, the pointer must be non-null and point to a readable array of at least the specified number of std::uint64_t elements.
The element count must be non-negative.
The pointer must be correctly aligned for std::uint64_t according to the platform’s alignment requirements.
The memory region referenced must remain valid for the duration of the call (no concurrent deallocation or mutation that would invalidate reads).
No explicit error reporting is documented; the return value is the computed 32-bit checksum.
Endianness of the data, initial CRC seed, and final XOR are not specified; callers should not rely on a particular convention without checking the implementation.

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::create_torrent
functions.signature: explicit libtorrent::create_torrent::create_torrent(libtorrent::file_storage& fs, int piece_size = 0, libtorrent::create_flags_t flags = {});
functions.description: Constructs a create_torrent object from a file_storage. piece_size must be a power of two and at least 16 KiB; 0 lets libtorrent choose automatically. flags controls creation behavior (e.g., v1_only, v2_only, modification_time, symlinks, etc.). Keep the file_storage alive as long as the create_torrent exists.
requirements: fs must describe all files and their sizes before construction.
fs (and any referenced storage) must remain alive for the entire lifetime of the create_torrent object.
piece_size must be a power of two and >= 16 KiB; 0 means auto-select.
Piece sizes > 128 MiB are rejected and will throw lt::system_error on use.
flags must be a valid combination of libtorrent::create_flags_t; semantics per flags documentation.
If v1_only is set, you must set all v1 hashes via set_hash() before generate(); setting any v2 hash is an error.
If v2_only is set, you must set all v2 hashes via set_hash2() before generate(); setting any v1 hash is an error.

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::~create_torrent
functions.description: Destructor for create_torrent. Releases any internal state. No special action is required from callers.
requirements: The referenced file_storage/torrent_info objects must still be valid up to (and including) destruction of this object, per constructor notes.

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::generate
functions.description: Builds and returns the .torrent as a bencode tree (entry). You can further modify the entry before bencoding to a file or stream. The resulting torrent is v1, v2, or hybrid depending on flags and which hashes were set. On failure, throws system_error with an explanatory message.
requirements: The associated file_storage must contain at least one non-empty file; otherwise this throws.
All required hashes must be set prior to calling: either all v1 piece hashes via set_hash(), all v2 per-file piece roots via set_hash2(), or both for a hybrid torrent, depending on flags.
For v2 metadata, file/directory name conflicts (a directory and a file with the same name) are invalid and cause failure.
If constructed with v1_only, no v2 hashes may be set; with v2_only, no v1 hashes may be set.
Caller must handle exceptions (std::system_error) thrown on any validation failure.

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::generate_buf
functions.description: Generates the .torrent as a bencoded byte buffer ready to write to disk. Equivalent to bencoding the result of generate().
requirements: Same preconditions and error behavior as generate().
Caller should expect std::system_error on failure and handle it accordingly.

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::files
functions.description: Returns an immutable reference to the file_storage used for creating the torrent.
requirements: Returned reference remains valid only while the referenced file_storage (owned externally) and this create_torrent object are alive.

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::set_comment
functions.description: Sets the optional UTF-8 comment field in the torrent metadata.
requirements: str should point to a UTF-8 encoded, null-terminated string. If null or empty, behavior is to clear or set empty comment (exact handling unspecified).

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::set_creator
functions.description: Sets the optional UTF-8 "created by" field (creator) in the torrent metadata.
requirements: str should point to a UTF-8 encoded, null-terminated string.

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::set_creation_date
functions.description: Sets the creation time (POSIX seconds). If set to 0, the "creation date" field is omitted from the generated torrent.
requirements: timestamp is POSIX seconds since epoch.
Set before generate() to affect the output.

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::set_hash
functions.description: Sets the v1 SHA-1 hash for a specific global piece index. All pieces must be set before generate() for v1 or hybrid torrents. A zero SHA-1 is treated as "not set". Calling this when constructed with v2_only throws std::system_error.
requirements: index must be within [0, num_pieces()).
h must be a valid SHA-1; all-zero hash is ignored (considered unset).
For v1 or hybrid torrents, the hash for every piece must be set prior to generate().
Must not be called if the create_torrent was constructed with v2_only; doing so will throw.

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::set_hash2
functions.signature: void libtorrent::create_torrent::set_hash2(libtorrent::file_index_t file, libtorrent::piece_index_t::diff_type piece, libtorrent::sha256_hash const& h);
functions.description: Sets the v2 per-file piece root (SHA-256) for a given file and file-relative piece index (starting at 0 for the file’s first piece). Each root is the merkle tree root of the 16 KiB blocks of that piece. An all-zero SHA-256 is treated as "not set". Calling this when constructed with v1_only throws std::system_error.
requirements: file must be a valid file index in the file_storage.
piece is relative to the first piece of the specified file and must be within that file’s piece range.
h must be a valid SHA-256; all-zero hash is ignored (considered unset).
For v2 or hybrid torrents, all required per-file piece roots must be set prior to generate().
Must not be called if constructed with v1_only; doing so will throw.

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::set_file_hash
functions.description: Deprecated (ABI < 3). Sets a legacy SHA-1 file hash stored under the key "sha1" for the file (or in the root info dictionary for single-file torrents). Obsolete with BitTorrent v2.
requirements: index must be a valid file index.
h should be a SHA-1 value. Semantics only apply to v1 metadata.
Available only when building with TORRENT_ABI_VERSION < 3.

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::add_url_seed
functions.description: Adds a URL seed. For single-file torrents this should be an HTTP URL to a file with identical content; for multi-file torrents it should point to a directory hosting the torrent’s files under the torrent name.
requirements: url should be a valid HTTP(S) URL string view; actual scheme requirements per documentation indicate HTTP for single-file. Multiple seeds are allowed.

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::add_http_seed
functions.description: Adds an HTTP seed (BEP 17-style). Semantics similar to add_url_seed().
requirements: url should be a valid HTTP(S) URL string view. Multiple seeds are allowed.

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::add_node
functions.description: Adds a bootstrap DHT node (host, port) to the torrent for trackerless operation.
requirements: node.first must be a hostname or IP string; node.second must be a valid port number (1-65535). Multiple nodes are allowed.

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::add_tracker
functions.description: Adds a tracker URL with an optional tier. All tier-0 trackers are tried first, then tier-1, etc. URL should be http:// or udp:// to a tracker that serves this torrent’s info-hash.
requirements: url should be a valid tracker URL with scheme http:// or udp://.
tier should be >= 0 (ordering/fallback tier). Multiple trackers are allowed.

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::set_root_cert
functions.description: Sets an X.509 root certificate in PEM format to make the torrent an SSL torrent. Peers must present certificates signed by this root.
requirements: cert must contain PEM-encoded certificate data (not a path).
Set before generate() to embed the certificate info as needed.

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::set_priv
functions.description: Sets the private flag on the torrent, asking clients not to use DHT or other peer sources besides trackers.
requirements: Call before generate() to affect the resulting metadata.

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::priv
functions.description: Returns whether the torrent is marked private.

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::is_v2_only
functions.description: Returns true if the creator is configured to only generate v2 metadata.

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::is_v1_only
functions.description: Returns true if the creator is configured to only generate v1 metadata and to not enforce v2 padding rules.

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::num_pieces
functions.description: Returns the total number of pieces in the file_storage.

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::end_piece
functions.description: Returns one-past-the-last global piece index.

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::piece_range
functions.description: Returns the half-open range [0, end_piece()) of all piece indices.

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::end_file
functions.description: Returns one-past-the-last file index.

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::file_range
functions.description: Returns the half-open range of all file indices in the torrent.

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::file_piece_range
functions.description: For v2 and hybrid torrents: returns the range of file-relative piece indices for the specified file, starting at 0 for the file’s first piece.
requirements: f must be a valid file index in the file_storage.

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::total_size
functions.description: Returns the total number of bytes across all files (including pad files).

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::piece_length
functions.description: Returns the standard piece length (all pieces except possibly the last).

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::piece_size
functions.description: Returns the size of a specific piece by global index (last piece may be shorter).
requirements: i must be within [0, num_pieces()).

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::merkle_tree
functions.description: Deprecated (BEP 30 support removed). For old merkle torrents, would return the merkle hash tree after generate(). In current versions this function is deprecated and returns an empty vector (per inline definition here).
requirements: Only relevant for legacy BEP 30 merkle torrents; support removed. Do not rely on this in new code.

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::add_similar_torrent
functions.description: Adds a similar torrent (by info-hash) reference (BEP 38) indicating expected shared content.
requirements: ih must be a valid v1 info-hash (SHA-1). Multiple similar torrents may be added.

functions.name: libtorrent::create_torrent::add_collection
functions.description: Adds a collection name (BEP 38) that groups torrents expected to share files with this one.
requirements: c should be a UTF-8 string view naming a collection. Multiple collections may be added.

functions.name: libtorrent::aux::nop
functions.description: No-op callback helper matching the signature void(piece_index_t). Used as a default progress callback for set_piece_hashes().

functions.name: libtorrent::add_files
functions.signature: void libtorrent::add_files(libtorrent::file_storage& fs, std::string const& file, std::function<bool(std::string)> p, libtorrent::create_flags_t flags = {});
functions.description: Recursively adds files rooted at path to file_storage. The predicate p is called for every file and directory; return true to include/traverse. The ".." directory is never traversed. flags should match those intended for create_torrent.
requirements: file must name a file or directory path accessible to the process.
Predicate p must be callable as bool(std::string const&) and should return true to include/traverse.
flags should be consistent with how the torrent will be created (e.g., no_attributes).
The function may skip unsupported attributes on some OS/filesystems; behavior is implementation-defined.

functions.name: libtorrent::set_piece_hashes
functions.signature: void libtorrent::set_piece_hashes(libtorrent::create_torrent& t, std::string const& p, std::function<void(libtorrent::piece_index_t)> const& f, libtorrent::error_code& ec);
functions.description: Reads files located under root path p, computes piece hashes and sets them into t. Calls callback f between each piece to report progress. Reports file I/O errors via ec (no exceptions).
requirements: t must have been constructed for the same file layout as exists under p.
p must be a valid filesystem path where the torrent’s files exist.
f must be callable as void(piece_index_t).
Caller must check ec after return to detect errors.
May perform significant I/O; ensure adequate permissions.

functions.name: libtorrent::aux::get_file_attributes
functions.description: Returns file attribute flags for a filesystem object at path p (e.g., hidden, executable, symlink). Intended for internal use during file enumeration/creation.
requirements: p must refer to an accessible filesystem object. On unsupported platforms some attributes may not be available.

functions.name: libtorrent::aux::get_symlink_path
functions.description: Returns the symlink target path for a filesystem object at p if it is a symbolic link; otherwise likely returns an empty string. Intended for internal use during torrent creation with symlink support.
requirements: p should reference a filesystem path. Must have permission to query symlink metadata.
Behavior when p is not a symlink is implementation-defined (commonly empty string).

functions.name: demangle
functions.description: Return a human-readable (demangled) C++ type or symbol name for the given mangled symbol. Intended for diagnostics/logging (e.g., printing handler types). Implementation is not shown in this header; availability and exact behavior may depend on platform/ABI.
requirements: name must be a non-null, null-terminated C-string.
The returned std::string contains the demangled name or a best-effort representation if demangling fails.
Behavior and fidelity may vary by platform/ABI (e.g., Itanium/GNU vs MSVC).

functions.name: has_outstanding_async
functions.description: Query whether there is a tracked outstanding async operation with the given name. Intended for debug builds with TORRENT_ASIO_DEBUGGING to check if an async task with this label is currently registered.
requirements: Only available when TORRENT_ASIO_DEBUGGING is defined; otherwise this function is not compiled in.
name must be a non-null, null-terminated C-string corresponding to the label used with add_outstanding_async/complete_async.
Thread-safe: the function internally synchronizes, and may be called from any thread.

functions.name: add_outstanding_async
functions.description: Register/start an outstanding async operation by name and capture a backtrace the first time this name is seen. Used for debugging async lifetimes and leak detection in builds with TORRENT_ASIO_DEBUGGING.
requirements: Only available when TORRENT_ASIO_DEBUGGING is defined; otherwise this function is not compiled in.
name must be a non-null, null-terminated C-string and should uniquely identify the async operation kind.
Every successful add_outstanding_async(name) must eventually be paired with a matching complete_async(name) to decrement the reference count.
Thread-safe: may be called from any thread; internal synchronization is provided.

functions.name: complete_async
functions.description: Mark completion of a previously registered async operation for the given name and record a wakeup event (timestamp, optional context switches, and operation name). Used for debugging async usage with TORRENT_ASIO_DEBUGGING.
requirements: Only available when TORRENT_ASIO_DEBUGGING is defined; otherwise this function is not compiled in.
name must be the same non-null, null-terminated label previously passed to add_outstanding_async for the operation being completed.
Must not be called more times than add_outstanding_async for the same name; otherwise an internal assertion (refs > 0) will fail in assert-enabled builds.
Thread-safe: may be called from any thread; internal synchronization is provided.

functions.name: async_inc_threads
functions.description: Increment the internal counter of threads participating in async operations tracking. Used by the debugging infrastructure to adjust expectations when accounting outstanding async handlers.
requirements: Only available when TORRENT_ASIO_DEBUGGING is defined; otherwise this function is not compiled in.
Must be paired with async_dec_threads() to keep the internal thread count accurate (call in symmetrical places, e.g., thread start/stop).
Thread-safe: may be called from any thread; internal synchronization is provided.

functions.name: async_dec_threads
functions.description: Decrement the internal counter of threads participating in async operations tracking. Complements async_inc_threads() in the debugging infrastructure.
requirements: Only available when TORRENT_ASIO_DEBUGGING is defined; otherwise this function is not compiled in.
Should only be called after a prior async_inc_threads() for the same logical thread participation; avoid decrementing below zero to prevent underflow or incorrect diagnostics.
Thread-safe: may be called from any thread; internal synchronization is provided.

functions.name: log_async
functions.description: Print diagnostic information about outstanding async operations whose reference count exceeds the number of participating threads minus one, including their names, counts, and captured backtraces. Returns the total count of such outstanding references considered ‘suspicious’.
requirements: Only available when TORRENT_ASIO_DEBUGGING is defined; otherwise this function is not compiled in.
Thread-safe: may be called from any thread; internal synchronization is provided.
Writes to stdout using std::printf; callers should ensure an appropriate logging/console environment if they rely on the output.

functions.name: log_handler_allocators
functions.description: Print a summary of handler allocator storage usage (capacity, largest allocation size, and demangled handler type) for internal handler types. Intended for diagnostics; automatically registered with atexit upon the first record_handler_allocation call.
requirements: Only available when TORRENT_ASIO_DEBUGGING is defined; otherwise this function is not compiled in.
Thread-safe: the function internally takes a mutex and may be called from any thread.
Writes a report to stdout using std::printf; callers should ensure output is acceptable in their environment.
No exceptions are thrown (noexcept).

functions.name: libtorrent::single_threaded::is_single_thread
functions.description: Check that all calls on this object occur from a single thread. On first call (or before thread_started()) it captures the current thread id; subsequent calls return true only if called from the same thread. In non-assert builds (TORRENT_USE_ASSERTS off), this always returns true and performs no tracking.
requirements: Object must remain alive across calls; the thread identity is stored within the object.
Safe usage pattern: call from the intended owning thread first (or call thread_started()) to establish the thread id before other threads interact with the object.
Behavior differs by build: with TORRENT_USE_ASSERTS off, function always returns true and does not enforce single-threading.

functions.name: libtorrent::single_threaded::is_not_thread
functions.description: Return true if the current call is made from a thread different from the one recorded in this object. If no thread has been recorded yet, returns true. In non-assert builds (TORRENT_USE_ASSERTS off), always returns true.
requirements: Object must remain alive across calls; the recorded thread id is stored within the object.
Behavior differs by build: with TORRENT_USE_ASSERTS off, function always returns true and does not enforce or check thread identity.

functions.name: libtorrent::single_threaded::thread_started
functions.description: Record the current thread id as the owning thread for this object. Useful to explicitly establish the thread identity before checks via is_single_thread()/is_not_thread(). In non-assert builds (TORRENT_USE_ASSERTS off), this is a no-op.
requirements: Should be called from the thread intended to own/use the object to establish the reference thread for subsequent checks.
Behavior differs by build: with TORRENT_USE_ASSERTS off, this function does nothing.

functions.name: libtorrent::buffer_allocator_interface::free_disk_buffer
functions.description: Pure virtual callback used to release a disk buffer back to the allocator used by libtorrent. Implement this in your disk buffer allocator to take ownership of the pointer and free/return it to the pool. Typically invoked by disk_buffer_holder when it is destroyed/reset or moved-from object is cleaned up.
requirements: b must be a pointer to a disk buffer that was allocated/handed out by the same allocator implementation (inferred from interface purpose)
The implementation must be safe to call with any buffer it previously provided; behavior for nullptr is unspecified by this header
The implementing allocator must remain valid for the duration of any holders that may call back into it to free buffers

functions.name: libtorrent::disk_buffer_holder::operator=
functions.description: Move-assignment operator. Transfers ownership of the held disk buffer from the source holder to this holder. After the move, the source holder is left empty (as-if default-constructed). Designed to be noexcept to allow efficient container moves.
requirements: This operator can only be invoked on an lvalue (note the & qualifier)
After assignment, the moved-from holder must not be assumed to hold a valid buffer; only destruction, reset, or reassignment are safe operations on it
The allocator associated with the incoming holder must outlive this holder until it frees/releases the buffer

functions.name: libtorrent::disk_buffer_holder::disk_buffer_holder
functions.description: Move constructor. Takes ownership of the buffer managed by another disk_buffer_holder. The source is left empty (as-if default-constructed).
requirements: After construction, the moved-from holder must not be assumed to hold a valid buffer; only destruction, reset, or reassignment are safe operations on it
The allocator pointer moved into this instance must remain valid for the lifetime of this holder while it owns a buffer

functions.name: libtorrent::disk_buffer_holder::~disk_buffer_holder
functions.description: Destructor. Frees the held disk buffer, if any, by calling the associated allocator’s free function and clears internal state.
requirements: If a buffer is owned, the associated allocator must still be valid at the time of destruction so the buffer can be freed safely

functions.name: libtorrent::disk_buffer_holder::data
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the held buffer or nullptr if the holder is empty. Although the type is char*, the class advertises that the buffer may not be modified in place (see is_mutable() == false).
requirements: If is_mutable() returns false (it always does in this class), callers must treat the returned pointer as read-only memory and must not modify the buffer contents in place
The returned pointer becomes invalid once the holder is destroyed, reset, or moved-from

functions.name: libtorrent::disk_buffer_holder::reset
functions.description: Releases the held disk buffer (if any) via the associated allocator and clears the holder to a default-constructed state (no buffer, no allocator).
requirements: The associated allocator must still be valid when reset() is called so the buffer can be freed safely
After reset(), previously obtained data() pointers are invalid and must not be used

functions.name: libtorrent::disk_buffer_holder::swap
functions.description: Swaps the allocator pointer, buffer pointer, and size with another holder. No allocation or deallocation occurs. Useful for exception-safe ownership transfer.
requirements: h must be a valid disk_buffer_holder instance; after swap, both holders’ data() and allocator associations are exchanged
Any outstanding data() pointers held externally may now refer to the other holder’s buffer; callers must account for this when using swap

functions.name: libtorrent::disk_buffer_holder::is_mutable
functions.description: Indicates whether the held buffer may be modified in place. This implementation always returns false, signaling read-only access semantics for the buffer memory.
requirements: Callers must not modify the buffer in place when this returns false (always)

functions.name: libtorrent::disk_buffer_holder::operator bool
functions.description: Checks whether the holder currently owns a buffer. Returns true if a buffer is held, false otherwise. Intended for simple validity tests in conditionals.
requirements: None beyond standard lifetime rules; value may change after moves, reset(), or assignment

functions.name: libtorrent::disk_buffer_holder::size
functions.description: Returns the size (in bytes) associated with the held buffer. If no buffer is held, this returns the stored size value (typically 0 as constructed).
requirements: Do not assume size() > 0 implies data() is non-null unless established by construction/assignment; always check operator bool() or data() first if needed

functions.name: libtorrent::disk_interface::new_torrent
functions.signature: virtual libtorrent::storage_holder libtorrent::disk_interface::new_torrent(libtorrent::storage_params const& p, std::shared_ptr<void> const& torrent) = 0;
functions.description: Create and register a new torrent storage with the disk I/O backend and return an owning storage_holder for it. The shared_ptr can be used by the implementation to keep the torrent internals alive while disk operations are pending.
requirements: Must be called to obtain a storage_index_t (via returned storage_holder) before issuing any I/O for that torrent.
The returned storage_holder owns the storage and must outlive any operations issued against it.
Implementations must be prepared to receive further async_* calls referencing the returned storage.

functions.name: libtorrent::disk_interface::remove_torrent
functions.description: Unregister and release resources associated with the specified storage/torrent. Does not delete files from disk; only internal resources are released.
requirements: The storage_index_t must refer to a previously created storage (via new_torrent).
Must synchronize with any outstanding operations for the storage to avoid races.

functions.name: libtorrent::disk_interface::async_read
functions.signature: virtual void libtorrent::disk_interface::async_read(libtorrent::storage_index_t storage, libtorrent::peer_request const& r, std::function<void(libtorrent::disk_buffer_holder, libtorrent::storage_error const&)> handler, libtorrent::disk_job_flags_t flags = {}) = 0;
functions.description: Asynchronously read the requested range for a storage/torrent and invoke handler with a disk_buffer_holder containing the data or an error. Flags can hint cache behavior.
requirements: storage must be a valid storage_index_t previously obtained from new_torrent.
handler must be a valid callable and is expected to be posted back onto libtorrent's network thread by the implementation.
The peer_request r may not be block-aligned (reads can be unaligned).
flags may include: force_copy, sequential_access, volatile_read (hints only).

functions.name: libtorrent::disk_interface::async_write
functions.signature: virtual bool libtorrent::disk_interface::async_write(libtorrent::storage_index_t storage, libtorrent::peer_request const& r, char const* buf, std::shared_ptr<libtorrent::disk_observer> o, std::function<void(libtorrent::storage_error const&)> handler, libtorrent::disk_job_flags_t flags = {}) = 0;
functions.description: Asynchronously write a block-aligned range for a storage/torrent from buf and invoke handler on completion. Returns true if the write queue is full; in that case, the disk_observer will be used to notify when writes can resume.
requirements: storage must be a valid storage_index_t previously obtained from new_torrent.
The write range in r is guaranteed to be block-aligned (callers must respect this).
buf must point to at least r.length bytes of valid data until the implementation consumes/copies it.
handler must be a valid callable and is expected to be posted back onto the network thread by the implementation.
If the function returns true (queue full), the caller must wait for disk_observer notification before issuing more writes.
flags may include: force_copy, sequential_access (hints only).

functions.name: libtorrent::disk_interface::async_hash
functions.signature: virtual void libtorrent::disk_interface::async_hash(libtorrent::storage_index_t storage, libtorrent::piece_index_t piece, libtorrent::span<libtorrent::sha256_hash> v2, libtorrent::disk_job_flags_t flags, std::function<void(libtorrent::piece_index_t, libtorrent::sha1_hash const&, libtorrent::storage_error const&)> handler) = 0;
functions.description: Compute hash(es) for a piece. If flags contains v1_hash, compute the SHA-1 piece hash. If v2 span is non-empty, fill it with the SHA-256 block hashes for the piece. Optionally flush the piece if flags contains flush_piece. Completion is reported via handler.
requirements: storage must be valid.
If v2 is non-empty, it must be large enough to hold all v2 block hashes for the piece.
If v2 is empty, v2 (SHA-256) hashes are not computed.
If flags does not include v1_hash, the SHA-1 piece hash does not need to be computed (handler will still receive a value; exact value when not computed is unspecified by this header).
handler must be a valid callable and will be posted back onto the network thread by the implementation.

functions.name: libtorrent::disk_interface::async_hash2
functions.signature: virtual void libtorrent::disk_interface::async_hash2(libtorrent::storage_index_t storage, libtorrent::piece_index_t piece, int offset, libtorrent::disk_job_flags_t flags, std::function<void(libtorrent::piece_index_t, libtorrent::sha256_hash const&, libtorrent::storage_error const&)> handler) = 0;
functions.description: Compute the v2 (SHA-256) hash of a single block at offset within the specified piece. Completion is reported via handler.
requirements: storage must be valid.
offset selects the target block within the piece; exact units/constraints are not specified in this header (likely block offset).
handler must be a valid callable and will be posted back onto the network thread by the implementation.

functions.name: libtorrent::disk_interface::async_move_storage
functions.signature: virtual void libtorrent::disk_interface::async_move_storage(libtorrent::storage_index_t storage, std::string p, libtorrent::move_flags_t flags, std::function<void(libtorrent::status_t, std::string const&, libtorrent::storage_error const&)> handler) = 0;
functions.description: Move the files for a storage/torrent to a new location p. Must synchronize with outstanding I/O. Behavior regarding overwrites/replacements is controlled by move_flags_t flags. Completion and final path are reported via handler.
requirements: storage must be valid.
Implementation must synchronize against any outstanding operations to avoid races during move.
flags must be set consistently with the intended move behavior (see move_flags_t).
handler must be a valid callable.

functions.name: libtorrent::disk_interface::async_release_files
functions.signature: virtual void libtorrent::disk_interface::async_release_files(libtorrent::storage_index_t storage, std::function<void()> handler = std::function<void()>()) = 0;
functions.description: Close all open files associated with the specified storage/torrent, providing a point where all files are closed. Some files may be reopened by subsequent operations. Calls handler on completion.
requirements: storage must be valid.
handler may be omitted; if provided it must be callable.

functions.name: libtorrent::disk_interface::async_check_files
functions.signature: virtual void libtorrent::disk_interface::async_check_files(libtorrent::storage_index_t storage, libtorrent::add_torrent_params const* resume_data, libtorrent::aux::vector<std::string, libtorrent::file_index_t> links, std::function<void(libtorrent::status_t, libtorrent::storage_error const&)> handler) = 0;
functions.description: Validate on-disk files for the torrent against resume_data and optionally create hard links from known-identical files provided via links. Also verify seed-mode conditions and pieces indicated as present. Completion is reported via handler.
requirements: storage must be valid.
If links is non-empty, it must contain one entry per file in the torrent; an empty string indicates no known identical file for that position.
Pad files and files with zero priority may be skipped during verification, per the comments.
If resume_data indicates seed_mode, all files/pieces must exist on disk with correct sizes (implementation should verify).
handler must be a valid callable.

functions.name: libtorrent::disk_interface::async_stop_torrent
functions.signature: virtual void libtorrent::disk_interface::async_stop_torrent(libtorrent::storage_index_t storage, std::function<void()> handler = std::function<void()>()) = 0;
functions.description: Flush and quiesce any cached data and pending operations for the torrent. Should at least do what async_release_files() does. Calls handler when done.
requirements: storage must be valid.
handler may be omitted; if provided it must be callable.

functions.name: libtorrent::disk_interface::async_rename_file
functions.signature: virtual void libtorrent::disk_interface::async_rename_file(libtorrent::storage_index_t storage, libtorrent::file_index_t index, std::string name, std::function<void(std::string const&, libtorrent::file_index_t, libtorrent::storage_error const&)> handler) = 0;
functions.description: Rename a file in the storage/torrent identified by index to the new name. Must synchronize with any outstanding operations affecting the file. Reports the (final) name, index, and error via handler.
requirements: storage must be valid.
index must refer to a valid file in the torrent.
Implementation must synchronize with outstanding read/write/move ops on the target file to avoid races.
handler must be a valid callable.

functions.name: libtorrent::disk_interface::async_delete_files
functions.signature: virtual void libtorrent::disk_interface::async_delete_files(libtorrent::storage_index_t storage, libtorrent::remove_flags_t options, std::function<void(libtorrent::storage_error const&)> handler) = 0;
functions.description: Delete some or all on-disk files for the torrent according to options (e.g. delete_files, delete_partfile). Completion is reported via handler.
requirements: storage must be valid.
options determines which files to remove and must be set appropriately.
handler must be a valid callable.

functions.name: libtorrent::disk_interface::async_set_file_priority
functions.signature: virtual void libtorrent::disk_interface::async_set_file_priority(libtorrent::storage_index_t storage, libtorrent::aux::vector<libtorrent::download_priority_t, libtorrent::file_index_t> prio, std::function<void(libtorrent::storage_error const&, libtorrent::aux::vector<libtorrent::download_priority_t, libtorrent::file_index_t>)> handler) = 0;
functions.description: Set per-file priorities for a torrent. Changing priority to/from 0 may move data to/from the partfile; implementation must synchronize this work with outstanding operations. Calls handler with resulting priorities.
requirements: storage must be valid.
If prio is shorter than the number of files, unspecified files are assumed to have default priority.
Implementation must coordinate with any outstanding I/O that could be affected by moving data to/from partfile.
handler must be a valid callable.

functions.name: libtorrent::disk_interface::async_clear_piece
functions.signature: virtual void libtorrent::disk_interface::async_clear_piece(libtorrent::storage_index_t storage, libtorrent::piece_index_t index, std::function<void(libtorrent::piece_index_t)> handler) = 0;
functions.description: Synchronize with outstanding disk operations for the specified piece after it failed hash check, ensuring it is safe to re-request and overwrite its blocks. Calls handler when ready.
requirements: storage must be valid.
index must refer to a valid piece.
handler must be a valid callable.

functions.name: libtorrent::disk_interface::update_stats_counters
functions.description: Update gauges in the counters object that are not continuously updated during operations. Called before counters are snapshotted to the client.
requirements: May be called at any time by libtorrent to refresh gauges.
Must not modify external state; should only update entries in c.

functions.name: libtorrent::disk_interface::get_status
functions.description: Return a snapshot of currently open files for the specified storage/torrent, including open modes and last-use timestamps.
requirements: storage must be valid.
Should be safe to call concurrently with ongoing operations and reflect current state.

functions.name: libtorrent::disk_interface::abort
functions.description: Initiate shutdown of the disk I/O backend. Flush pending writes, cancel hash jobs, and tear down internal threads. If wait is true, do not return until threads have stopped and jobs are finished/aborted.
requirements: May be called during session shutdown.
If wait == true, the call must block until cleanup is complete and the object is ready to be destructed.

functions.name: libtorrent::disk_interface::submit_jobs
functions.description: Notify the disk I/O backend after batching async_* calls so worker threads can be awakened to process queued jobs.
requirements: May be called after issuing one or more async_* operations to improve batching.
Implementation should wake any waiting worker thread(s).

functions.name: libtorrent::disk_interface::settings_updated
functions.description: Notify the disk I/O backend that session settings have changed so it can react to relevant changes.
requirements: May be called whenever settings change; implementation should re-read settings provided via the constructor.

functions.name: libtorrent::storage_holder::storage_holder
functions.description: Default-construct an empty storage_holder that does not reference any disk_interface storage.
requirements: Object is empty; conversion to storage_index_t must not be used until it holds a valid storage (check operator bool).

functions.name: libtorrent::storage_holder::storage_holder
functions.description: Construct a storage_holder that owns the storage identified by idx and is tied to the given disk_interface.
requirements: idx must be a valid storage index managed by disk_io.
The referenced disk_interface must outlive the holder or until reset/destruction removes the torrent.

functions.name: libtorrent::storage_holder::storage_holder
functions.description: Move-construct from another storage_holder, transferring ownership and leaving the source empty.
requirements: After the move, rhs is left empty and must not be used for conversion to storage_index_t without reinitialization.

functions.name: libtorrent::storage_holder::~storage_holder
functions.description: Destructor. If bound to a disk_interface, calls remove_torrent(m_idx) on destruction to release the associated storage.
requirements: Destruction will notify the underlying disk_interface to remove the torrent if it is still held.
No exceptions should be thrown from the destructor (usual C++ guidance; not explicitly stated).

functions.name: libtorrent::storage_holder::operator bool
functions.description: Return true if this holder currently references a disk_interface storage; false if empty.
requirements: Safe to call at any time. Use to check validity before converting to storage_index_t.

functions.name: libtorrent::storage_holder::operator storage_index_t
functions.description: Implicit conversion to the underlying storage_index_t for use with disk_interface functions. Asserts internally that the holder is valid.
requirements: Must only be called when the holder is valid (operator bool() returns true); otherwise assertion may trigger.

functions.name: libtorrent::storage_holder::reset
functions.description: Release the currently held storage: calls remove_torrent(m_idx) if bound, then clears the reference to become empty.
requirements: Safe to call multiple times; subsequent calls when already empty are no-ops.

functions.name: libtorrent::storage_holder::operator=
functions.description: Copy assignment is disabled; storage_holder is non-copyable to preserve unique ownership semantics.
requirements: Copy assignment cannot be used; attempting to copy will fail at compile time.

functions.name: libtorrent::storage_holder::operator=
functions.description: Move-assign from another storage_holder. If this holder previously owned a storage, it first calls remove_torrent() on it, then takes ownership from rhs and leaves rhs empty.
requirements: Self-assignment is handled (no-op).
After move-assignment, rhs is left empty and must not be used for conversion to storage_index_t without reinitialization.

functions.name: libtorrent::disk_observer::on_disk
functions.description: Callback invoked by libtorrent when the disk cache size has dropped below the low watermark and downloading from peers may be resumed. Implement this in a subclass of libtorrent::disk_observer to receive notifications. This is a pure virtual function; the base class provides no implementation.
requirements: Must be overridden in a class derived from libtorrent::disk_observer (pure virtual).
The derived instance must remain alive for as long as it may receive callbacks (lifetime management is the responsibility of the registrant).
No arguments are provided and no value is returned; implementations should perform any needed reaction to the low-disk-watermark event.

functions.name: libtorrent::entry::type
