functions.description: Returns the current concrete type tag of this variant entry (integer, string, list, dictionary, undefined, or preformatted). Typical use is to branch before calling a typed accessor.
requirements: Object must be a valid libtorrent::entry instance.
Callers should use the returned value to pick the matching accessor (integer(), string(), list(), dict(), preformatted()).

functions.name: libtorrent::entry::entry
functions.description: Constructs an entry initialized to a dictionary by copying the provided dictionary value.
requirements: The input dictionary must contain keys comparable by aux::strview_less (standard string keys).
The argument is copied; it need not outlive the entry.

functions.name: libtorrent::entry::~entry
functions.description: Destructor. Destroys the entry and releases owned resources.
requirements: The entry must not be used after destruction.

functions.name: libtorrent::entry::operator=
functions.description: Assigns from a bdecode_node, replacing this entry with the decoded structure.
requirements: This is an lvalue-qualified assignment; the target must be an lvalue.
The source node must be valid.

functions.name: libtorrent::entry::integer
functions.description: Returns a mutable reference to the stored integer value. Throws system_error if the entry is not an integer.
requirements: The entry must currently hold an integer (type() == int_t).
On mismatch, a system_error is thrown.

functions.name: libtorrent::entry::string
functions.description: Returns a mutable reference to the stored string. Throws system_error if the entry is not a string.
requirements: The entry must currently hold a string (type() == string_t).
On mismatch, a system_error is thrown.

functions.name: libtorrent::entry::list
functions.description: Returns a mutable reference to the stored list. Throws system_error if the entry is not a list.
requirements: The entry must currently hold a list (type() == list_t).
On mismatch, a system_error is thrown.

functions.name: libtorrent::entry::dict
functions.description: Returns a mutable reference to the stored dictionary. Throws system_error if the entry is not a dictionary.
requirements: The entry must currently hold a dictionary (type() == dictionary_t).
On mismatch, a system_error is thrown.

functions.name: libtorrent::entry::preformatted
functions.description: Returns a mutable reference to the stored preformatted byte vector. Throws system_error if the entry is not preformatted.
requirements: The entry must currently hold a preformatted blob (type() == preformatted_t).
On mismatch, a system_error is thrown.

functions.name: libtorrent::entry::swap
functions.description: Swaps the contents of this entry with e.
requirements: Both entries must be valid.
After swap, both objects remain valid with exchanged contents.

functions.name: libtorrent::entry::operator[]
functions.description: Dictionary index (inserting). Requires this entry to be a dictionary; returns a reference to the value for key, inserting a default-constructed entry if it doesn’t exist.
requirements: This entry must currently hold a dictionary (type() == dictionary_t); otherwise throws system_error.
key must be a valid string_view; its data is copied as the dictionary key if insertion happens.

functions.name: libtorrent::entry::find_key
functions.description: Finds a key in a dictionary entry and returns a pointer to the value; returns nullptr if not found. Requires this entry to be a dictionary.
requirements: This entry must currently hold a dictionary (type() == dictionary_t); otherwise throws system_error.
key is not inserted if missing; function returns nullptr.

functions.name: libtorrent::entry::to_string
functions.description: Returns a pretty-printed JSON-style string representation of this bencoded structure. If single_line is true, emits a single-line form.
requirements: The entry must be valid. Large or deeply nested entries may produce large strings.

functions.name: libtorrent::operator==
functions.signature: bool libtorrent::operator==(libtorrent::entry const& lhs, libtorrent::entry const& rhs)
functions.description: Compares two entries for equality by value and structure.
requirements: Both entries must be valid.

functions.name: libtorrent::aux::integer_to_str
functions.description: Converts the signed 64-bit integer val to its decimal ASCII representation in buf and returns a string_view to the written characters. The returned view is not null-terminated.
requirements: buf must be a std::array<char,21> passed by lvalue reference and will be overwritten.
The returned string_view points into buf; buf must outlive the view.
Do not modify or destroy buf before consuming the returned view.
val is a 64-bit integer (entry::integer_type).

functions.name: libtorrent::enum_net_interfaces
functions.description: Returns a list of the configured IP interfaces on the machine. Use to discover local interface addresses and properties. On error, the error is reported via ec and the returned vector may be empty.
requirements: ios must be a valid, initialized libtorrent::io_context instance.
ec is used for error reporting and will be set on failure; callers should check ec after the call.
The caller should not assume any specific ordering of returned interfaces.
Returned interfaces include address, netmask, name, flags, and state as available; some fields may be empty or defaults depending on platform.

functions.name: libtorrent::enum_routes
functions.description: Enumerates the system routing table and returns a list of routes (destination, netmask, gateway, source hint, interface name, MTU). On error, ec is set and the returned list may be empty.
requirements: ios must be a valid, initialized libtorrent::io_context instance.
ec is used for error reporting and will be set on failure; callers should check ec after the call.
The caller should not assume any specific ordering or completeness of the returned routes; availability is platform-dependent.

functions.name: libtorrent::family
functions.description: Returns AF_INET or AF_INET6 depending on the address family of a. Use to branch logic based on IPv4 vs IPv6.
requirements: a must be a valid libtorrent::address instance.
The return value corresponds to standard address family constants (AF_INET or AF_INET6).

functions.name: libtorrent::match_addr_mask
functions.signature: bool libtorrent::match_addr_mask(libtorrent::address const& a1, libtorrent::address const& a2, libtorrent::address const& mask)
functions.description: Returns whether (a1 & mask) == (a2 & mask). Useful for checking whether two addresses are in the same subnet under the given mask.
requirements: a1, a2, and mask must all be of the same address family (either all IPv4 or all IPv6).
Addresses should be valid; behavior is undefined if families differ.

functions.name: libtorrent::build_netmask
functions.description: Builds and returns a netmask address for the specified address family with the most significant bits set according to bits. Intended to construct subnet masks for IPv4 or IPv6.
requirements: family must specify an address family (AF_INET for IPv4 or AF_INET6 for IPv6).
bits must be a non-negative prefix length appropriate for the family (commonly 0..32 for AF_INET and 0..128 for AF_INET6).
If bits exceeds the maximum for the family, the resulting behavior is unspecified by this header.

functions.name: libtorrent::get_gateway
functions.signature: boost::optional<libtorrent::address> libtorrent::get_gateway(libtorrent::ip_interface const& iface, libtorrent::span<libtorrent::ip_route const> routes)
functions.description: Returns the configured gateway address for the given interface if one is present in routes; otherwise returns boost::none. Use to find the next-hop gateway for an interface.
requirements: iface should correspond to a real interface present in routes for meaningful results.
routes must reference a valid, non-dangling span of ip_route entries for the current system state.

functions.name: libtorrent::has_internet_route
functions.signature: bool libtorrent::has_internet_route(libtorrent::string_view device, int family, libtorrent::span<libtorrent::ip_route const> routes)
functions.description: Checks whether there is a route to the internet for any global address of the specified address family via the named device. Returns true if such a route exists.
requirements: device should be the interface name as reported by enumeration (exact match).
family must be a valid address family (AF_INET or AF_INET6).
routes must reference a valid, non-dangling span of ip_route entries.

functions.name: libtorrent::has_any_internet_route
functions.description: Returns whether there are any routes to the internet present in the routing table. Can be used to detect if the routing table is fully populated.
requirements: routes must reference a valid, non-dangling span of ip_route entries.
Interpretation of "internet route" is implementation-defined within the library; callers should not assume specific destination prefixes.

functions.name: libtorrent::bind_socket_to_device
functions.signature:
template <class Socket>
libtorrent::address libtorrent::bind_socket_to_device(libtorrent::io_context& ios, Socket& sock, libtorrent::tcp const& protocol, char const* device_name, int port, libtorrent::error_code& ec)
functions.description: Attempts to bind the given socket to the specified network device or address. If device_name parses as an IP address, the socket is bound directly to that address. Otherwise, on platforms supporting SO_BINDTODEVICE, the socket is bound to the device; if not supported or it fails, the function looks up the interface by name and binds to one of its IP addresses matching protocol. Returns the address the socket was bound to (or address_v4::any() when SO_BINDTODEVICE succeeds and no specific IP needs verification). Callers on systems without SO_BINDTODEVICE should verify the socket’s local endpoint after connect/accept if they require strict device binding.
requirements: sock must be an open socket of a type compatible with bind and the specified protocol (e.g., protocol v4/v6 must match the address family to bind).
sock must not already be bound or connected when calling bind.
protocol must be either boost::asio::ip::tcp::v4() or boost::asio::ip::tcp::v6() to select the address family.
device_name may be an interface name or a numeric IP address string; if an IPv4 any address ("0.0.0.0") is provided with IPv6 protocol, it is treated as "::" per implementation comment.
port must be in the valid TCP port range (0..65535).
ios must be valid and is used for interface enumeration when needed.
ec is set on failure; callers must check ec after the call.

On platforms without SO_BINDTODEVICE, the function binds to a specific IP of the named device; callers who require strict device binding should verify the local endpoint after the connection is established.
If no matching device is found, ec is set to errc::no_such_device and the returned address corresponds to the attempted bind endpoint address.

functions.name: libtorrent::device_for_address
functions.signature: std::string libtorrent::device_for_address(libtorrent::address addr, libtorrent::io_context& ios, libtorrent::error_code& ec)
functions.description: Returns the device name whose local address is addr. If no matching device is found, returns an empty string. Errors are reported via ec.
requirements: addr must be a valid local address to resolve to a device; otherwise an empty result is expected.
ios must be a valid, initialized libtorrent::io_context instance.
ec is used for error reporting and will be set on failure; callers should check ec after the call.

functions.name: libtorrent::errors::make_error_code
functions.description: Constructs a boost::system::error_code representing a libtorrent-specific error in the libtorrent error category from the given error_code_enum value. Typical usage: create or propagate standardized libtorrent errors via error_code.
requirements: Parameter e must be a valid value of libtorrent::errors::error_code_enum.
The returned error_code uses the libtorrent error category.

functions.name: libtorrent::libtorrent_category
functions.description: Returns the singleton error_category instance that maps libtorrent error codes (errors::error_code_enum) to human-readable messages. Use this to compare categories or to construct error_code values tied to libtorrent.
requirements: Returns a reference valid for the lifetime of the process (singleton semantics).
Thread-safe to call for access to the category (typical for error_category singletons).

functions.name: libtorrent::http_category
functions.description: Returns the singleton error_category for HTTP-related errors reported by libtorrent (errors::http_errors). Use this category when interpreting HTTP status-related error_code values.
requirements: Returns a reference valid for the lifetime of the process (singleton semantics).
Thread-safe to call for access to the category (typical for error_category singletons).

functions.name: libtorrent::get_libtorrent_category
functions.description: Deprecated ABI v1 helper that returns libtorrent_category(). Provided inline for compatibility when exceptions are enabled and TORRENT_ABI_VERSION == 1.
requirements: Only available when TORRENT_ABI_VERSION == 1 and exceptions are not disabled (BOOST_NO_EXCEPTIONS not defined).
Callers should migrate to libtorrent::libtorrent_category().

functions.name: libtorrent::get_http_category
functions.description: Deprecated ABI v1 helper that returns http_category(). Provided inline for compatibility when exceptions are enabled and TORRENT_ABI_VERSION == 1.
requirements: Only available when TORRENT_ABI_VERSION == 1 and exceptions are not disabled (BOOST_NO_EXCEPTIONS not defined).
Callers should migrate to libtorrent::http_category().

functions.name: libtorrent::storage_error::operator bool
functions.description: Conversion operator returning true if this storage_error represents an error (i.e. ec.value() != 0), otherwise false. Use to test whether an operation failed.
requirements: The storage_error instance must be initialized (default-constructed or constructed with an error_code).
No side effects; safe to call repeatedly.

functions.name: libtorrent::storage_error::file
functions.description: Getter returning the index of the file (within the torrent) associated with this error. May also return special values defined in torrent_status.
requirements: Valid to call regardless of whether an error is present; returns the stored index (default is -1 cast to file_index_t).

functions.name: libtorrent::storage_error::file
functions.description: Setter storing the index of the file (within the torrent) associated with this error. Special sentinel values defined in torrent_status may be used.
requirements: Parameter f should be a valid file index within the torrent or a documented special value from torrent_status.
Does not validate the range; caller is responsible for passing meaningful indices.

functions.name: libtorrent::storage_error::operation_str
functions.description: Deprecated ABI v1 helper returning a string literal describing which file operation failed (derived from the operation field). Returns an empty string if no failure. Provided for backward compatibility.
requirements: Only available when TORRENT_ABI_VERSION == 1.
Returned pointer is a string literal and remains valid for the lifetime of the program; do not free.

functions.name: libtorrent::print_error
functions.description: Formats the given error_code into a human-readable string, using its category and value. Intended for internal use but can help with diagnostics and logging.
requirements: Parameter must be a valid boost::system::error_code (libtorrent::error_code alias).
No ownership transfer; safe to pass temporary or persistent error_code objects.

functions.name: libtorrent::plugin::~plugin
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the session-wide plugin base class. Allows proper cleanup via base-class pointer.
requirements: Must be invoked on a valid libtorrent::plugin instance (normally by libtorrent).
Any outstanding async operations should have been cancelled in abort() before destruction (per class contract).

functions.name: libtorrent::plugin::implemented_features
functions.description: Returns a bitmask of feature flags indicating which callbacks this session plugin expects to receive (e.g. tick, DHT request, alert, unknown_torrent, optimistic unchoke). If a feature is not indicated, some callbacks may not be invoked.
requirements: Return a combination of libtorrent::plugin::optimistic_unchoke_feature, tick_feature, dht_request_feature, alert_feature, unknown_torrent_feature as needed.
May be called at startup; must be noexcept in practice (no requirement stated, but throwing has no defined behavior).

functions.name: libtorrent::plugin::new_torrent
functions.signature: virtual std::shared_ptr<libtorrent::torrent_plugin> new_torrent(libtorrent::torrent_handle const& th, libtorrent::client_data_t userdata);
functions.description: Called by the session when a new torrent is added. Return a per-torrent plugin instance to attach to this torrent, or an empty shared_ptr to ignore the torrent.
requirements: May return nullptr to skip attaching to this torrent.
The returned object must derive from libtorrent::torrent_plugin if non-null.
Must not access libtorrent internals from other threads; this is called on the libtorrent network thread.
If this function throws, libtorrent will ignore the plugin for this torrent (behavior not guaranteed; prefer not to throw).

functions.name: libtorrent::plugin::added
functions.description: Notification that this session plugin has been added to a session. Use to perform session-wide initialization.
requirements: Called on the libtorrent network thread.
Must return promptly; long-running work should be deferred.

functions.name: libtorrent::plugin::abort
functions.description: Notification that the session is being aborted. Perform any cleanup necessary to allow session destruction (e.g., cancel outstanding async operations).
requirements: Should cancel/stop any outstanding operations initiated by the plugin.
Must be safe to call once at session shutdown and return promptly.

functions.name: libtorrent::plugin::on_dht_request
functions.signature: virtual bool on_dht_request(libtorrent::string_view query, libtorrent::udp::endpoint const& source, libtorrent::bdecode_node const& message, libtorrent::entry& response);
functions.description: Called when a DHT request is received. May optionally handle the request and write a response. Return true if handled.
requirements: Will only be called reliably if implemented_features() includes libtorrent::plugin::dht_request_feature.
If returning true, response should be populated with a valid DHT reply for the given query.
Arguments are only valid for the duration of the call; do not store references.

functions.name: libtorrent::plugin::on_alert
functions.description: Called when an alert is posted (alerts filtered out by category are not posted). Use to observe session events and communicate via custom alerts.
requirements: Will only be called reliably if implemented_features() includes libtorrent::plugin::alert_feature.
Parameter a is a non-null pointer to a valid alert object for the duration of the call; do not store the raw pointer beyond the call without appropriate lifetime management.

functions.name: libtorrent::plugin::on_unknown_torrent
functions.signature: virtual bool on_unknown_torrent(libtorrent::info_hash_t const& ih, libtorrent::peer_connection_handle const& pc, libtorrent::add_torrent_params& p);
functions.description: Called when an incoming connection refers to a torrent unknown to the session. Allows the plugin to provide add_torrent_params to add the torrent. Return true to indicate params should be added.
requirements: Will only be called reliably if implemented_features() includes libtorrent::plugin::unknown_torrent_feature.
If returning true, add_torrent_params p must be filled with valid parameters to add the torrent.
Do not retain pc beyond the call without following handle lifetime rules.

functions.name: libtorrent::plugin::on_tick
functions.description: Called approximately once per second for session-wide periodic work.
requirements: Will only be called reliably if implemented_features() includes libtorrent::plugin::tick_feature.
Must return promptly; avoid blocking the network thread.

functions.name: libtorrent::plugin::get_unchoke_priority
functions.description: Assigns a priority to a peer for optimistic unchoke selection. Lower values mean higher priority. Values above 2^63−1 are reserved; return 2^64−1 if no priority is assigned.
requirements: If the plugin does not wish to influence priority, return std::numeric_limits<std::uint64_t>::max().
If multiple plugins return priorities, the lowest value wins.
Do not throw exceptions; throwing has unspecified effects.

functions.name: libtorrent::plugin::save_state
functions.description: Serialize session-wide plugin state into key/value pairs to be stored in session_params.
requirements: Return a map with string keys and values; keep payload sizes reasonable.
May be called at startup/shutdown; must not depend on transient thread-local state.

functions.name: libtorrent::plugin::load_state
functions.signature: virtual void load_state(std::map<std::string, std::string> const& kv);
functions.description: Load session-wide plugin state from key/value pairs provided in session_params.
requirements: Accept missing or partial keys gracefully.
Must not block; validate values before use.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_plugin::~torrent_plugin
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the per-torrent plugin base class.
requirements: Instance must have been created by new_torrent() and attached to a torrent.
Destruction occurs on the libtorrent network thread.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_plugin::new_connection
functions.description: Called when a new peer connects to the torrent. Return a peer_plugin instance to attach to this peer, or nullptr to ignore.
requirements: If this function throws, the connection will be closed by libtorrent.
Do not keep a shared_ptr to your peer_plugin; keep weak_ptr if you need references.
Called before any peer-specific callbacks; may be invoked for bt or web seed peers (web seeds don't receive some handshake hooks).

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_plugin::on_piece_pass
functions.description: Called when a piece passed the hash check on this torrent.
requirements: index must be treated as belonging to this torrent only.
Do not perform blocking operations.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_plugin::on_piece_failed
functions.description: Called when a piece failed the hash check on this torrent.
requirements: index must be treated as belonging to this torrent only.
Do not perform blocking operations.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_plugin::tick
functions.description: Per-torrent periodic callback (approximately once per second).
requirements: Must return promptly; avoid blocking the network thread.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_plugin::on_pause
functions.description: Called when the torrent is being paused. Return true to indicate the event was fully handled and to suppress default behavior and any later plugins.
requirements: If you call pause() from within this handler, be aware it recurses into your handler; manage state to avoid unintended recursion.
Return false to allow default pause behavior.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_plugin::on_resume
functions.description: Called when the torrent is being resumed. Return true to indicate the event was fully handled and to suppress default behavior and later plugins.
requirements: If you call resume() from within this handler, be aware it recurses into your handler; manage state accordingly.
Return false to allow default resume behavior.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_plugin::on_files_checked
functions.description: Called when initial file checking completes (or immediately if there are no files). Indicates the torrent can start downloading.
requirements: Do not block the network thread.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_plugin::on_state
functions.description: Called when the torrent changes state (see torrent_status::state_t).
requirements: Do not block; handle all possible state enum values.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_plugin::on_add_peer
functions.signature: virtual void on_add_peer(libtorrent::tcp::endpoint const& ep, libtorrent::peer_source_flags_t source, libtorrent::add_peer_flags_t flags);
functions.description: Called when a peer is added to the torrent's peer list (before connecting). Provides the peer endpoint, source bitmask, and add-peer flags.
requirements: This is called for each addition; may be the first time a peer is seen (flags may include first_time) or filtered by IP filter (flags may include filtered).
Must not modify global state in a way that blocks.

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_plugin::~peer_plugin
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the per-peer plugin base class.
requirements: The instance must have been created by torrent_plugin::new_connection().
Destruction may happen upon disconnect or when the peer is removed.

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_plugin::type
functions.description: Returns a short identifier/name for this peer plugin.
requirements: Should return a stable string_view (typically referring to static storage or internal member with lifetime >= plugin).

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_plugin::add_handshake
functions.description: Add entries to the extension handshake message sent to the peer. Not called for web seeds.
requirements: May only write fields allowed by the extension protocol into e.
Do not assume the peer supports any specific extension.

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_plugin::on_disconnect
functions.description: Called when the peer is being disconnected. Useful for cleanup or logging.
requirements: Must not throw; keep work minimal since disconnect path is sensitive.

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_plugin::on_connected
functions.description: Called after an outgoing peer is successfully connected. Incoming peers are already connected when the plugin attaches and won't receive this.
requirements: Do not block; this is on the network thread.

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_plugin::on_handshake
functions.description: Called when the initial BitTorrent handshake is received. Return false to indicate the peer does not support this extension (the plugin will be removed). Not called for web seeds.
requirements: Must not assume full extension support until on_extension_handshake() confirms.
Throwing from this handler (as with most handlers) will close the connection.

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_plugin::on_extension_handshake
functions.description: Called when the peer's extension handshake is received. Return false if the extension isn't supported by this peer (the plugin will be removed). Not called for web seeds.
requirements: The bdecode_node is only valid during the call; do not store references.
Return true only if your extension is supported; otherwise return false.

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_plugin::on_choke
functions.description: Called when a choke message is received. Return true to mark the message handled and suppress further handling.
requirements: Return false to allow default behavior and other plugins to handle.

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_plugin::on_unchoke
functions.description: Called when an unchoke message is received. Return true to mark handled and suppress further handling.
requirements: Return false to allow default behavior and other plugins to handle.

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_plugin::on_interested
functions.description: Called when an interested message is received. Return true to mark handled and suppress further handling.
requirements: Return false to allow default behavior and other plugins to handle.

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_plugin::on_not_interested
functions.description: Called when a not-interested message is received. Return true to mark handled and suppress further handling.
requirements: Return false to allow default behavior and other plugins to handle.

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_plugin::on_have
functions.description: Called when a have message is received. Return true to mark handled and suppress further handling.
requirements: index refers to a piece in this torrent; validate if needed.
Return false to allow default behavior.

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_plugin::on_dont_have
functions.description: Called when a dont_have message is received. Return true to mark handled and suppress further handling.
requirements: index refers to a piece in this torrent; validate if needed.
Return false to allow default behavior.

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_plugin::on_bitfield
functions.description: Called when a bitfield message is received. Return true to mark handled and suppress further handling.
requirements: bf is valid only during the call; do not store references.
Return false to allow default behavior.

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_plugin::on_have_all
functions.description: Called when a have_all message is received. Return true to mark handled and suppress further handling.
requirements: Return false to allow default behavior.

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_plugin::on_have_none
functions.description: Called when a have_none message is received. Return true to mark handled and suppress further handling.
requirements: Return false to allow default behavior.

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_plugin::on_allowed_fast
functions.description: Called when an allowed_fast message is received. Return true to mark handled and suppress further handling.
requirements: index refers to a piece in this torrent; validate if needed.

functions.name: libtorrent::crypto_plugin::set_outgoing_key

functions.name: libtorrent::crypto_plugin::encrypt
functions.description: Encrypt the provided outgoing buffers. Returns (produce, prepend_buffers). produce is the number of bytes ready to send to the lower layer (>= input). prepend_buffers is a span of buffers owned by the plugin that must be prepended (e.g., headers/IV). Any returned buffers must remain valid until the next encrypt() call or plugin destruction.
requirements: Must return at least the number of bytes passed in send_vec as produce.
Any buffers referenced by the returned span and the span object itself must be owned by the crypto plugin and remain alive until the next encrypt() call or destruction.
May increase size to account for encryption overhead; provide required prepend buffers accordingly.

functions.name: libtorrent::crypto_plugin::decrypt
functions.description: Decrypt the provided incoming buffers. Returns (consume, produce, packet_size). consume: bytes to trim from the head of buffers. produce: bytes of plaintext now ready for the upper layer (defaults to input size if unchanged). packet_size: minimum number of bytes required to advance decryption (0 if unknown).
requirements: Must not write beyond provided buffers; may adjust in-place within receive_vec.
Return values must be consistent: 0 <= consume <= total input size; 0 <= produce <= total input size (or more only if in-place coalescing is documented by implementation); packet_size >= 0.
Must handle partial packets by indicating packet_size when more data is required.

functions.name: libtorrent::aux::pwrite_all

requirements: handle must be a valid, open file handle (not libtorrent::invalid_handle).
buf must reference a valid memory region with the data to write.
file_offset should be non-negative (typical for file offsets; exact constraints not documented).
Caller must supply a libtorrent::error_code reference to receive error information.
Thread-safety and blocking behavior are not documented here; assume a potentially blocking, synchronous write based on naming.

requirements: handle must be a valid, open file handle (not libtorrent::invalid_handle).
buf must reference a valid writable memory region large enough to receive the requested data.
file_offset should be non-negative (typical for file offsets; exact constraints not documented).
Caller must supply a libtorrent::error_code reference to receive error information.
Thread-safety and blocking behavior are not documented here; assume a potentially blocking, synchronous read based on naming.

functions.name: libtorrent::inflate_gzip
functions.signature: void libtorrent::inflate_gzip(libtorrent::span<char const> in, std::vector<char>& buffer, int maximum_size, libtorrent::error_code& ec)
functions.description: Decompresses a gzip-compressed byte span into the provided output buffer. The function inflates the gzip stream contained in 'in' and writes the uncompressed bytes to 'buffer'. If decompression fails or would exceed 'maximum_size', it reports an error via 'ec' using the libtorrent gzip error category. Intended for callers needing to inflate in-memory gzip data with a hard cap on the output size to prevent over-allocation. Whether the function appends to or replaces the contents of 'buffer' is not specified in this header (unknown).

'maximum_size' must be non-negative; if the inflated data would exceed this limit, the function sets 'ec' to gzip_errors::inflated_data_too_large and rejects the data.
Caller must check 'ec' after the call to determine success or failure; errors are reported via the error_code parameter rather than exceptions.
On gzip parsing/inflate failures, 'ec' will contain a value from libtorrent::gzip_errors in the category returned by libtorrent::gzip_category().
Thread-safety and whether 'buffer' is cleared or appended to are not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: libtorrent::validate_hash_request
functions.signature: bool libtorrent::validate_hash_request(libtorrent::hash_request const& hr, libtorrent::file_storage const& fs)
functions.description: Validates that a hash_request describes a legal range within the Merkle tree for the given torrent file_storage. Intended to be called before sending a request or accepting hashes, ensuring base/index/count/proof_layers are consistent with the file's tree layout. Details of exact constraints are defined by libtorrent’s Merkle tree structure; if invalid, the function returns false.
requirements: hr.base >= 0, hr.index >= 0, hr.count >= 0 (inferred from usage of indices and counts)
hr must refer to an existing file in fs (hr.file within fs’s valid file_index_t range)
The (base, index, count) range must fit within the Merkle tree level for the file (i.e., not exceed the number of nodes at that level)
proof_layers must be compatible with verifying the requested nodes against the file’s root (or piece-layer) hash
Callers should use the return value; do not proceed with sending/adding hashes if this returns false

requirements: files must remain valid for the lifetime of this hash_picker instance
trees must be a vector indexed by file_index_t containing a merkle_tree per file; the reference must remain valid and refer to the same storage during the picker’s lifetime

requirements: pieces must represent the set of pieces the peer can provide (typed_bitfield sized to the torrent’s number of pieces)

functions.description: Supplies hashes received in response to a prior hash_request. The picker verifies them against known roots/proofs, updates internal Merkle trees, and reports which pieces/blocks passed or failed verification.

requirements: len must be >= 0.
out must point to a writable buffer of at least len * 2 bytes.
If len > 0, in and out must be non-null and in must point to at least len readable bytes; out must be valid for writing len * 2 bytes.
If len == 0, no bytes are written.

functions.name: libtorrent::aux::from_hex
functions.description: Converts a hexadecimal text buffer into its binary representation, writing the result to out. Returns true on success and false on invalid input. The output length is (in.size() + 1) / 2 bytes.
requirements: out must point to a writable buffer of at least (in.size() + 1) / 2 bytes.
The input should contain only hex characters; use libtorrent::aux::is_hex to validate if needed.
in may be empty; if in.size() == 0, no bytes are written.
If in.size() > 0, out must be non-null and valid for the required capacity.
Callers must check the boolean return value before using the contents written to out; false indicates conversion failed due to invalid hex input.

functions.name: libtorrent::to_hex
functions.signature: void libtorrent::to_hex(char const* in, int len, char* out);
functions.description: Deprecated (available only when TORRENT_ABI_VERSION == 1). Wrapper that converts the binary buffer [in, in + len) into its hexadecimal representation, writing 2*len characters to out. Calls libtorrent::aux::to_hex under the hood.
requirements: len must be >= 0.
out must point to a writable buffer of at least len * 2 bytes.
If len > 0, in and out must be non-null and valid for the stated sizes.
Deprecated API: prefer libtorrent::aux::to_hex overloads.

functions.name: libtorrent::to_hex
functions.description: Deprecated (available only when TORRENT_ABI_VERSION == 1). Returns the hexadecimal string representation of the binary contents of s. Calls libtorrent::aux::to_hex under the hood.
requirements: s may be empty.
Deprecated API: prefer libtorrent::aux::to_hex(libtorrent::span<char const>)

functions.name: libtorrent::from_hex
functions.signature: bool libtorrent::from_hex(char const* in, int len, char* out);
functions.description: Deprecated (available only when TORRENT_ABI_VERSION == 1). Converts a hexadecimal text buffer [in, in + len) into binary and writes to out. Returns true on success and false on invalid input. Calls libtorrent::aux::from_hex under the hood. Output size is (len + 1) / 2 bytes.
requirements: len must be >= 0.
out must point to a writable buffer of at least (len + 1) / 2 bytes.
If len > 0, in and out must be non-null and valid for the stated sizes.
Input should contain only hex characters; callers must check the boolean return value before using the output.
Deprecated API: prefer libtorrent::aux::from_hex(libtorrent::span<char const>, char*).

functions.name: libtorrent::http_connection::http_connection
functions.description: Constructs an HTTP client connection object bound to a given io_context and DNS resolver. The caller supplies callbacks for connection, filtering, and HTTP events. If bottled is true, the response body is buffered up to max_bottled_buffer_size and delivered once; otherwise data is streamed. When built with SSL support, ssl_ctx is used for TLS handshakes when connecting with SSL. Typically followed by get() or start() to initiate a request.
requirements: ios (io_context&) must remain valid for the lifetime of the http_connection (stored by reference).
resolver (aux::resolver_interface&) must remain valid for the lifetime of the http_connection (stored by reference).
handler (http_handler) must be a valid callable; it will be invoked asynchronously from the io_context thread.
ch (http_connect_handler), fh (http_filter_handler), and hfh (hostname_filter_handler) must be valid callables if non-empty; they may be invoked during resolve/connect.
If bottled is true, the response body may be buffered in memory up to max_bottled_buffer_size bytes; choose a size appropriate to available memory.
max_bottled_buffer_size must be >= 0.
When built with TORRENT_USE_SSL, ssl_ctx may be provided to enable TLS for SSL connections; this parameter is unavailable when SSL support is not compiled in.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_connection::~http_connection
functions.description: Virtual destructor for http_connection. Cleans up any outstanding asynchronous operations and closes underlying resources when the object is destroyed.
requirements: The object must be destroyed on or after all user code has finished using it; after destruction, references returned from socket(), endpoints(), or url() become invalid.
Must not be used after destruction.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_connection::rate_limit
functions.description: Sets the download rate limit, in bytes per second, for this HTTP connection. A limit of 0 disables throttling (unlimited).
requirements: limit must be >= 0 (0 means unlimited).

functions.name: libtorrent::http_connection::rate_limit
functions.description: Returns the current download rate limit in bytes per second. A value of 0 indicates no limit (unlimited).

functions.name: libtorrent::http_connection::get
functions.description: Initiates an HTTP GET request to the specified URL with optional timeout, proxy, redirect handling, User-Agent, local bind, resolver flags, and Authorization string. If built with I2P support, an i2p_connection may be supplied for I2P destinations. Response and progress are reported via the http_handler supplied to the constructor. When bottled mode is enabled, data is buffered and delivered once upon completion.
requirements: url must be a valid URL string for the intended scheme (e.g. http/https; I2P destinations if built with I2P).
timeout should be a non-negative duration; a too-short timeout may abort the request.
ps may be null; if non-null, it must point to a valid aux::proxy_settings object for the duration of the operation.
handle_redirects should be >= 0; it limits how many sequential redirects are followed.
user_agent may be empty; if provided, it is sent as the User-Agent header.
bind_addr, if provided, specifies the local device and/or IP to bind the outgoing socket to.
resolve_flags control DNS resolution behavior; choose flags appropriate for your environment.
auth_ may contain credentials (e.g. for Authorization); format and semantics are application-defined.
When built without TORRENT_USE_I2P, the i2p_conn parameter is not available; when available and provided, it must point to a valid i2p_connection for the duration of the operation.
Must call from a context where the http_connection object remains alive until completion or cancellation (the operation is asynchronous).

functions.name: libtorrent::http_connection::start
functions.description: Starts an HTTP connection to a specific hostname and port using optional proxy settings, timeout, SSL flag, redirect handling, local bind, and resolver flags. If built with I2P support, an i2p_connection may be provided. Use this overload when you already split a URL into components or need non-GET methods assembled manually in m_sendbuffer.
requirements: hostname should be a non-empty DNS name or IP literal.
port must be in the range 1..65535.
timeout should be a non-negative duration.
ps may be null; if non-null, it must point to a valid aux::proxy_settings object for the duration of the operation.
ssl indicates whether to perform a TLS handshake; requires that the http_connection was constructed with an SSL context when SSL is desired.
handle_redirect should be >= 0; it limits sequential redirects to follow.
bind_addr, if provided, specifies the local device and/or IP to bind the socket to.
resolve_flags control DNS lookup behavior.
When built without TORRENT_USE_I2P, the i2p_conn parameter is not available; when available and provided, it must point to a valid i2p_connection for the duration of the operation.
Must call from a context where the http_connection object remains alive until completion or cancellation (the operation is asynchronous).

functions.name: libtorrent::http_connection::close
functions.description: Closes the HTTP connection and cancels outstanding operations. If force is true, pending asynchronous operations are aborted immediately.
requirements: Safe to call even if no operation is in progress; behavior is to close/cancel. Further operations on this object after close() may fail or have no effect.
If force is true, the caller should be prepared to handle partial/incomplete callbacks or error codes in the handler.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_connection::socket
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the underlying socket wrapper used by this HTTP connection. Useful for inspection (e.g., local/remote endpoints) but not for modification.
requirements: The returned reference is only valid while the http_connection object is alive.
Do not attempt to modify or take ownership of the underlying socket through this const reference.
The socket may be disengaged or not yet connected; callers must handle such states gracefully.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_connection::endpoints
functions.description: Returns the list of candidate remote endpoints (IP:port) resolved or considered for connection attempts.
requirements: The returned reference is only valid while the http_connection object is alive.
The vector may be empty if resolution has not completed or yielded no results; callers must handle an empty list.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_connection::url
functions.description: Returns the URL associated with the current/last request for this connection.
requirements: The returned reference is only valid while the http_connection object is alive.
May be empty if start() (host/port) was used instead of get() or before any request is initiated.

functions.name: libtorrent::is_ok_status
functions.description: Returns true if the given HTTP status code is considered successful or acceptable by libtorrent (200, 206, or any 3xx code up to 400). Intended to quickly gate handling of HTTP responses.
requirements: http_status must be a valid HTTP status code integer (typically in range 100–599).
Return value is a pure function of http_status; no side effects are implied.

functions.name: libtorrent::is_redirect
functions.description: Returns true if the given HTTP status code represents a redirect response. Use to decide whether to follow a redirect and to inspect the Location header.
requirements: http_status must be a valid HTTP status code integer (typically in range 100–599).
Return value is a pure function of http_status; no side effects are implied.

functions.name: libtorrent::resolve_redirect_location
functions.description: Resolves a redirect target (Location) against a referrer (the original request URL) to produce an absolute URL. Use when handling HTTP redirects to compute the next URL to request.
requirements: referrer should be a valid URL string representing the request that triggered the redirect (absolute URL expected).
location should be the value of the HTTP Location header (may be absolute or relative).
Return is a new string; inputs are passed by value and may be moved from by the implementation.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_parser::http_parser
functions.description: Constructs an HTTP/1.x parser. The flags parameter toggles parser behavior; currently supports dont_parse_chunks (1) to avoid parsing chunked encoding. Use to feed incoming() data incrementally and query response components.
requirements: flags must be a bitwise-or of values from http_parser::flags_t (e.g., 0 or dont_parse_chunks).
Object must remain alive while any spans or references returned from its methods are used.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_parser::~http_parser
functions.description: Destroys the HTTP parser and releases any internal resources. After destruction, any spans or references previously obtained from the parser must not be used.
requirements: All spans or references previously obtained from this instance (e.g., from get_body(), header(), headers(), chunks()) must not be accessed after destruction.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_parser::header
functions.description: Retrieves the value for a specific HTTP header field by name. Intended for accessing parsed headers after or during parsing. If the header is not present, the exact return behavior is not documented here (it may return an empty string or a stored default).
requirements: key must be the case-insensitive header field name to look up; string_view must reference valid memory for the duration of the call.
The returned reference remains valid as long as the parser object is alive and its internal header storage is not modified in a way that invalidates references (implementation-defined).
Behavior for missing keys is not explicitly documented in this header; callers should be prepared for an empty string or a reference to a static/empty value.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_parser::header_duration
functions.description: Parses a duration value from the specified HTTP header and returns it as an optional seconds32. Intended for headers like Retry-After or Cache-Control max-age. Returns boost::none if the header is missing or cannot be parsed.
requirements: key must be the header field name; string_view must be valid for the duration of the call.
Caller must handle boost::optional being disengaged (no value) when the header is absent or unparsable.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_parser::protocol
functions.description: Returns the HTTP protocol string from the status line (e.g., "HTTP/1.1").
requirements: Callable once the status line has been parsed; before that, it may be an empty string.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_parser::status_code
functions.description: Returns the parsed HTTP status code from the response status line, or -1 if not yet parsed.
requirements: Callable at any time; before the status line is parsed, returns -1.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_parser::method
functions.description: Returns the HTTP method of a parsed request (if this parser is used for requests) or as parsed from an incoming request line. For typical HTTP responses, this may be empty.
requirements: Value is only meaningful if a request line has been parsed; otherwise may be empty.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_parser::path
functions.description: Returns the request target/path from a parsed request line. For typical HTTP responses, this may be empty.
requirements: Value is only meaningful if a request line has been parsed; otherwise may be empty.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_parser::message
functions.description: Returns the reason phrase (server message) from the HTTP status line (e.g., "OK").
requirements: Callable once the status line has been parsed; before that, may be empty.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_parser::get_body
functions.description: Returns a span over the currently parsed HTTP message body bytes available to the parser. For chunked responses, this represents the assembled body according to parsing state.
requirements: The returned span refers to memory owned/managed by the parser (internally backed by the last buffer passed via incoming()); it remains valid only as long as that underlying storage remains valid and unchanged and the parser object remains alive.
Callers must not write through the returned span (it is const data).
For complete body retrieval, ensure header_finished() is true and, if not chunked, that content_length() bytes have been received; exact completeness guarantees are not documented.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_parser::header_finished
functions.description: Returns true once the HTTP header section has been fully parsed and the parser is positioned to read the body.
requirements: Use after feeding data via incoming(); before that it will be false.
No side effects; may be polled.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_parser::finished
functions.description: Returns true when the full HTTP message has been parsed (including body).
requirements: Use after feeding data via incoming(); before completion it returns false.
No side effects; may be polled.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_parser::incoming
functions.signature: std::tuple<int, int> libtorrent::http_parser::incoming(libtorrent::span<char const> recv_buffer, bool& error)
functions.description: Feeds received bytes into the parser and advances parsing of the HTTP message. Returns a tuple of two integers (semantics not documented here) and sets error to indicate parse failure. Call repeatedly as new data arrives.
requirements: recv_buffer must reference valid memory containing the next contiguous bytes from the HTTP stream; the memory must remain valid for the duration of the call.
error must be a valid reference; on return it will be set to true if a parse error occurred, otherwise false.
Call this function with data in correct order without gaps or reordering.
Do not call concurrently from multiple threads on the same parser instance (thread-safety unspecified).
Exact meaning of the returned tuple elements is not documented in this header; callers should not assume semantics beyond using the error flag and other query methods to drive parsing.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_parser::body_start
functions.description: Returns the byte offset (from the start of the received HTTP message) where the body begins, or 0 if unknown/not parsed yet.
requirements: Meaningful after headers are parsed (e.g., when header_finished() is true).

functions.name: libtorrent::http_parser::content_length
functions.description: Returns the Content-Length value parsed from headers, or -1 if not present or not yet known.
requirements: Only meaningful after headers have been parsed; otherwise returns -1.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_parser::content_range
functions.description: Returns the parsed Content-Range start and end (inclusive or exclusive semantics not specified here) as a pair, or (-1, -1) if not present.
requirements: Only meaningful when a Content-Range header was parsed; otherwise both values may be -1.
Callers should not assume inclusivity/exclusivity of the end value; this header does not specify it.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_parser::chunked_encoding
functions.description: Returns true if the response uses Transfer-Encoding: chunked.
requirements: Use after headers have been parsed to get a meaningful value.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_parser::collapse_chunk_headers
functions.description: Removes chunked-transfer headers from the supplied buffer using the parser's internal chunk list, compacting the body in-place. Returns the span of the new logical body region (the new length).
requirements: buffer must be the contiguous byte stream received from the HTTP server that this parser instance parsed (same data that was fed to incoming()).
This function relies on the internal list of parsed chunk ranges; callers must first parse the response and its chunks (via incoming() and parse_chunk_header()) so that chunk metadata is known.
The buffer memory must be writable and large enough to allow in-place compaction; the span must reference valid mutable storage for the duration of the call.
Only applicable when chunked_encoding() is true; otherwise behavior is unspecified in this header.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_parser::parse_chunk_header
functions.signature: bool libtorrent::http_parser::parse_chunk_header(libtorrent::span<char const> buf, std::int64_t* chunk_size, int* header_size)
functions.description: Parses a single chunk header from a chunked-encoding response. On success, writes the chunk byte size into chunk_size and the header byte count into header_size and returns true. Returns false if the supplied buffer does not contain a complete chunk header; in that case, provide more data and call again. A chunk_size of 0 indicates the terminating chunk; additional trailing headers may then be available in the parser.
requirements: buf must contain bytes starting at the beginning of a chunk header; provide more bytes if the header is incomplete.
chunk_size must be a non-null pointer to receive the number of data bytes in the chunk following the header (0 signifies the terminating chunk).
header_size must be a non-null pointer to receive the size in bytes of the chunk header itself; skip this many bytes to reach the chunk data.
If the function returns false, chunk_size and header_size may have been modified but their values are undefined; callers must treat them as unspecified and retry with more data.
Call this only when chunked_encoding() is true.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_parser::reset
functions.description: Resets the parser to its initial state to begin parsing a new HTTP message. Clears previously parsed headers, body state, and chunk metadata.
requirements: After reset(), any previously obtained spans or references into parser-managed data (e.g., headers, body spans) are invalid and must not be used.
Should not be called concurrently with incoming() or other methods on the same instance.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_parser::connection_close
functions.description: Returns true if the server is HTTP/1.0 or sent "Connection: close" indicating the connection should not be reused.
requirements: Meaningful after headers have been parsed; before that, may be false by default.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_parser::headers
functions.signature: std::multimap<std::string, std::string, libtorrent::aux::strview_less> const& libtorrent::http_parser::headers() const
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the multimap of parsed HTTP headers (possibly with multiple entries per key). Keys are compared using aux::strview_less for case-insensitive-like behavior.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid while the parser object is alive and its internal header container is not modified by a mutating operation (no mutators are exposed here).
Do not attempt to modify the returned container (it is const).

functions.name: libtorrent::http_parser::chunks
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the list of byte offset ranges for each chunk in a chunked response. Each pair denotes [start, end) positions within the received body stream including chunk layout as tracked by the parser.
requirements: Meaningful only for responses using chunked transfer-encoding after chunks have been parsed.
The returned reference remains valid while the parser object is alive; do not modify (const).

functions.name: libtorrent::http_seed_connection::http_seed_connection
functions.description: Constructs an HTTP-seed (web seed) peer connection. Initializes the web-connection state using the provided peer_connection_args and the web seed descriptor. Typically created by the torrent/session machinery to talk to an HTTP seed and fetch pieces over HTTP.
requirements: pack must reference a fully initialized libtorrent::peer_connection_args object valid for the lifetime of this constructor call.
web must reference a valid libtorrent::web_seed_t describing the target web seed; it must outlive construction (it is stored as a pointer member).
Must be invoked on a newly created libtorrent::http_seed_connection object; not re-entrant.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_seed_connection::type
functions.description: Returns the connection type of this peer connection. For http_seed_connection it is always connection_type::http_seed. Useful for distinguishing web seeds from other peer types.
requirements: May be called at any time after object construction.
No side effects; return value should not be assumed to change over the lifetime.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_seed_connection::on_receive
functions.description: Main receive handler for this connection. Processes incoming data from the HTTP seed, parses HTTP/chunked responses, and advances piece download state. Called by the I/O loop when data has been read or an error occurred.
requirements: error must be a valid libtorrent::error_code; if it indicates failure, the implementation treats it as a receive error.
bytes_transferred must reflect the number of new bytes available for processing in the connection’s read buffer for this event (typically as reported by the I/O layer).
Must only be called by the network/event loop associated with this connection; not thread-safe unless the surrounding library guarantees it.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_seed_connection::on_connected
functions.description: Notifies the connection that the underlying transport has connected. Performs post-connect initialization, such as issuing initial HTTP requests and setting up state for talking to the web seed.
requirements: Call only once per successful transport connection, after the socket is connected.
Must be invoked by the owning I/O/session machinery; not intended for external callers.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_seed_connection::url
functions.description: Returns the canonical URL identifying this web seed. The returned reference remains valid for the lifetime of the http_seed_connection instance.
requirements: Do not store the returned reference beyond the lifetime of the http_seed_connection instance.
The caller must not attempt to modify the returned string (it is const).

functions.name: libtorrent::http_seed_connection::get_specific_peer_info
functions.description: Populates the provided peer_info structure with http-seed-specific details for diagnostic or UI purposes. Intended to augment general peer_info with web-seed fields (e.g., URL, progress).
requirements: p must reference a valid libtorrent::peer_info object that the caller owns and can be written to.
May be called after construction; the granularity/availability of data may depend on connection state.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_seed_connection::disconnect
functions.signature: void libtorrent::http_seed_connection::disconnect(libtorrent::error_code const& ec, libtorrent::operation_t op, libtorrent::disconnect_severity_t error = libtorrent::peer_connection_interface::normal)
functions.description: Closes the connection to the HTTP seed and tears down associated state. The parameters describe the reason (error code), the operation context, and the severity used for peer management/accounting.
requirements: ec should contain the reason for disconnect; use a default-constructed error_code to indicate no specific failure if appropriate.
op must be a valid libtorrent::operation_t describing the operation during which the disconnect happened.
error must be one of libtorrent::disconnect_severity_t values; default is peer_connection_interface::normal.
Safe to call when connected or during error handling; subsequent calls after the first may be ignored depending on implementation (not specified).

functions.name: libtorrent::http_seed_connection::write_request
functions.description: Enqueues/sends an HTTP request to the web seed for the specified block of data described by peer_request. Translates the piece/block coordinates into an HTTP range request and manages request state.
requirements: r must describe a valid block within the torrent: piece index, block offset, and length must be within torrent bounds and non-negative.
May only be called when the connection is established (after on_connected) and ready to send requests.
The caller must not modify r during the call; it is passed as a const reference.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_stream::http_stream
functions.description: Constructs an HTTP proxy stream bound to the given I/O context. The stream is used to establish TCP connections via an HTTP proxy (using CONNECT when enabled). Typical usage is to construct the object, optionally configure proxy parameters (username, host header, no-connect behavior), and then call async_connect.
requirements: io_context must be a valid, running I/O context for asynchronous operations to progress.
The constructed http_stream object must remain alive for the duration of any asynchronous operations started on it.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_stream::set_no_connect
functions.description: Enables or disables sending the HTTP CONNECT request during async_connect. When set to true, the stream will connect to the proxy and complete without issuing CONNECT, allowing direct HTTP communication with the proxy instead of tunneling.
requirements: Should be called before async_connect to affect the behavior of the next connection attempt.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_stream::set_username
functions.signature: void libtorrent::http_stream::set_username(std::string const& user, std::string const& password)
functions.description: Sets proxy Basic Authentication credentials to be used in the Proxy-Authorization header during the CONNECT handshake. If not set, no Proxy-Authorization header is sent.
requirements: Call before async_connect to include credentials in the handshake.
Strings are used verbatim in a Base64-encoded "user:password" blob; ensure they match the proxy’s expected credentials format.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_stream::set_host
functions.description: Sets the Host header value to include in the HTTP CONNECT request. If unset or empty, the Host header is omitted.
requirements: Call before async_connect to include the Host header in the handshake.
Host should be a valid hostname string as expected by the proxy. (No additional validation is performed here.)

functions.name: libtorrent::http_stream::close
functions.description: Closes the underlying connection and clears the configured Host header. This non-throwing overload reports errors via the provided error_code reference and delegates to proxy_base::close(ec).
requirements: The error_code reference must be valid for the duration of the call.
May be called at any time; any outstanding asynchronous operations on the stream may complete with an error after closing.
After closing, the object must be reconnected before reuse.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_stream::async_connect
functions.signature:
template <class Handler>
void libtorrent::http_stream::async_connect(endpoint_type const& endpoint, Handler const& handler)
functions.description: Asynchronously connects to the configured HTTP proxy, optionally performs an HTTP/1.0 CONNECT handshake to tunnel to the specified remote endpoint, and invokes the completion handler with the resulting status. On success with CONNECT enabled, the proxy has returned HTTP status 200 and the stream is ready for tunneled I/O. If set_no_connect(true) was used, the CONNECT request is skipped and the handler is invoked after establishing the TCP connection to the proxy.
requirements: A valid proxy host name (m_hostname) and port (m_port) must have been configured on the underlying proxy_base prior to calling (inferred from use of m_hostname/m_port).
endpoint must be a valid endpoint_type designating the final remote target for the CONNECT tunnel.
handler must be a callable that can be invoked with a single argument of type libtorrent::error_code (completion condition).
The http_stream object must remain alive until the handler is invoked.
An io_context must be running to drive the asynchronous resolve/connect/write/read operations.
If authentication is required, set_username must be called before async_connect to include Proxy-Authorization.
If a Host header is desired, set_host must be called before async_connect.
On non-200 HTTP responses or malformed proxy replies, the handler is invoked with boost::asio::error::operation_not_supported and the stream is closed.

functions.name: libtorrent::http_tracker_connection::http_tracker_connection
functions.signature: http_tracker_connection(io_context& ios, tracker_manager& man, tracker_request req, std::weak_ptr<request_callback> c)
functions.description: Constructor for an HTTP-based tracker connection. It initializes a tracker_connection instance bound to the given io_context and tracker_manager for performing an HTTP announce/scrape based on the supplied tracker_request, and optionally reports events via the request_callback. Usage: construct the object (typically managed by a shared_ptr via the tracker_manager) and then call start() to initiate the network operation. Internal storage keeps a reference to the io_context; other arguments are used to configure the connection and callbacks. Exact side-effects and validation are based on libtorrent’s tracker subsystem; detailed behavior is not fully documented here.
requirements: ios must be a valid io_context that remains alive for at least the lifetime of the http_tracker_connection instance (the object stores a reference).
man must refer to a valid tracker_manager that remains alive as required by the tracker subsystem (inferred from reference semantics).
req should represent a valid tracker_request (e.g., include a valid tracker URL and relevant fields); exact required fields are library-defined and not specified in this header.
c may be expired; if not expired, it should point to a valid request_callback object that can handle callbacks during the tracker operation.

The constructed object is expected to be managed (kept alive) for the duration of any asynchronous operations started via start(); destruction during active operations can lead to undefined behavior (inferred from async pattern and shared_from_this usage).

functions.name: libtorrent::http_tracker_connection::start
functions.description: Begins the asynchronous HTTP tracker request associated with this connection. Typically performs DNS filtering/connection and issues the HTTP request to the tracker. Intended to be called once after construction to start the announce/scrape workflow. Actual I/O runs on the associated io_context.
requirements: The http_tracker_connection instance must be valid and remain alive for the duration of the asynchronous operation (inferred from async design).

Should be called after successful construction; calling order relative to close() must ensure the connection is not already closed (exact idempotency not documented; behavior if called multiple times is unknown).
Runs on/with the associated io_context; any thread-safety requirements beyond that are not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: libtorrent::http_tracker_connection::close
functions.description: Stops the tracker connection, canceling any in-flight operations and cleaning up resources. Use to abort an ongoing HTTP announce/scrape or to shut down the connection.
requirements: The instance must be valid when close() is called.

functions.description: Forwards to boost::asio::post to schedule a completion handler for execution on an executor or execution context. functions.name: libtorrent::ip_voter::cast_vote

functions.name: libtorrent::link::unlink
functions.signature:
template <class T>
void libtorrent::link::unlink(libtorrent::aux::vector<T*>& list, libtorrent::torrent_list_index_t const link_index)
functions.description: Removes this link’s owning object from the given list in O(1) time by swapping in the last element and shrinking the list. If the link is not in any list (index == -1) the function is a no-op. When the last element is moved, its corresponding link at link_index is updated to the new position.
requirements: The link must either be not in a list (index == -1) or have an index within [0, list.size()). In debug builds, out-of-range indices trigger TORRENT_ASSERT.
The list must be the same aux::vector<T*> that this link was previously inserted into; otherwise the stored index will not be valid.
T must provide a member m_links that is indexable by libtorrent::torrent_list_index_t and yields a libtorrent::link (or compatible) whose index field can be updated.
If this link is present (index >= 0), list.size() must be > 0.
link_index must be a valid index into T::m_links for all elements in list.
This operation may reorder elements (moves the last element into the removed slot); callers must not rely on the original order of list.

functions.name: libtorrent::link::insert
functions.signature:
template <class T>
void libtorrent::link::insert(libtorrent::aux::vector<T*>& list, T* self)
functions.description: Inserts the owning object into the end of the given list and records its index for O(1) membership and removal. If the link is already in a list (index >= 0), the function is a no-op.
requirements: The link must not already be in any list (index == -1). In debug builds, this is enforced by TORRENT_ASSERT.
self must be a valid pointer to the T instance that owns this link.
list must be a valid libtorrent::aux::vector<T*> that is intended to hold pointers to objects whose link fields refer back to this list.
After insertion, the link’s index becomes list.size() - 1.

functions.description: Stops the LSD service and closes associated sockets/timers, preventing further announcements or callbacks. Use to gracefully shut down before destruction.

functions.name: download_queue
functions.description: Returns the queue of blocks we have requested from this peer and are awaiting.

functions.name: request_queue
functions.description: Returns the queue of blocks we have reserved to request from this peer (not yet sent).

functions.name: upload_queue

functions.name: clear_request_queue
functions.description: Clears the outgoing request queue (blocks we intend to request).

functions.name: clear_download_queue
functions.description: Clears the download queue and likely sends cancels as appropriate.

functions.name: download_queue_time
