requirements: extra_bytes must be >= 0 (negative not meaningful).

functions.name: is_interesting
functions.description: Returns whether the peer has pieces we are interested in.

functions.name: is_choked
functions.description: Returns whether we are currently choking this peer (upload).

functions.name: is_peer_interested
functions.description: Returns whether the peer has expressed interest in downloading from us.

functions.name: has_peer_choked
functions.description: Returns whether the remote peer is choking us (upload from their side).

functions.name: choke_this_peer
functions.description: Transitions to choking the peer and sends a choke message if needed.

functions.name: maybe_unchoke_this_peer
functions.description: Evaluates policy and unchokes the peer if eligible, sending an unchoke message.

functions.name: update_interest
functions.description: Schedules/marks interest evaluation. Actual recalculation is coalesced to second_tick/do_update_interest.

functions.name: get_peer_info
functions.description: Fills a peer_info struct with current state and statistics for this connection.
requirements: p must be a valid reference; fields will be overwritten.

functions.name: associated_torrent
functions.description: Returns the torrent this connection is associated with (weak_ptr). May be empty for early incoming connections.

functions.name: associated_info_hash
functions.description: Returns the info-hash associated with this connection (sha1 or truncated sha256 per protocol).

functions.name: statistics
functions.description: Returns statistics object tracking rates and totals for this connection.

functions.name: add_stat
functions.signature: void add_stat(std::int64_t downloaded, std::int64_t uploaded) override;
functions.description: Accumulates payload byte counters for this connection.
requirements: downloaded and uploaded should be >= 0.

functions.name: sent_bytes
functions.description: Accounts bytes sent, split into payload and protocol overhead.
requirements: bytes_payload and bytes_protocol should be >= 0.

functions.name: received_bytes
functions.description: Accounts bytes received, split into payload and protocol overhead.
requirements: bytes_payload and bytes_protocol should be >= 0.

functions.name: trancieve_ip_packet
functions.description: Accounts the size of a transceived IP packet for DHT/UTP TCP/IP stats; name contains a historical misspelling.
requirements: bytes should be >= 0.

functions.name: sent_syn
functions.description: Marks that we sent a TCP SYN; used for TCP handshake stats.

functions.name: received_synack
functions.description: Marks that we received a TCP SYN-ACK; used for TCP handshake stats.

functions.name: second_tick
functions.description: Called once per second by the main loop to update timers, quotas, and periodic logic. tick_interval_ms is the scheduling interval.
requirements: tick_interval_ms should be > 0.

functions.name: get_socket
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the underlying socket type wrapper.

functions.name: get_socket
functions.description: Returns a mutable reference to the underlying socket type wrapper.

functions.name: remote
functions.description: Returns the remote endpoint (may be the proxy endpoint when using a proxy).

functions.name: local_endpoint
functions.description: Returns this connection’s local endpoint (address and port).

functions.name: destination
functions.description: For I2P connections, returns the remote destination address string.
requirements: Available only when TORRENT_USE_I2P is enabled.

functions.name: local_i2p_endpoint
functions.description: For I2P connections, returns the local I2P endpoint string.
requirements: Available only when TORRENT_USE_I2P is enabled.

functions.name: get_bitfield
functions.description: Returns the bitfield of pieces the peer reports having.

functions.name: allowed_fast
functions.description: Returns the peer’s allowed-fast piece list (pieces we may request regardless of choke).

functions.name: suggested_pieces
functions.description: Returns pieces the peer suggested we download from it (incoming suggests).

functions.name: connected_time
functions.description: Returns the time when the connection was established or async_connect initiated.

functions.name: last_received
functions.description: Returns the last time any bytes were received on this connection (relative to connect time).

functions.name: disconnect
functions.signature: void disconnect(error_code const& ec, operation_t op, disconnect_severity_t = peer_connection_interface::normal) override;
functions.description: Disconnects the peer, reporting the specified error and operation context. Severity decides reconnection/backoff behavior.
requirements: ec must be a valid error_code.
op should describe the operation context (e.g., sock_read, sock_write).

functions.name: connect_failed
functions.description: Handles a failure to establish a connection (pre-established state).
requirements: e must be a valid error_code.

functions.name: is_disconnecting
functions.description: Returns true if the connection is in the process of disconnecting.

functions.name: on_connection_complete
functions.description: Called when the async connect attempt completes to finalize setup or handle errors.
requirements: e must be a valid error_code.

functions.name: is_connecting
functions.description: Returns true if the connection attempt is still in progress.

functions.name: received_valid_data
functions.description: Trust-management hook for good data received for a piece index; may adjust endgame/parole/trust status.

functions.name: received_invalid_data
functions.signature: virtual bool received_invalid_data(piece_index_t index, bool single_peer);
functions.description: Trust-management hook for bad data; returns false to avoid disconnecting the peer in special cases.

functions.name: is_outgoing
functions.description: Returns true if we initiated the connection (outgoing).

functions.name: received_listen_port
functions.description: Returns true if we have learned the peer’s incoming listen port (extended handshake).

functions.name: received_listen_port
functions.description: Marks that we learned the peer’s incoming listen port.

functions.name: on_local_network
functions.description: Returns whether the peer is on the local network (inferred from addressing/routing).

functions.name: ignore_unchoke_slots
functions.description: Returns whether this peer should be unchoked even when no unchoke slots are available (policy).

functions.name: failed
functions.description: Returns true if the connection has failed (timed out/closed) and should not be reconnected.

functions.name: desired_queue_size
functions.description: Returns the target number of outstanding requests to keep with this peer (1 if endgame or snubbed).

functions.name: download_payload_rate
functions.description: Returns current measured download payload rate (bytes/s).

functions.name: reset_choke_counters
functions.description: Resets counters used for unchoke/choke decisions across rounds.

functions.name: disconnect_if_redundant
functions.description: Disconnects the peer if neither side is interested (useless connection). Returns true if disconnected.

functions.name: should_log
functions.description: Returns whether peer logging is enabled for the given direction (in/out).
requirements: Available only when TORRENT_DISABLE_LOGGING is undefined.

functions.name: peer_log
functions.signature: void peer_log(peer_log_alert::direction_t direction, char const* event, char const* fmt, ...) const noexcept final;
functions.description: Logs a formatted peer event message for diagnostics. Variadic printf-style formatting.
requirements: Available only when TORRENT_DISABLE_LOGGING is undefined.
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string matching provided arguments.
event and fmt must be valid null-terminated strings.

functions.name: peer_log
functions.signature: void peer_log(peer_log_alert::direction_t direction, char const* event) const noexcept;
functions.description: Logs a peer event without extra formatted details.
requirements: Available only when TORRENT_DISABLE_LOGGING is undefined.
event must be a valid null-terminated string.

functions.name: incoming_keepalive
functions.description: Handles an incoming keep-alive message from the peer.

functions.name: incoming_choke
functions.description: Handles an incoming choke message from the peer.

functions.name: incoming_unchoke
functions.description: Handles an incoming unchoke message from the peer.

functions.name: incoming_interested
functions.description: Handles an incoming interested message from the peer.

functions.name: incoming_not_interested
functions.description: Handles an incoming not-interested message from the peer.

functions.name: incoming_have
functions.description: Handles an incoming have message; marks the peer as having the given piece.

functions.name: incoming_dont_have
functions.description: Handles an incoming don't-have message; marks the peer as not having the given piece.

functions.name: incoming_bitfield
functions.description: Handles an incoming bitfield message from the peer.

functions.name: incoming_request
functions.description: Handles an incoming piece request from the peer.

functions.name: incoming_piece

requirements: data must point to a buffer at least p.length bytes long for the piece data (implied by protocol).

functions.name: incoming_piece_fragment
functions.description: Accounts a fragment of a piece payload being received (for progress tracking).
requirements: bytes should be > 0.

functions.name: start_receive_piece
functions.description: Marks the start of receiving a specific requested block to track progress and timeouts.

functions.name: incoming_cancel
functions.description: Handles an incoming cancel request from the peer.

functions.name: can_disconnect
functions.description: Returns whether it is appropriate to disconnect for the specified error (policy-dependent).
requirements: ec must be a valid error_code.

functions.name: incoming_dht_port
functions.description: Handles an incoming DHT port message (peer's DHT port).
requirements: listen_port should be in [0, 65535].

functions.name: incoming_reject_request
functions.description: Handles an incoming reject-request message from the peer.

functions.name: incoming_have_all
functions.description: Handles an incoming have-all message; marks the peer as having all pieces.

functions.name: incoming_have_none
functions.description: Handles an incoming have-none message; marks the peer as having no pieces.

functions.name: incoming_allowed_fast
functions.description: Handles an incoming allowed-fast piece announcement from the peer.

functions.name: incoming_suggest
functions.description: Handles an incoming suggest message; records the suggested piece.

functions.name: set_has_metadata
functions.description: Sets whether this peer is considered to have the metadata.

functions.name: has_metadata
functions.description: Returns whether this peer is considered to have the metadata.

functions.name: send_choke
functions.description: Enqueues a choke message to the send buffer. Returns true if queued.

functions.name: send_unchoke
functions.description: Enqueues an unchoke message to the send buffer. Returns true if queued.

functions.name: send_interested
functions.description: Enqueues an interested message to the send buffer.

functions.name: send_not_interested
functions.description: Enqueues a not-interested message to the send buffer.

functions.name: send_suggest
functions.description: Enqueues a suggest message for the given piece.

functions.name: send_upload_only
functions.description: Enqueues an extended message indicating upload-only state to the peer.

functions.name: snub_peer
functions.description: Marks the peer as snubbed due to timeouts; limits outstanding requests.

functions.name: reject_piece
functions.description: Rejects any queued requests from this piece and sends reject messages as needed.

functions.name: can_request_time_critical
functions.description: Returns whether time-critical requests can be issued based on current queue/time state.

functions.name: make_time_critical
functions.description: Marks a queued block as time-critical, affecting request ordering. Returns true if it changed state.

functions.name: add_request
functions.signature: bool add_request(piece_block const& b, request_flags_t flags = {});
functions.description: Adds a block request to the outgoing request queue with optional flags (time_critical, busy). Returns true on success.

functions.name: cancel_all_requests
functions.description: Clears both request and download queues and sends cancels for all pending blocks.

functions.name: cancel_request
functions.signature: void cancel_request(piece_block const& b, bool force = false);
functions.description: Removes a specific block from queues and sends cancel if appropriate. If force is true, also frees it in the piece picker immediately.

functions.name: send_block_requests
functions.description: Schedules sending of queued block requests to the peer.

functions.name: send_block_requests_impl
functions.description: Internal implementation to emit request messages for queued blocks.

functions.name: assign_bandwidth
functions.signature: void assign_bandwidth(int channel, int amount) override;
functions.description: Called by the bandwidth manager to assign bandwidth quota to the specified channel (upload/download).
requirements: channel must be upload_channel or download_channel.
amount should be >= 0.

functions.name: check_invariant
functions.description: Debug-only invariant check for internal state (enabled with TORRENT_USE_INVARIANT_CHECKS).
requirements: Only available when TORRENT_USE_INVARIANT_CHECKS is defined.

functions.name: in_handshake
functions.description: Returns true if the connection is still in its handshake phase (protocol-dependent). Pure virtual.

functions.name: downloading_piece_progress
functions.description: Returns progress information for the currently downloading block; default returns invalid piece_index if idle.

functions.name: send_buffer
functions.description: Appends raw bytes to the send buffer.
requirements: buf.size() must fit available memory; may throw on allocation failure.

functions.name: setup_send
functions.description: Initiates or continues async sending of data from the send buffer if conditions permit.

functions.name: append_send_buffer
functions.signature: template <typename Holder> void append_send_buffer(Holder buffer, int size);
functions.description: Appends an owned buffer to the chained send buffer. Asserts single-threaded access.
requirements: Must be called from the session network thread (is_single_thread()).
size must be >= 0 and match the actual size of the Holder buffer.

functions.name: outstanding_bytes
functions.description: Returns the number of response bytes expected from the peer to satisfy outstanding piece requests.

functions.name: send_buffer_size
functions.description: Returns the current number of pending bytes in the send buffer.

functions.name: send_buffer_capacity
functions.description: Returns the allocated capacity of the send buffer.

functions.name: max_out_request_queue
functions.description: Sets the limit on the number of outstanding requests allowed to this peer.
requirements: s must be >= 0 and fits in uint16_t (values above are clamped/adjusted internally).

functions.name: max_out_request_queue
functions.description: Returns the limit on the number of outstanding requests allowed to this peer.

functions.name: last_seen_complete
functions.description: Returns the last time this peer reported seeing a complete copy of the torrent.

functions.name: set_last_seen_complete
functions.description: Sets last-seen-complete timestamp to now - ago seconds.
requirements: ago must be >= 0.

functions.name: uploaded_in_last_round
functions.description: Returns payload bytes uploaded since the previous unchoke round.

functions.name: downloaded_in_last_round
functions.description: Returns payload bytes downloaded since the previous unchoke round.

functions.name: uploaded_since_unchoked
functions.description: Returns payload bytes uploaded since this peer was last unchoked.

functions.name: time_of_last_unchoke
functions.description: Returns the timestamp when we last unchoked this peer.

functions.name: on_disk
functions.description: Called when disk write buffer is drained; resumes downloading payload as applicable.

functions.name: num_reading_bytes
functions.description: Returns number of bytes currently being read from disk that will be added to the send buffer.

functions.name: setup_receive
functions.description: Initiates or continues async reading from the socket into the receive buffer.

functions.name: self
functions.description: Returns a shared_ptr to this connection. Asserts that the object is fully constructed and in-use.
requirements: Must not be called from constructor (m_in_constructor must be false).
Object must be managed by shared_from_this (enable_shared_from_this).

functions.name: stats_counters
functions.description: Returns a reference to the session-wide counters object.

functions.name: get_priority
functions.description: Returns the I/O priority for the specified bandwidth channel (upload/download).
requirements: channel must be upload_channel or download_channel.

functions.name: get_specific_peer_info
functions.description: Derived-class hook to fill protocol-specific peer_info fields.
requirements: p must be a valid reference; fields may be overwritten.

functions.name: write_choke
functions.description: Derived-class method to serialize a choke message into the send buffer.

functions.name: write_unchoke
functions.description: Derived-class method to serialize an unchoke message into the send buffer.

functions.name: write_interested
functions.description: Derived-class method to serialize an interested message into the send buffer.

functions.name: write_not_interested
functions.description: Derived-class method to serialize a not-interested message into the send buffer.

functions.name: write_request
functions.description: Derived-class method to serialize a request message for the specified block.
requirements: r must contain a valid piece, offset and length per protocol.

functions.name: write_cancel
functions.description: Derived-class method to serialize a cancel message for the specified block.
requirements: r must match a previously requested block to be meaningful.

functions.name: write_have
functions.description: Derived-class method to serialize a have message for the given piece.

functions.name: write_dont_have
functions.description: Derived-class method to serialize a don't-have message for the given piece.

functions.name: write_keepalive
functions.description: Derived-class method to serialize a keep-alive message.

functions.name: write_piece
functions.signature: virtual void write_piece(peer_request const& r, disk_buffer_holder buffer) = 0;
functions.description: Derived-class method to serialize a piece payload message backed by the provided disk buffer.
requirements: buffer must contain at least r.length bytes of payload starting at r.begin offset.
r must be valid per protocol.

functions.name: write_suggest
functions.description: Derived-class method to serialize a suggest message for the given piece.

functions.name: write_bitfield
functions.description: Derived-class method to serialize our bitfield to the peer.

functions.name: write_reject_request
functions.description: Derived-class method to serialize a reject-request message for the specified block.

functions.name: write_allow_fast
functions.description: Derived-class method to serialize an allow-fast message for the given piece.

functions.name: write_upload_only
functions.description: Derived-class method to serialize an upload-only state message.

functions.name: on_connected
functions.description: Derived-class hook called when the TCP/transport connection is established and ready.

functions.name: on_tick
functions.description: Derived-class optional hook called from second_tick for protocol-specific periodic tasks.

functions.name: on_receive
functions.signature: virtual void on_receive(error_code const& error, std::size_t bytes_transferred) = 0;
functions.description: Derived-class completion handler for async reads from the socket.
requirements: error must be a valid error_code.
bytes_transferred is the number of bytes delivered in this completion.

functions.name: on_sent
functions.signature: virtual void on_sent(error_code const& error, std::size_t bytes_transferred) = 0;
functions.description: Derived-class completion handler for async writes to the socket.
requirements: error must be a valid error_code.
bytes_transferred is the number of bytes delivered in this completion.

functions.name: send_piece_suggestions
functions.description: Sends up to num suggest messages based on internal suggestion queue and policy.
requirements: num should be >= 0.

functions.name: hit_send_barrier
functions.description: Optional hook to split send buffer at a barrier. Returns a tuple of barrier offset and extra buffers to prepend/append. Default returns INT_MAX and empty span.

functions.name: attach_to_torrent
functions.description: Associates this peer connection with the torrent identified by the given info-hash (for incoming connections).

functions.name: validate_piece_request
functions.description: Validates that an incoming piece request is well-formed and within torrent bounds.

functions.name: update_desired_queue_size
functions.description: Recalculates the desired number of outstanding requests to keep based on current transfer state.

functions.name: set_send_barrier
functions.description: Sets a barrier to stop sending after bytes bytes (or INT_MAX for no barrier). Asserts bytes <= current send buffer size unless INT_MAX.
requirements: bytes must be INT_MAX or 0 <= bytes <= send_buffer_size().

functions.name: get_send_barrier
functions.description: Returns the current send barrier limit (INT_MAX means no barrier).

functions.name: timeout
functions.description: Returns the connection timeout in seconds used for idle/read/write timeouts. Overridable by derived classes.

functions.name: get_context
functions.description: Returns the io_context backing this connection for scheduling async operations.

functions.name: on_send_data
functions.signature: void on_send_data(error_code const& error, std::size_t bytes_transferred);
functions.description: Internal completion handler for a socket async send; updates quotas and state, then delegates to on_sent.
requirements: error must be a valid error_code.
bytes_transferred must be the number of bytes reported by the OS.

functions.name: on_receive_data
functions.signature: void on_receive_data(error_code const& error, std::size_t bytes_transferred);
functions.description: Internal completion handler for socket async receive; updates accounting and calls on_receive.
requirements: error must be a valid error_code.
bytes_transferred must be the number of bytes reported by the OS.

functions.name: account_received_bytes
functions.description: Accounts received bytes into stats and timers.
requirements: bytes_transferred should be >= 0.

functions.name: do_update_interest
functions.description: Performs the actual (coalesced) recalculation of interest for this peer.

functions.name: fill_send_buffer
functions.description: Refills the send buffer with payload/protocol data from queues and disk reads as needed.

functions.name: on_disk_read_complete
functions.signature: void on_disk_read_complete(disk_buffer_holder buffer, storage_error const& error, peer_request const&, time_point issue_time);
functions.description: Completion callback for disk read operations, to push read payload into send buffer or handle errors.

functions.name: on_disk_write_complete
functions.signature: void on_disk_write_complete(storage_error const& error, peer_request const&, std::shared_ptr<torrent>);
functions.description: Completion callback for disk write operations to update state and possibly issue further reads/writes.

functions.name: on_seed_mode_hashed

functions.description: Completion callback when a piece was hashed in seed-mode pre-read; decides whether to serve piece data.

functions.name: request_timeout
functions.description: Returns the request timeout used for outstanding block requests, factoring in observed RTTs.

functions.name: check_graceful_pause
functions.description: Checks whether the torrent/session is gracefully pausing and adapts behavior (e.g., stop requesting).

functions.name: wanted_transfer
functions.description: Returns how many bytes this connection wants to transfer on the specified channel (for bandwidth allocator).
requirements: channel must be upload_channel or download_channel.

functions.name: request_bandwidth
functions.description: Asks the bandwidth manager for quota on the specified channel, optionally specifying a desired byte count.
requirements: channel must be upload_channel or download_channel.
bytes must be >= 0.

functions.name: cork::cork
functions.description: RAII helper to temporarily cork sending by marking the upload channel as network-busy to batch writes until destruction.
requirements: p must outlive the cork object.
Must be created on the same thread manipulating the peer_connection.

functions.name: cork::~cork
functions.description: Releases the cork: clears the network-busy flag and calls setup_send(), handling exceptions by disconnecting with appropriate error.
requirements: Must be destroyed on the same thread; destructor must not throw (it catches and converts to disconnect).

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_connection_handle::peer_connection_handle
functions.description: Constructs a lightweight handle wrapping a weak reference to an internal peer_connection. Intended for plugin/extension code to interact with a peer without owning it.
requirements: impl may refer to an already-expired peer_connection; callers should be prepared for subsequent operations to fail or return default/invalid results if the underlying object has expired.

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_connection_handle::type
functions.description: Returns the connection type for the underlying peer_connection (e.g. BitTorrent, web seed, etc.).
requirements: The underlying peer_connection must still exist; otherwise the result may be unspecified or a default value (implementation-defined).

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_connection_handle::add_extension
functions.description: Adds a peer_plugin instance to the connection, enabling custom behavior or protocol extensions for this peer.
requirements: The shared_ptr must point to a valid peer_plugin instance.
The underlying peer_connection must exist; otherwise the call has no effect or fails silently (implementation-defined).

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_connection_handle::find_plugin
functions.description: Finds a previously added peer_plugin matching the provided type identifier and returns a pointer to it, or nullptr if not found.
requirements: type must identify the plugin (matching whatever naming/type convention the plugin uses).
Returned pointer, if non-null, remains valid only as long as the underlying peer_connection and plugin remain alive.

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_connection_handle::is_seed
functions.description: Reports whether the remote peer is known to have all pieces (i.e. is a seed).

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_connection_handle::upload_only
functions.description: Returns true if the remote peer is flagged as upload-only (it will not download).

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_connection_handle::pid
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the peer's PeerID.
requirements: The returned reference is only valid while the underlying peer_connection remains alive.

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_connection_handle::has_piece
functions.description: Returns true if the peer is known to have the specified piece index.
requirements: i must refer to a valid piece within the associated torrent's piece range.

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_connection_handle::is_interesting
functions.description: Indicates whether this peer is currently considered interesting (i.e. we want data from it).

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_connection_handle::is_choked
functions.description: Returns true if we are currently choking this peer (not uploading to it).

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_connection_handle::is_peer_interested
functions.description: Returns true if the peer has expressed interest in downloading from us.

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_connection_handle::has_peer_choked
functions.description: Returns true if the peer is currently choking us (not uploading to us).

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_connection_handle::choke_this_peer
functions.description: Actively choke this peer, preventing further uploads to it until unchoked.
requirements: Underlying peer_connection must exist to have any effect.

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_connection_handle::maybe_unchoke_this_peer
functions.description: Attempt to unchoke the peer if policy and slot availability allow it.
requirements: Effect depends on current choking policy and available unchoke slots of the session/torrent.

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_connection_handle::get_peer_info
functions.description: Populates the provided peer_info structure with the current state and statistics of this connection.
requirements: p must be a valid reference to a peer_info object that the caller owns and can be written to.

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_connection_handle::associated_torrent
functions.description: Returns a handle to the torrent associated with this peer connection.
requirements: Returned torrent_handle may be invalid if the torrent has been removed or the peer is not associated.

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_connection_handle::remote
functions.description: Returns the remote network endpoint (IP and port) of the peer.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid only while the underlying peer_connection exists.
If the socket/connection is not yet established, the value may be unspecified.

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_connection_handle::local_endpoint
functions.description: Returns the local network endpoint used for this connection.
requirements: If the socket is not bound/connected yet, the result may be unspecified or default constructed (implementation-defined).

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_connection_handle::disconnect
functions.signature: void libtorrent::peer_connection_handle::disconnect(error_code const& ec, operation_t op, disconnect_severity_t = peer_connection_interface::normal)
functions.description: Disconnects the peer with the specified error condition and operation context, optionally specifying severity for alerting/logging.
requirements: ec should contain the reason for disconnect (may be success or an error).
op must specify the context/operation causing the disconnect.
May be a no-op if the underlying peer_connection no longer exists.

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_connection_handle::is_disconnecting
functions.description: Returns true if the connection is in the process of disconnecting or already disconnected.

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_connection_handle::is_connecting
functions.description: Returns true if the connection is in the process of establishing (e.g. handshake/connecting).

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_connection_handle::is_outgoing

functions.name: libtorrent::piece_picker::pick_pieces
functions.signature: picker_flags_t libtorrent::piece_picker::pick_pieces(typed_bitfield<piece_index_t> const& pieces, std::vector<piece_block>& interesting_blocks, int num_blocks, int prefer_contiguous_blocks, torrent_peer* peer, picker_options_t options, std::vector<piece_index_t> const& suggested_pieces, int num_peers, counters& pc) const;
functions.description: Selects up to num_blocks piece blocks to request from a peer, honoring availability, priorities, partials, sequencing, and options. Writes chosen blocks to interesting_blocks and returns flags about the pick operation.
requirements: pieces must represent the remote peer's have-set.

options controls strategies (e.g., rarest_first, sequential).

pc is an out-parameter for internal counters/statistics.

functions.name: libtorrent::posix_disk_io_constructor
functions.signature: std::unique_ptr<libtorrent::disk_interface> libtorrent::posix_disk_io_constructor(libtorrent::io_context& ios, libtorrent::settings_interface const& settings, libtorrent::counters& cnt)
functions.description: Factory function that constructs a POSIX-style disk I/O backend implementing libtorrent's disk_interface. The backend is intended for platforms lacking a 64-bit virtual address space or memory-mapped file support and is implemented using portable C file APIs. It is single-threaded. Usage: call this to obtain a disk_interface instance wired to the provided io_context, settings, and counters objects; manage the returned std::unique_ptr to control the backend’s lifetime. Details about error behavior and ownership beyond the references are not documented in this header and are inferred where noted.
requirements: ios must be a valid libtorrent::io_context reference at the time of the call (inferred from parameter type).
settings must be a valid libtorrent::settings_interface object; it is passed by const reference (inferred from parameter type).
cnt must be a valid libtorrent::counters object; it is passed by non-const reference and may be modified by the disk backend (inferred from parameter type).
The function returns a std::unique_ptr<disk_interface>. The caller owns and controls the lifetime of the returned object via the unique_ptr (inferred from return type).
The backend is single-threaded; do not assume it performs internal multithreading (stated in comments).

Lifetimes of ios, settings, and cnt are likely required to outlive the returned disk_interface if it retains references to them; this is not explicitly documented but is a common pattern for factory functions taking references (inferred, unknown exact guarantees).

template <class Mutable_Buffers, class Handler>
void libtorrent::proxy_base::async_read_some(Mutable_Buffers const& buffers, Handler handler)

functions.name: libtorrent::session_handle::dht_put_item

functions.name: libtorrent::session_handle::dht_get_peers

functions.name: libtorrent::session_handle::dht_announce

functions.description: Announces to the DHT that we are seeding/downloading a torrent identified by info_hash, advertising the specified port or the source port if port==0. For advanced/explicit announcements; libtorrent announces eligible torrents automatically.
requirements: If port is 0, the DHT message source port is used.
flags are from dht::announce_flags_t.

functions.name: libtorrent::session_handle::dht_live_nodes
functions.description: Requests a list of live DHT nodes near nid. Results are posted as dht_live_nodes_alert and are always posted regardless of alert mask.
requirements: Caller must process alerts to receive the result.

functions.name: libtorrent::session_handle::dht_sample_infohashes
functions.signature: void libtorrent::session_handle::dht_sample_infohashes(udp::endpoint const& ep, sha1_hash const& target)
functions.description: Queries the specified DHT node for a sample of the info-hashes it stores. target aids in iterative traversals. Result posted as dht_sample_infohashes_alert.
requirements: Caller must process alerts to receive the result.
ep must be a reachable DHT node endpoint.

functions.name: libtorrent::session_handle::dht_direct_request
functions.signature: void libtorrent::session_handle::dht_direct_request(udp::endpoint const& ep, entry const& e, client_data_t userdata = {})
functions.description: Sends an arbitrary DHT request to ep, intended for plugins. Response or timeout is reported via dht_direct_response_alert with the provided userdata. Always posted regardless of alert mask.
requirements: Caller must process alerts to receive the response.
Used for advanced/plugin use; ensure message conforms to DHT RPC expectations.

functions.name: libtorrent::session_handle::is_listening

requirements: If false, adjust settings_pack::listen_interfaces and retry.

functions.name: libtorrent::session_handle::set_peer_class_filter
functions.description: Sets the peer-class IP filter mapping IP ranges to peer class bitmasks (lower 32 classes). Affects new connections only; existing peers are unaffected.
requirements: Only peer classes 0-31 can be assigned via this filter (bitmask width).
Does not remove classes from existing peers; only adds on connect.

functions.name: libtorrent::session_handle::get_peer_class_filter
functions.description: Returns the current peer-class IP filter.
requirements: None.

functions.name: libtorrent::session_handle::set_peer_class_type_filter
functions.description: Sets the peer-class type filter, controlling automatic class assignment/removal based on socket type.
requirements: Rules are applied after peer-class IP filter removes and before it adds classes as documented order.

functions.name: libtorrent::session_handle::get_peer_class_type_filter
functions.description: Returns the current peer-class type filter.
requirements: None.

functions.name: libtorrent::session_handle::create_peer_class
functions.description: Creates a new peer class with the specified name and returns its identifier. Identifiers are assigned from low to high values.
requirements: Create classes early if they must fit within the lower 32 IDs for use with set_peer_class_filter().
name is used for identification; multiple classes can share the same name.

functions.name: libtorrent::session_handle::delete_peer_class
functions.description: Dereferences and eventually deletes the specified peer class when no longer in use by peers or torrents. Call at most once per created class.
requirements: Must only be called once per class; multiple calls lead to memory corruption (per docs).
Class will be removed only after last reference is released.

functions.name: libtorrent::session_handle::get_peer_class
functions.description: Returns information/configuration for the specified peer class.

functions.name: libtorrent::session_handle::set_peer_class
functions.description: Updates the configuration of the specified peer class with the provided peer_class_info.
requirements: cid must refer to an existing peer class.
All fields in pci are applied; there is no partial update.

functions.name: libtorrent::session_handle::use_interfaces
functions.description: [Deprecated in 0.16, ABI 1] Sets interfaces for outgoing connections. Replaced by session settings.
requirements: Available only when TORRENT_ABI_VERSION == 1.

functions.signature: void libtorrent::session_handle::listen_on(std::pair<int, int> const& port_range, error_code& ec, const char* net_interface = nullptr, int flags = 0)
functions.description: [Deprecated, ABI 1] Rebinds the listen socket to a new interface and port range. On failure returns false in older API; this overload reports via ec and is void in header comment context. Prefer settings_pack::listen_interfaces.
requirements: Available only when TORRENT_ABI_VERSION == 1.

ec is set on failure; caller should check generated alerts for details.
flags are deprecated; listen_reuse_address always on since 0.16.2.

functions.name: libtorrent::session_handle::remove_torrent
functions.description: Removes a torrent: closes peers, announces stopped to trackers, and erases it from the session. Optionally deletes files (delete_files) or partfile (delete_partfile). Non-blocking; completion reported via torrent_removed_alert and optionally torrent_deleted_alert.
requirements: The provided handle should refer to a torrent in the session; otherwise it’s a no-op.

When deleting files, ensure you intend to remove all data on disk.

functions.name: libtorrent::session_handle::apply_settings
functions.description: Asynchronously applies the provided settings_pack to the session.
requirements: Operation is asynchronous; changes take effect later on the libtorrent main thread.

functions.name: libtorrent::session_handle::get_settings

requirements: Returned copy reflects settings at call time; concurrent changes may occur later.

functions.name: libtorrent::session_handle::get_pe_settings

functions.name: libtorrent::session_handle::i2p_proxy

requirements: Available only when TORRENT_ABI_VERSION == 1.

functions.name: libtorrent::session_handle::pop_alerts
functions.description: Retrieves and pops pending alerts from the session into alerts. The session owns the alerts; they remain valid until the next pop_alerts() call.
requirements: alerts must be non-null.
Do not delete alert pointers; ownership remains with the session.
Safe to call from multiple threads, but callers must ensure alerts aren’t accessed after another thread calls pop_alerts().

functions.name: libtorrent::session_handle::wait_for_alert
functions.description: Blocks up to max_wait for an alert to become available and returns the head of the alert queue without popping it. Returns nullptr on timeout.
requirements: The returned alert remains valid until pop_alerts() is called twice after it is returned (first to pop it, second to free it).
Caller should subsequently call pop_alerts() to consume alerts.

functions.name: libtorrent::session_handle::set_alert_notify
functions.description: Registers a callback invoked when the alert queue transitions from empty to having one alert. Intended to wake up an external event loop to call pop_alerts(). The callback should be non-blocking and lightweight.
requirements: Callback may be called from within libtorrent (main/user thread); it must not block and should not perform expensive work.
Fetching alerts must not be done inside the callback; just notify the main thread.

functions.name: libtorrent::session_handle::set_alert_queue_size_limit
functions.description: [Deprecated, ABI 1] Sets and returns the alert queue size limit.
requirements: Available only when TORRENT_ABI_VERSION == 1.

functions.description: [Deprecated, ABI 1] Sets the alert category mask controlling which alerts are posted.
requirements: Available only when TORRENT_ABI_VERSION == 1.
m is a bitmask of categories (see category_t).

functions.name: libtorrent::session_handle::get_alert_mask

functions.name: libtorrent::session_handle::add_port_mapping
functions.signature: std::vector<port_mapping_t> libtorrent::session_handle::add_port_mapping(portmap_protocol t, int external_port, int local_port)
functions.description: Adds port mappings on all listen sockets via enabled UPnP/NAT-PMP services. Returns handles for each mapping created.
requirements: Requires UPnP and/or NAT-PMP to be enabled for effect.
external_port and local_port must be valid port numbers (1..65535).

functions.name: libtorrent::session_handle::delete_port_mapping

requirements: Call when detecting IP/interface changes or after adjusting system networking.
If options includes reopen_map_ports, requires NAT-PMP/UPnP to be enabled to take effect.

functions.name: libtorrent::session_handle::native_handle
functions.description: Returns an internal implementation pointer for plugin/advanced use. API is not stable and should be used sparingly.
requirements: For plugin/internal use only; avoid relying on stability across versions.

functions.name: libtorrent::session_params::session_params
functions.description: Constructs a session_params using the provided settings_pack rvalue. According to the header comment, this constructor can be used to start with the default plugins (ut_metadata, ut_pex, smart_ban) and to set initial session settings.
requirements: sp must hold valid libtorrent session settings. Other constraints unknown.

functions.name: libtorrent::session_params::~session_params
functions.description: Destroys the session_params object and releases its resources. Marked hidden in the header.
requirements: No special requirements are documented.

functions.name: libtorrent::session_params::operator=
functions.description: Copy-assigns from another session_params to this object. The ref-qualifier requires the left-hand side to be an lvalue.
requirements: This operator can only be invoked on an lvalue (due to the '&' ref-qualifier).
Source object must be a valid libtorrent::session_params. Other constraints unknown.

functions.name: libtorrent::read_session_params
functions.signature: libtorrent::session_params libtorrent::read_session_params(libtorrent::bdecode_node const& e, libtorrent::save_state_flags_t flags = libtorrent::save_state_flags_t::all());
functions.description: Deserializes a session_params from a bdecoded node. Use flags to load only selected aspects of the session state.
requirements: e must represent a valid bencoded structure for session_params (typically produced by write_session_params).
flags must be a valid combination of libtorrent::save_state_flags_t bits.
Error handling and exceptions are not documented in this header; behavior on invalid input is unknown.

functions.name: libtorrent::write_session_params
functions.signature: libtorrent::entry libtorrent::write_session_params(libtorrent::session_params const& sp, libtorrent::save_state_flags_t flags = libtorrent::save_state_flags_t::all());
functions.description: Serializes a session_params into a bencoded entry object. Use flags to save only selected aspects of the session state. Torrents in the session are not part of session_params and must be handled separately.
requirements: sp must be a valid libtorrent::session_params instance.
flags must be a valid combination of libtorrent::save_state_flags_t bits.

functions.name: libtorrent::write_session_params_buf
functions.signature: std::vector<char> libtorrent::write_session_params_buf(libtorrent::session_params const& sp, libtorrent::save_state_flags_t flags = libtorrent::save_state_flags_t::all());
functions.description: Serializes a session_params into a buffer of bencoded data. Use flags to save only selected aspects of the session state. Torrents in the session are not part of session_params and must be handled separately.
requirements: sp must be a valid libtorrent::session_params instance.
flags must be a valid combination of libtorrent::save_state_flags_t bits.

functions.name: libtorrent::session_stats_metrics
functions.description: Returns the full list of statistics metrics exposed by libtorrent’s statistics API. Each metric contains its name, value_index (position in the session_stats_alert values array), and type (counter or gauge). Typical usage: call this once to enumerate metrics and map names to indices before sampling stats via post_session_stats().
requirements: None beyond standard C++ usage; the function takes no parameters and returns a vector of metrics.
Callers should not assume stability of indices across library versions; use names to resolve indices at runtime if portability across versions is required.
Use the returned value_index with the values array from session_stats_alert (produced after calling post_session_stats()).

functions.name: libtorrent::find_metric_idx
functions.description: Looks up a statistics metric by name and returns its index into the session_stats_alert values array; returns -1 if the metric name is not found. Typical usage: pass a metric name (e.g., "peer.incoming_requests") and use the returned index to read the corresponding element from the values array in session_stats_alert sampled via post_session_stats().
requirements: name must reference a valid, non-empty metric name to obtain a non-negative index; otherwise the function returns -1 (caller must handle -1).
Only use a non-negative returned index to access the corresponding element in the session_stats_alert values array obtained after calling post_session_stats().
The input is a libtorrent::string_view; the referenced memory must remain valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: libtorrent::load_pack_from_dict

requirements: context must be a valid, non-null pointer to a libtorrent::sha1_ctx that has been initialized with SHA1_init and not yet finalized (inferred).

functions.name: libtorrent::SHA1_final

The exact post-conditions on the context are not documented, but typical SHA-1 APIs make further updates invalid until reinitialized.
requirements: digest must be a valid, non-null pointer to at least 20 bytes of writable memory to receive the SHA-1 digest (inferred from SHA-1 output size).
context must be a valid, non-null pointer to a libtorrent::sha1_ctx previously initialized with SHA1_init and not yet finalized (inferred).

requirements: digest must point to a writable buffer of at least 32 bytes to receive the SHA-256 result (inferred from SHA-256 output size).

functions.name: libtorrent::endpoint_to_bytes
functions.description: Serializes a UDP endpoint (IP address and port) to its raw binary bytes and returns them in a std::string. For IPv4 the result is 6 bytes (4 for IP, 2 for port); for IPv6 the result is 18 bytes (16 for IP, 2 for port). Suitable for compact storage or bencoded representations as used by libtorrent (inferred from aux helpers).
requirements: ep must be a valid, initialized libtorrent::udp::endpoint.
The returned string contains binary data (may include null bytes); do not treat it as text.
Port is serialized as a 16-bit value in network byte order; IP bytes are the raw address bytes (inferred from aux::write_endpoint/read_*).

functions.name: libtorrent::hash_address
functions.description: Computes a SHA-1 hash derived from the given IP address’s raw bytes and returns it as libtorrent::sha1_hash. Useful for bucketing, anonymized identifiers, or DHT/peer-related logic. Exact salt or additional context (if any) is not documented; assumed to hash the address bytes only.
requirements: ip must be a valid, initialized libtorrent::address.
The resulting hash is deterministic for the same input address; cryptographic security properties beyond SHA-1’s standard behavior are not guaranteed.
Details of any endianness or normalization prior to hashing are not documented; treat it as a hash of the raw address bytes.

functions.name: libtorrent::socket_type_name
functions.description: Return a short, human-readable name for a given libtorrent::socket_type_t value. Intended for diagnostics, logging, and UI display where a textual socket type is useful. The returned pointer refers to a C-style, null-terminated string that should be treated as read-only. Details about exact strings and coverage of all enum values are not specified in this header.
requirements: Argument 'type' must be a valid libtorrent::socket_type_t enumerator (e.g., tcp, socks5, http, utp, i2p, tcp_ssl, socks5_ssl, http_ssl, utp_ssl).
The returned char const* must be treated as read-only; do not modify or free it.
The lifetime/ownership of the returned string is not specified; assume it is static or otherwise managed by the library and should not be deallocated by the caller.
Behavior for values not represented in libtorrent::socket_type_t is unspecified.
In builds with TORRENT_ABI_VERSION <= 2, the deprecated enum value 'udp' aliases 'utp'; callers should not rely on receiving a distinct name for 'udp'.

functions.name: libtorrent::socks_category
functions.description: Returns the error_category instance for SOCKS-related errors in libtorrent. Use this category to interpret error_code values originating from the SOCKS5/SOCKS4 logic.
requirements: Thread-safety and lifetime of the returned category follow typical error_category singleton semantics (unknown if thread-safe init is guaranteed; assumed standard).
No inputs or preconditions.

functions.name: libtorrent::get_socks_category
functions.description: Deprecated ABI-compat alias for socks_category(). Returns the same SOCKS error_category. Only available when TORRENT_ABI_VERSION == 1.
requirements: Availability is conditional: only defined when TORRENT_ABI_VERSION == 1.
Callers should prefer libtorrent::socks_category().

functions.name: libtorrent::socks5_stream::socks5_stream
functions.description: Move constructor for socks5_stream. Transfers ownership of the underlying proxy socket/stream state from another socks5_stream.
requirements: The source instance must be a valid rvalue socks5_stream.
After the move, the source object is left in a valid but unspecified state.

functions.name: libtorrent::socks5_stream::set_version
functions.description: Sets the SOCKS protocol version to use for subsequent connections (supported: 5 or 4).
requirements: Only values 4 or 5 are supported. Other values will cause connections to fail with unsupported_version.

functions.name: libtorrent::socks5_stream::set_command
functions.description: Selects which SOCKS command to issue during connect. Supported commands are socks5_connect and socks5_udp_associate.
requirements: c must be either socks5_connect (1) or socks5_udp_associate (3). Passing any other value violates an internal assertion.

functions.name: libtorrent::socks5_stream::set_username
functions.signature: void libtorrent::socks5_stream::set_username(std::string const& user, std::string const& password);
functions.description: Sets optional username and password to use for SOCKS5 username/password authentication during the handshake.
requirements: For SOCKS5 username/password authentication, both username and password must be shorter than 256 bytes (fits uint8 length field).
Empty user/password disables username/password auth; no authentication will be attempted if empty.

functions.name: libtorrent::socks5_stream::set_dst_name
functions.description: Specifies a DNS host name for the destination, to be sent to a SOCKS5 proxy using the domain-name address type. Useful when the target address is not known or when name resolution is delegated to the proxy.
requirements: host must be a hostname, not an IP address literal (internal assertion rejects IP strings).
If host length exceeds 255 bytes, it will be truncated to 255 to conform to SOCKS5 domain-name length limits.
When using INADDR_ANY in the endpoint for async_connect, SOCKS version must be 5 and a non-empty destination name must be set prior to connecting (enforced by assertion in async_connect).

functions.name: libtorrent::socks5_stream::close
functions.description: Closes the underlying proxied stream, clearing any stored destination name and reporting errors through the provided error_code reference.
requirements: ec is used for error reporting; caller must inspect ec to detect failures.
Safe to call multiple times; subsequent calls may report an error depending on proxy_base implementation (behavior unspecified in this header).

functions.name: libtorrent::socks5_stream::async_connect
functions.signature:
template <class Handler>
void libtorrent::socks5_stream::async_connect(endpoint_type const& endpoint, Handler handler);
functions.description: Asynchronously establishes a connection through the configured SOCKS proxy to the specified endpoint (or to a destination name if set for SOCKS5). Performs proxy name resolution, TCP connect to the proxy, SOCKS handshake (including optional username/password), and issues the configured SOCKS command (connect or UDP associate). The completion handler is invoked with a single parameter: boost::system::error_code indicating success or failure.
requirements: A valid proxy hostname and port must be configured in the socks5_stream (via proxy_base members) before calling; the function resolves m_hostname and m_port (inferred from code).
endpoint.address() must not be the 'any' address, unless both conditions hold: (a) SOCKS version is 5, and (b) a non-empty destination name has been set via set_dst_name().
If set_version(4) is used, endpoint must be IPv4; IPv6 is not supported by SOCKS4.
If username/password authentication is required by the proxy, set_username() must be called with credentials whose lengths are each < 256 bytes.
Handler must be MoveConstructible and invocable with a single argument of type boost::system::error_code (i.e., signature equivalent to void handler(boost::system::error_code const&)).

async_connect must not be called after the stream has been closed; the underlying socket must be in a state where async_connect on it is valid (inferred from proxy_base behavior; exact state requirements unknown).

functions.name: libtorrent::span::span
functions.description: Default-constructs an empty span with null data() and size 0. Useful as a sentinel or to defer binding to storage until later.
requirements: No requirements; result has data() == nullptr and size() == 0.

functions.name: libtorrent::span::operator=

libtorrent::span<T>& libtorrent::span<T>::operator=(libtorrent::span<U> const& rhs) noexcept
functions.description: Assigns this span from another span<U> when element types are cv-compatible. Copies pointer and length; does not copy elements or manage ownership.
requirements: U must be cv-compatible with T per libtorrent::aux::compatible_type.
The source span rhs must remain valid for as long as this span is used after assignment.

functions.name: libtorrent::span::front

T& libtorrent::span<T>::front() const noexcept

functions.name: libtorrent::span::back

T& libtorrent::span<T>::back() const noexcept

template <typename T>
libtorrent::span<T> libtorrent::span<T>::first(difference_type const n) const
functions.description: Returns a subspan of the first n elements.

functions.name: libtorrent::span::last
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
libtorrent::span<T> libtorrent::span<T>::last(difference_type const n) const
functions.description: Returns a subspan of the last n elements.

functions.name: libtorrent::span::subspan
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
libtorrent::span<T> libtorrent::span<T>::subspan(index_type const offset) const

functions.name: libtorrent::span::operator[]
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
T& libtorrent::span<T>::operator[](index_type const idx) const
functions.description: Returns a reference to the element at position idx without bounds checking beyond debug assertions.
requirements: idx must be >= 0 and < size() (both asserted).
Underlying storage must remain valid.

functions.name: libtorrent::operator==
functions.signature:
template <class T, class U>
bool libtorrent::operator==(libtorrent::span<T> const& lhs, libtorrent::span<U> const& rhs)
functions.description: Compares two spans for equality. Returns true if sizes are equal and elements compare equal. If the data pointers are identical, returns true immediately when sizes match.
requirements: T and U must be comparable with operator== via std::equal on their ranges.
Both spans must reference valid, comparable sequences of at least size() elements.

functions.name: libtorrent::operator!=
functions.signature:
template <class T, class U>
bool libtorrent::operator!=(libtorrent::span<T> const& lhs, libtorrent::span<U> const& rhs)
functions.description: Returns the negation of operator==. True if sizes differ or any element differs. If data pointers differ and std::equal reports inequality, returns true.
requirements: T and U must be comparable with operator== via std::equal on their ranges.
Both spans must reference valid, comparable sequences of at least size() elements.

functions.name: libtorrent::ssl::get_handle
functions.description: Returns the native SSL/TLS context handle for the given libtorrent::ssl::context. Under OpenSSL this is SSL_CTX*, under GnuTLS it is a pointer to the wrapper context. Use when integrating with native SSL APIs or when lower-level configuration is required.
requirements: The input context reference must refer to a valid, initialized SSL/TLS context object.
The returned handle is only valid as long as the referenced context remains alive.

functions.name: libtorrent::ssl::get_handle
functions.description: Returns the native SSL/TLS stream handle for the given libtorrent::ssl::stream<T>. Under OpenSSL this is SSL*, under GnuTLS it is a pointer to the wrapper stream. Useful for native API interop or fine-grained stream control.
requirements: The input stream reference must refer to a valid, initialized SSL/TLS stream object.
The returned handle is only valid as long as the referenced stream remains alive.

functions.name: libtorrent::ssl::get_context_handle
functions.description: Returns the native SSL/TLS context handle currently associated with the given SSL/TLS stream. Under OpenSSL this resolves to the SSL_CTX* tied to the SSL*, under GnuTLS it returns a pointer to the stream’s context.
requirements: The input stream reference must refer to a valid SSL/TLS stream.
The returned context handle remains valid only while the underlying context object remains alive and associated with the stream.

functions.name: libtorrent::ssl::set_trust_certificate
functions.signature: void libtorrent::ssl::set_trust_certificate(libtorrent::ssl::native_context_type nc, libtorrent::string_view pem, libtorrent::ssl::error_code& ec)
functions.description: Configures the trust store of the given native SSL/TLS context with one or more certificates provided as a PEM-encoded blob. Intended to install CA certificates or pin certificates for peer verification. Errors are reported via ec.
requirements: nc must be a valid native SSL/TLS context handle compatible with the current TLS backend (e.g., OpenSSL SSL_CTX*).
pem must contain valid PEM-encoded certificate data (one or more certificates).
ec is set on failure; callers should check ec after the call.
The context referenced by nc must outlive the call and any subsequent use of the installed trust material.

functions.name: libtorrent::ssl::set_server_name_callback
functions.signature: void libtorrent::ssl::set_server_name_callback(libtorrent::ssl::context_handle_type c, libtorrent::ssl::server_name_callback_type cb, void* arg, libtorrent::ssl::error_code& ec)
functions.description: Installs a Server Name Indication (SNI) callback on the given SSL/TLS context. The callback is invoked during handshakes to react to the indicated server name (e.g., to select a certificate/context). The arg pointer is passed through to the callback. Errors are reported via ec.
requirements: c must be a valid context handle obtained from libtorrent::ssl::get_handle or equivalent.
cb must be a valid function pointer of the appropriate type for the active TLS backend and must remain valid while installed.
arg is an opaque pointer passed to the callback; its lifetime management is the caller’s responsibility.
ec is set on failure; callers should check ec after the call.
This function must be called before initiating handshakes on streams that should use the SNI callback.

functions.name: libtorrent::ssl::set_host_name
functions.signature: void libtorrent::ssl::set_host_name(libtorrent::ssl::stream_handle_type s, std::string const& name, libtorrent::ssl::error_code& ec)
functions.description: Sets the TLS Server Name Indication (SNI) hostname for the given SSL/TLS stream so the peer sees the intended server name during the handshake. Errors are reported via ec.
requirements: s must be a valid native SSL/TLS stream handle compatible with the current TLS backend.
name must be a non-empty DNS host name compliant with RFC constraints for SNI.
Call this before performing the TLS handshake on the stream.
ec is set on failure; callers should check ec after the call.

functions.name: libtorrent::ssl::set_context
functions.description: Associates the given SSL/TLS context with the specified SSL/TLS stream. Typically used to switch or set the context backing an existing stream.
requirements: s must be a valid native SSL/TLS stream handle.
c must be a valid SSL/TLS context handle compatible with the stream and current backend.
The stream and context lifetimes must cover any subsequent use after reassociation.

functions.name: libtorrent::ssl::has_context
functions.description: Checks whether the given SSL/TLS stream currently uses the specified SSL/TLS context. Returns true if the context matches, false otherwise.
requirements: s must be a valid native SSL/TLS stream handle.
c must be a valid SSL/TLS context handle.

functions.name: libtorrent::ssl::get_context
functions.description: Returns the SSL/TLS context handle currently associated with the given SSL/TLS stream.
requirements: s must be a valid native SSL/TLS stream handle.
The returned context handle is only valid as long as the underlying context remains alive and associated with the stream.

functions.name: libtorrent::ssl_stream::get_executor
functions.description: Returns the associated executor of the underlying SSL stream (available when BOOST_VERSION >= 106600). Useful for binding handlers or querying the I/O context associated with this stream.
requirements: Must only be used when compiled with BOOST_VERSION >= 106600 (otherwise the member is not available).
The ssl_stream instance must be valid (not moved-from).

functions.name: libtorrent::ssl_stream::handle
functions.description: Returns the native SSL stream handle for the underlying SSL/TLS stream. Intended for advanced/custom SSL operations that need access to the native handle.
requirements: The ssl_stream instance must be valid (not moved-from).
The returned handle is only meaningful while the underlying stream remains alive.

functions.name: libtorrent::ssl_stream::context_handle
functions.description: Returns the native SSL context handle used by this stream. Useful for low-level SSL configuration or querying context state.
requirements: The ssl_stream instance must be valid (not moved-from).
The returned handle is only meaningful while the underlying stream/context remains alive.

functions.name: libtorrent::ssl_stream::set_host_name
functions.description: Sets the TLS Server Name Indication (SNI) host name on the SSL stream and throws on error. Use to specify the expected server name during client handshakes.
requirements: name must contain the desired SNI host name (non-empty recommended).
Throws boost::system::system_error on failure; callers must be prepared to catch exceptions.

functions.name: libtorrent::ssl_stream::set_verify_callback
functions.signature:
template <class T>
void set_verify_callback(T const& fun, libtorrent::error_code& ec)
functions.description: Sets the certificate verification callback for the SSL stream, reporting errors via ec. The callback controls peer certificate verification during the handshake.
requirements: fun must be a callable compatible with the SSL verification callback expected by the underlying TLS implementation.
Caller must check ec after the call to detect errors.
Must be set before the SSL handshake to affect verification for that session.

functions.name: libtorrent::ssl_stream::async_connect
functions.signature:
template <class Handler>
void async_connect(endpoint_type const& endpoint, Handler const& h)
functions.description: Asynchronously connects the underlying transport to endpoint and then performs an SSL client handshake. The provided completion handler is invoked with the result of the overall operation.
requirements: endpoint must specify a valid remote endpoint.
h must be a valid completion handler and remain valid until invocation.
The ssl_stream must be unopened or not already connected when called.
Buffers/handlers must meet Boost.Asio lifetime rules (handler must be invocable after the operation completes).

functions.name: libtorrent::ssl_stream::async_accept_handshake
functions.signature:
template <class Handler>
void async_accept_handshake(Handler const& h)
functions.description: Asynchronously performs an SSL server handshake on an already-connected underlying transport. Intended for accepting inbound SSL connections.
requirements: Underlying transport must already be connected to a peer (e.g., after TCP accept).
h must be a valid completion handler and remain valid until invocation.
A properly configured ssl::context (e.g., certificates/keys) should be set beforehand to complete a server handshake.

functions.name: libtorrent::ssl_stream::accept_handshake
functions.description: Performs a synchronous SSL server handshake on an already-connected underlying transport. Reports any error in ec.
requirements: Underlying transport must already be connected to a peer.
Caller must check ec after the call to detect handshake errors.
A properly configured ssl::context (e.g., certificates/keys) should be set beforehand to complete a server handshake.

functions.name: libtorrent::ssl_stream::async_shutdown
functions.description: Asynchronously shuts down the SSL stream. Cancels the underlying next_layer() first and then initiates the SSL shutdown. The handler is invoked when shutdown completes.
requirements: handler must be a valid completion handler and remain valid until invocation.
The stream should have completed a handshake before shutdown for predictable behavior.

functions.name: libtorrent::ssl_stream::shutdown
functions.description: Synchronously shuts down the SSL stream and reports any error through ec.
requirements: Caller must check ec after the call to detect shutdown errors.
The stream should have completed a handshake before shutdown for predictable behavior.

handler must be a valid completion handler and remain valid until invocation.
