The returned allocation_slot is only valid for this allocator instance and its current generation.

functions.name: libtorrent::aux::stack_allocator::copy_buffer
functions.description: Allocates space and copies the raw bytes from buf into the allocator, returning an allocation_slot referencing the stored data.
requirements: buf may be empty; if non-empty, it must reference accessible memory for the duration of the call.
The returned allocation_slot is only valid for this allocator instance and its current generation.

functions.name: libtorrent::aux::stack_allocator::allocate
functions.description: Reserves 'bytes' bytes in the allocator without initializing them, and returns an allocation_slot referencing the reserved region. Typically used for manual population followed by ptr() to fill the data.
requirements: bytes must be >= 0. If 0, the returned slot may reference an empty region.
The returned allocation_slot is only valid for this allocator instance and its current generation.

functions.name: libtorrent::aux::stack_allocator::ptr
functions.description: Returns a mutable pointer to the start of the buffer referenced by the given allocation_slot within this allocator.
requirements: idx must be a valid allocation_slot previously returned by this allocator in its current generation.
Passing an invalid or foreign allocation_slot results in undefined behavior.

functions.name: libtorrent::aux::stack_allocator::swap
functions.description: Swaps the internal storage and generation counter with another stack_allocator.
requirements: rhs must be a valid stack_allocator object.
After swap, any allocation_slot/pointers should be considered associated with the allocator that now owns the underlying storage (use with care).

functions.name: libtorrent::aux::stack_allocator::reset
functions.description: Clears the internal storage and sets the allocator's generation counter to the specified value. Used to invalidate cached slots and start a fresh allocation cycle.
requirements: No preconditions. Note that calling reset invalidates all existing allocation_slot values and pointers from this allocator by changing generation and clearing storage.

functions.name: libtorrent::aux::stack_allocator::gen
functions.description: Returns the current generation counter for the allocator. Useful for cache invalidation or checking whether cached slots are still valid.
requirements: No preconditions; safe to call at any time.

functions.name: libtorrent::aux::cached_slot::copy_string
functions.signature: template <typename F> libtorrent::aux::allocation_slot libtorrent::aux::cached_slot::copy_string(libtorrent::aux::stack_allocator& a, F fun)
functions.description: Caches a string allocation inside this cached_slot, keyed by the allocator's generation. If the cached generation differs from a.gen() or the slot is invalid, calls fun() to obtain a string, stores a copy in 'a' using a.copy_string(...), and updates the cache. Otherwise returns the previously cached allocation_slot.
requirements: a must be a valid stack_allocator reference.
fun must be callable with no arguments and return a value acceptable by stack_allocator::copy_string (i.e., libtorrent::string_view or char const*).
The returned allocation_slot is only valid for allocator 'a' and its current generation.

functions.name: libtorrent::aux::cached_slot::clear
functions.description: Clears the cached slot, making it invalid without changing the stored generation. Subsequent copy_string() calls will re-populate the cache.
requirements: No preconditions; safe to call at any time.

functions.name: libtorrent::stat_channel::operator+=
functions.description: Accumulates counters from another stat_channel into this one. Adds s.m_counter to both this channel's per-second accumulator and total counter. Intended to merge statistics from two channels.
requirements: s must represent counters that fit within 32-bit (per-second) and 64-bit (total) addition without overflow. The code asserts against overflow.
This operation assumes counters are non-negative (consistent with how add() is used).

functions.name: libtorrent::stat_channel::add
functions.description: Increments the current second's counter and the total counter by count. Used to record additional bytes/events for the current time slice.
requirements: count must be >= 0 (asserted).
The additions must not overflow 32-bit (m_counter) or 64-bit (m_total_counter) storage (asserted).

functions.name: libtorrent::stat_channel::second_tick
functions.description: Advances the channel's internal time accounting by one tick and updates a smoothed (5-second) average rate based on the elapsed tick interval. Should be called periodically (typically once per second).
requirements: tick_interval_ms should be a positive duration in milliseconds (typically around 1000).
Call this at a steady cadence; comments indicate it should be called once every second.

functions.name: libtorrent::stat_channel::rate
functions.description: Returns the current smoothed rate (5-second average) for this channel.

functions.name: libtorrent::stat_channel::low_pass_rate
functions.description: Returns the low-pass filtered rate; in this implementation it is identical to rate() (the 5-second average).

functions.name: libtorrent::stat_channel::total
functions.description: Returns the total accumulated count for this channel over its lifetime.

functions.name: libtorrent::stat_channel::offset
functions.description: Adjusts the total counter by c without affecting the current per-second counter. Intended to initialize or correct totals (e.g., when resuming from previous sessions).
requirements: The resulting total must not overflow 64-bit signed integer range (asserted).
c may be positive or negative; when negative, the resulting total must remain within valid range.

functions.name: libtorrent::stat_channel::counter
functions.description: Returns the current per-second accumulator value since the last tick.

functions.name: libtorrent::stat_channel::clear
functions.description: Resets the channel's per-second counter, smoothed rate, and total counter to zero.

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::operator+=
functions.description: Accumulates per-channel statistics from another stat into this one by summing corresponding channels.
requirements: Channel-wise additions must not overflow the underlying stat_channel counters (asserted within stat_channel).

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::sent_syn
functions.description: Accounts for sending a TCP SYN (and associated IP/TCP headers) by adding IP protocol overhead to the upload side. Uses 40 bytes for IPv4 or 60 for IPv6 (IP+TCP).
requirements: ipv6 indicates whether the packet was IPv6 (true) or IPv4 (false).

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::received_synack
functions.description: Accounts for receiving a TCP SYN-ACK and sending the ACK, charging corresponding IP/TCP header overhead to both download and upload IP protocol channels. Uses 40 bytes for IPv4 or 60 for IPv6 per direction.
requirements: ipv6 indicates whether the packets were IPv6 (true) or IPv4 (false).

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::received_bytes
functions.description: Accounts received traffic by adding payload and protocol byte counts to the respective download channels.
requirements: bytes_payload must be >= 0 (asserted).
bytes_protocol must be >= 0 (asserted).
Values should be sized such that internal additions do not overflow stat_channel storage (asserted within stat_channel).

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::sent_bytes
functions.description: Accounts sent traffic by adding payload and protocol byte counts to the respective upload channels.
requirements: bytes_payload must be >= 0 (asserted).
bytes_protocol must be >= 0 (asserted).
Values should be sized such that internal additions do not overflow stat_channel storage (asserted within stat_channel).

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::trancieve_ip_packet
functions.description: Accounts IP/TCP header overhead for transferring bytes_transferred over TCP, assuming an MTU of 1500 and charging one packet's header per data packet in both directions (data and ACK). Adds the computed overhead to both upload and download IP protocol channels.
requirements: bytes_transferred should be >= 0 to yield meaningful accounting.
ipv6 indicates whether IPv6 (true) or IPv4 (false) headers are used.

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::upload_ip_overhead
functions.description: Returns the current per-second accumulator of upload-side IP protocol overhead bytes.

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::download_ip_overhead
functions.description: Returns the current per-second accumulator of download-side IP protocol overhead bytes.

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::second_tick
functions.description: Advances all statistic channels by one tick and updates their smoothed rates. Should be called once every second (or with the provided tick interval).
requirements: tick_interval_ms should be a positive duration in milliseconds (typically about 1000).
Call this periodically at a steady cadence; comments indicate it should be called once every second.

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::low_pass_upload_rate
functions.description: Returns the low-pass filtered (smoothed) upload rate, summing payload, protocol, and IP protocol upload channels.

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::low_pass_download_rate
functions.description: Returns the low-pass filtered (smoothed) download rate, summing payload, protocol, and IP protocol download channels.

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::upload_rate
functions.description: Returns the instantaneous (smoothed over ~5s in channels) upload rate by summing payload, protocol, and IP protocol upload channel rates.

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::download_rate
functions.description: Returns the instantaneous (smoothed over ~5s in channels) download rate by summing payload, protocol, and IP protocol download channel rates.

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::total_upload
functions.description: Returns the total uploaded bytes across payload, protocol, and IP protocol channels.

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::total_download
functions.description: Returns the total downloaded bytes across payload, protocol, and IP protocol channels.

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::upload_payload_rate
functions.description: Returns the upload payload rate (smoothed) from the upload_payload channel.

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::download_payload_rate
functions.description: Returns the download payload rate (smoothed) from the download_payload channel.

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::total_payload_upload
functions.description: Returns the total uploaded payload bytes.

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::total_payload_download
functions.description: Returns the total downloaded payload bytes.

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::total_protocol_upload
functions.description: Returns the total uploaded protocol (non-payload) bytes.

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::total_protocol_download
functions.description: Returns the total downloaded protocol (non-payload) bytes.

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::total_transfer
functions.description: Returns the total bytes for the specified channel index.
requirements: channel must be a valid channel index in [0, libtorrent::stat::num_channels).

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::transfer_rate
functions.description: Returns the smoothed rate for the specified channel index.
requirements: channel must be a valid channel index in [0, libtorrent::stat::num_channels).

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::add_stat
functions.description: Offsets the total payload counters to account for prior transfers (e.g., reconnects). Adds downloaded to the download_payload total and uploaded to the upload_payload total.
requirements: downloaded and uploaded should be chosen so resulting totals do not overflow 64-bit signed integer range (asserted within offset()).
Values are expected to be non-negative in normal use (per comment about previous transfers).

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::last_payload_downloaded
functions.description: Returns the current per-second accumulator for downloaded payload bytes (since the last tick).

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::last_payload_uploaded
functions.description: Returns the current per-second accumulator for uploaded payload bytes (since the last tick).

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::last_protocol_downloaded
functions.description: Returns the current per-second accumulator for downloaded protocol bytes (since the last tick).

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::last_protocol_uploaded
functions.description: Returns the current per-second accumulator for uploaded protocol bytes (since the last tick).

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::clear
functions.description: Clears all channels' counters and rates, resetting the stat object to zeroed state.

functions.name: libtorrent::stat::operator[]
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the specified stat_channel by index.
requirements: i must satisfy 0 <= i < libtorrent::stat::num_channels (asserted).
Returned reference remains valid as long as the stat object is alive and not cleared/reinitialized.

functions.name: libtorrent::stat_cache::stat_cache
functions.description: Constructor. Initializes an empty stat_cache used to cache file sizes and file stat errors for a set of files managed by a file_storage. Intended to be used by libtorrent internals to avoid repeated filesystem stat calls.

functions.name: libtorrent::stat_cache::~stat_cache
functions.description: Destructor. Cleans up internal resources associated with the stat cache.

functions.name: libtorrent::stat_cache::reserve
functions.description: Preallocates internal storage for per-file cache entries for num_files files. Useful to avoid reallocations when the number of files is known.
requirements: num_files must be non-negative (inferred from typical reserve semantics and vector sizing).
Should be called before heavy use if the number of files is known to improve performance (inferred).

functions.name: libtorrent::stat_cache::get_filesize
functions.signature: std::int64_t libtorrent::stat_cache::get_filesize(libtorrent::file_index_t i, libtorrent::file_storage const& fs, std::string const& save_path, libtorrent::error_code& ec)
functions.description: Returns the size of file i in the given file_storage, using and updating an internal cache to avoid repeated stat calls. On error, sets ec to indicate the failure. Intended for use when accessing files on disk under save_path.
requirements: i must refer to a valid file in fs (inferred from the use of file_index_t and per-file cache).
save_path should be a valid path to the root directory where fs is stored (inferred from parameter name and typical libtorrent usage).
Caller must check ec after the call; if ec is set, an error occurred and the returned size may not be meaningful (explicit from comment and standard error_code usage).

functions.name: libtorrent::stat_cache::set_dirty
functions.description: Marks the cache entry for file i as dirty/invalid so it will be refreshed on the next query.
requirements: i must refer to an existing file entry in the cache (inferred from per-file cache semantics).

functions.name: libtorrent::stat_cache::clear
functions.description: Clears all cached file sizes and recorded errors, forcing subsequent queries to restat files.

functions.name: libtorrent::stat_cache::set_cache
functions.description: Internal. Sets the cached file size for file i to size.
requirements: i must be a valid file index into the cache (inferred).
size should be a non-negative file size in bytes (inferred from semantics of file size).
Intended for internal use; external callers should prefer get_filesize (noted as internal in header).

functions.name: libtorrent::stat_cache::set_error
functions.description: Internal. Records an error ec for file i in the cache so subsequent queries can return the same error without restatting.
requirements: i must be a valid file index into the cache (inferred).
ec should represent an error condition (non-success error_code) (inferred).
Intended for internal use; external callers should prefer get_filesize (noted as internal in header).

functions.name: libtorrent::operator|
functions.description: Bitwise OR for libtorrent::status_t, enabling combination of status/flag values. It converts both operands to their underlying 8-bit representation, ORs them, and converts back to status_t. Use to combine base status values (e.g., status_t::no_error) with flag bits (e.g., status_t::oversized_file), or to merge multiple flags. Result may contain bits that don't correspond to a single named enumerator; treat as a bitmask.
requirements: lhs must be a libtorrent::status_t value (either a named enumerator or a previously combined value).
rhs must be a libtorrent::status_t value (either a named enumerator or a previously combined value).
Callers should interpret the result as a bitmask; compare/clear bits using corresponding operators or masks (e.g., status_t::mask).
Thread-safe and side-effect free; no object state requirements.

functions.name: libtorrent::operator&
functions.description: Bitwise AND for libtorrent::status_t, enabling masking/testing of flag bits. It converts both operands to their underlying 8-bit representation, ANDs them, and converts back to status_t. Use to extract or test particular bits (e.g., status_t::mask, status_t::oversized_file). Result should be interpreted as a bitmask, not necessarily a standalone enumerator.
requirements: lhs must be a libtorrent::status_t value (either a named enumerator or a previously combined value).
rhs must be a libtorrent::status_t value (either a named enumerator or a previously combined value).
The result is a bitmask of intersecting bits; callers should test against specific flags/masks.
Thread-safe and side-effect free; no object state requirements.

functions.name: libtorrent::operator~
functions.description: Bitwise NOT for libtorrent::status_t. It inverts the underlying 8-bit bits of the operand and converts back to status_t. Use to build negated masks when clearing or testing subsets of bits. The result is a bitmask and may not correspond to any named enumerator.
requirements: lhs must be a libtorrent::status_t value (either a named enumerator or a previously combined value).
Callers should treat the result as a bitmask; typically AND with a mask to clear bits.
Be aware that inversion affects all 8 bits; mask appropriately (e.g., with status_t::mask) to limit to meaningful bits.
Thread-safe and side-effect free; no object state requirements.

functions.name: libtorrent::is_alpha
functions.description: Returns whether the given character is an ASCII alphabetic character. Intended for lightweight, ASCII-only checks.
requirements: Input c is treated as an ASCII character; behavior for negative signed char values is unspecified (cast to unsigned char if needed).

functions.name: libtorrent::to_string
functions.description: Converts a 64-bit signed integer to its textual representation and returns it in a fixed-size character array. Details of formatting (e.g. null-termination, exact placement) are not documented in the header; typically expected to produce a decimal ASCII representation starting at index 0.
requirements: Caller should treat the returned array as a fixed buffer containing the textual representation; do not assume null-termination unless verified from implementation.

functions.name: libtorrent::strip_string
functions.description: Returns a view of the input string with leading and trailing whitespace removed. The operation is non-allocating and returns a substring view into the original.
requirements: The lifetime of the returned string_view must not exceed the lifetime of the input storage referenced by in.
Whitespace definition is implementation-defined; do not rely on non-ASCII space handling without checking implementation.

functions.name: libtorrent::is_print
functions.description: Returns whether the given character is printable (likely ASCII-printable).
requirements: Input c is interpreted as ASCII; if char is signed and may be negative, cast to unsigned char to avoid undefined behavior in classification.

functions.name: libtorrent::is_space
functions.description: Returns whether the given character is a whitespace character (likely ASCII space classification).
requirements: Input c is interpreted as ASCII; if char is signed and may be negative, cast to unsigned char to avoid undefined behavior in classification.

functions.name: libtorrent::to_lower
functions.description: Converts the given character to lower-case (ASCII).
requirements: Input c is interpreted as ASCII; locales and non-ASCII characters are not handled.
Returned value is a char; behavior for non-ASCII input is unspecified.

functions.name: libtorrent::string_begins_no_case
functions.signature: bool libtorrent::string_begins_no_case(char const* s1, char const* s2);
functions.description: Case-insensitive prefix check. Returns true if the C-string s1 begins with the C-string s2, ignoring ASCII case.
requirements: s1 must be a valid, null-terminated C-string.
s2 must be a valid, null-terminated C-string.
Comparison is ASCII case-insensitive; non-ASCII behavior is unspecified.
Pointers must be non-null.

functions.name: libtorrent::string_equal_no_case
functions.description: Case-insensitive equality check between two string_view values using ASCII case folding.
requirements: s1 and s2 must reference valid memory for the duration of the call.
Comparison is ASCII case-insensitive; behavior on non-ASCII is unspecified.

functions.name: libtorrent::url_random
functions.description: Fills the provided span with random, URL-safe characters. Exact alphabet and entropy per character are not documented in this header.
requirements: dest must reference a valid, writable contiguous character buffer of size dest.size().
Function writes exactly dest.size() characters; ensure sufficient capacity.
No guarantees are stated about null-termination; caller must not assume a trailing '\0'.

functions.name: libtorrent::string_ends_with
functions.description: Returns true if s1 ends with the substring s2 (case-sensitive).
requirements: s1 and s2 must remain valid for the duration of the call.
Empty s2 should be considered a suffix; exact behavior follows implementation but typical semantics treat empty suffix as true.

functions.name: libtorrent::search
functions.signature: int libtorrent::search(libtorrent::span<char const> src, libtorrent::span<char const> target);
functions.description: Searches for the byte sequence target within src. Returns the offset at which target matches src; returns -1 if no match is found.

If target is empty, behavior is not explicitly documented; treat as implementation-defined.

functions.name: libtorrent::parse_listen_interfaces
functions.description: Parses the listen_interfaces setting string. Accepts a comma-separated list of IP addresses or device names with ports (e.g., "eth0:6881,eth1:6881" or "127.0.0.1:6881"). Returns a list of listen_interface_t entries. Any parse problems are recorded into the provided errors vector.

functions.name: libtorrent::print_listen_interfaces
functions.description: Formats a collection of listen_interface_t into the listen_interfaces string syntax (comma-separated DEVICE:PORT or IP:PORT). Availability is conditional on build configuration macros.

in must remain valid during the call.

functions.name: libtorrent::parse_comma_separated_string_port
functions.signature: void libtorrent::parse_comma_separated_string_port(std::string const& in, std::vector<std::pair<std::string, int>>& out);

functions.description: Parses a comma-separated list of tokens (device names or IPs) and appends each trimmed token to out. Intended for outgoing_interfaces setting like "eth0, eth1, 127.0.0.1".

functions.name: libtorrent::allocate_string_copy
functions.description: Allocates a new C-string and copies the contents of str into it, similar to strdup, and returns a pointer to the newly allocated, null-terminated buffer. Provided because strdup is not standard in strict ANSI builds.

functions.name: libtorrent::split_string
functions.description: Splits the input view at the first occurrence of sep. Returns a pair where first is the substring before sep and second is the remainder after sep. If sep is not found, first is the whole input and second is an empty view.

requirements: The returned string_view objects reference the same underlying storage as last; the storage must outlive the returned views.

sep is a single character separator.

functions.name: libtorrent::ltrim
functions.description: Removes leading whitespace from the given string in-place.
requirements: s must be a valid std::string reference.
Operation is in-place and may reduce the size of s; callers relying on positions should account for modified indices.

functions.name: libtorrent::is_i2p_url
functions.description: Returns whether the given URL refers to I2P. Exact matching rules are not documented in the header (e.g., scheme, host suffix). Availability depends on TORRENT_USE_I2P being enabled at build time.
requirements: Available only when TORRENT_USE_I2P is defined.
url must be a valid string; semantics of what constitutes an I2P URL are implementation-defined in this context.

functions.name: libtorrent::find_first_of
functions.signature: libtorrent::string_view::size_type find_first_of(libtorrent::string_view const v, char const c, libtorrent::string_view::size_type pos)

functions.name: libtorrent::operator""_sv

functions.name: libtorrent::postinc
functions.description: Returns the current pointer e and advances e to its next node (e = e->next). Intended for iterating intrusive singly-linked lists whose nodes expose a member pointer named next.
requirements: e must be non-null; the function dereferences e to read e->next.
The pointed-to type N must have a publicly accessible member named next that is convertible to N*.
After the call, the caller’s pointer reference e is updated to the original e->next.
Safe only when the list node invariants are valid (i.e., next either points to the next node or is nullptr).

functions.name: libtorrent::tailqueue_iterator::get
functions.description: Returns the current node pointer held by the iterator. May be nullptr to indicate end-of-list.

functions.name: libtorrent::tailqueue_iterator::next
functions.description: Advances the iterator to the next node in the intrusive singly-linked list (current = current->next).
requirements: The iterator’s current pointer must be non-null before calling next(), as it dereferences current to access current->next.

functions.name: libtorrent::tailqueue::iterate
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
libtorrent::tailqueue_iterator<const T> libtorrent::tailqueue<T>::iterate() const

The returned iterator may hold a nullptr if the queue is empty.

functions.name: libtorrent::tailqueue::append
functions.description: Appends all nodes from rhs to the end of this queue, leaving rhs empty. This is a splice of two intrusive queues without relinking individual nodes.
requirements: This function can only be called on an lvalue queue (ref-qualified with &).
Pass rhs as an rvalue (e.g., std::move(other)) because libtorrent::tailqueue is non-copyable and the parameter is by value (move-constructed).
Both queues must be well-formed: their last node’s next must be nullptr (internal asserts rely on this).
No nodes may form cycles; the intrusive next chain must terminate with nullptr in both queues.

functions.description: Prepends all nodes from rhs to the front of this queue, leaving rhs empty. Effectively splices rhs before this queue.
requirements: This function can only be called on an lvalue queue (ref-qualified with &).
Pass rhs as an rvalue (e.g., std::move(other)) because libtorrent::tailqueue is non-copyable and the parameter is by value (move-constructed).
Both queues must be well-formed: their last node’s next must be nullptr and empty-state invariants must hold ((m_last == nullptr) == (m_first == nullptr)).
No nodes may form cycles; the intrusive next chain must terminate with nullptr in both queues.

functions.name: libtorrent::tailqueue::pop_front
functions.description: Removes and returns the first node from the queue. The returned node’s next is set to nullptr and the queue size is decremented.

The queue must be well-formed so that the last node’s next is nullptr (asserted internally).

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent::set_tracker_login

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent::find_tracker
functions.description: Finds and returns the internal tracker entry for the given URL, or nullptr if not present.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent::recalc_share_mode

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent::set_super_seeding

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent::is_predictive_piece
functions.description: Returns true if the piece is currently announced as predictive (expected to be completed imminently).

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent::num_have
functions.description: Returns the number of pieces considered ‘have’ (may include unflushed pieces; seed mode pretends all).

requirements: peer must be connected to this torrent.
index must be within the torrent’s piece range.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent::block_size

functions.description: Converts a piece_block (piece, block index) into a peer_request (piece, offset, size).
requirements: p must refer to a valid piece and block within the torrent.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent::disconnect_all
functions.description: Disconnects all peers from this torrent with the specified error and operation context.
requirements: ec and op should describe the reason for disconnect for logging/alerts.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent::disconnect_peers

ec describes the reason for disconnect.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent::maybe_done_flushing

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent::completed

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent::on_i2p_resolve
functions.signature: void libtorrent::torrent::on_i2p_resolve(libtorrent::error_code const& ec, char const* dest)

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent::is_i2p
functions.description: Returns true if this torrent uses I2P transport.
requirements: Only meaningful when TORRENT_USE_I2P is enabled.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent::on_proxy_name_lookup

requirements: web iterator must be valid at callback time.
addrs may be empty on failure; e indicates error state.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent::on_inactivity_tick

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent::remove_web_seed_iter

requirements: web must be a valid iterator into m_web_seeds for this torrent.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent::finished
