requirements: ep must contain a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address and port.

functions.name: libtorrent::block_info::peer
functions.description: Returns the peer endpoint (IP address and port) recorded for this block.

functions.name: libtorrent::hash_value
functions.description: Hash function for torrent_handle to support use in unordered containers. The ordering/hash is stable for the lifetime of the handle but not across processes or sessions.
requirements: h must be a (possibly default-constructed) torrent_handle; no validity requirement for hashing is stated.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::torrent_handle
functions.description: Default-constructs an invalid torrent_handle. Any operation (except is_valid()) on it may throw.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::add_piece
functions.signature: void libtorrent::torrent_handle::add_piece(piece_index_t piece, char const* data, add_piece_flags_t flags = {}) const
functions.description: Writes the provided piece data to storage as if downloaded from a peer. This overload blocks until the data has been copied into libtorrent’s buffers.
requirements: The torrent must not be in checking state (torrent_status::checking_files).
data must point to a buffer exactly the size of the specified piece (file_storage::piece_size(piece)).
If flags does not include overwrite_existing, existing downloaded data for this piece will not be overwritten.
Handle must be valid and refer to a torrent in session; otherwise operations may throw system_error.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::read_piece
functions.description: Starts an asynchronous read of the specified piece. Completion is delivered via read_piece_alert regardless of alert mask.
requirements: The specified piece must be fully downloaded and written to disk before calling.
Handle must be valid; otherwise a system_error may be thrown.
Completion order is not guaranteed if multiple pieces are read.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::have_piece
functions.description: Returns whether the specified piece has been completely downloaded and written to disk.
requirements: Handle must be valid; otherwise a system_error may be thrown.
piece must be a valid piece index for the torrent.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::post_peer_info
functions.description: Asynchronously posts a peer_info_alert containing peer_info for each connected peer of this torrent.
requirements: Handle must be valid; otherwise a system_error may be thrown.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::get_peer_info
functions.description: Synchronously fills v with one peer_info per connected peer to this torrent.
requirements: v will be cleared and then filled.
Handle must be valid; otherwise a system_error may be thrown.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::status
functions.description: Synchronously queries and returns the current torrent_status. Use flags to request specific fields to reduce overhead; by default all fields are included.
requirements: This call blocks waiting for the libtorrent thread to respond.
Handle must be valid; otherwise a system_error may be thrown.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::post_status
functions.description: Asynchronously posts a state_update_alert containing a single torrent_status for this torrent with the requested fields.
requirements: Handle must be valid; otherwise a system_error may be thrown.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::post_download_queue
functions.description: Triggers posting of a download_queue_alert containing partial_piece_info for pieces with outstanding requests/writes.
requirements: Handle must be valid; otherwise a system_error may be thrown.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::get_download_queue
functions.description: Synchronously returns a vector describing pieces that are partially downloaded or have outstanding requests/writes.
requirements: Returned block_info pointers inside partial_piece_info are invalidated by the next get_download_queue() call.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::set_piece_deadline
functions.signature: void libtorrent::torrent_handle::set_piece_deadline(piece_index_t index, int deadline, deadline_flags_t flags = {}) const
functions.description: Associates a deadline (milliseconds from now) with a piece, prioritizing it for download until complete. Optionally requests a read_piece_alert when it becomes available (alert_when_available).
requirements: index must be a valid piece index.
deadline must be non-negative milliseconds.
If the piece is already downloaded, nothing happens unless flags include alert_when_available, in which case a read_piece() equivalent is triggered.
Handle must be valid; otherwise a system_error may be thrown.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::reset_piece_deadline
functions.description: Removes any deadline associated with the given piece, restoring normal priority.
requirements: index must be a valid piece index.
Handle must be valid; otherwise a system_error may be thrown.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::clear_piece_deadlines
functions.description: Removes deadlines from all pieces in the torrent.
requirements: Handle must be valid; otherwise a system_error may be thrown.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::file_progress
functions.description: Synchronously fills progress with the number of bytes downloaded for each file in the torrent, in torrent_info file order. Optionally uses piece_granularity to make it cheaper but only count verified pieces.
requirements: progress will be cleared and filled to match the number of files.
Operation complexity is O(n + m·j) unless piece_granularity is specified.
Handle must be valid; otherwise a system_error may be thrown.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::post_file_progress
functions.description: Asynchronously posts an alert with file progress (implementation posts open_file_info via alerts; see docs).
requirements: Handle must be valid; otherwise a system_error may be thrown.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::file_status
functions.description: Returns a vector describing the files currently open for this torrent. Files not open are not included; the vector may be empty.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::clear_error
functions.description: If the torrent is in an error state, clears the error and restarts the torrent.
requirements: Handle must be valid; otherwise a system_error may be thrown.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::trackers
functions.description: Returns the current list of trackers (announce_entry) for this torrent.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::replace_trackers
functions.description: Replaces the torrent’s tracker list with the supplied list. To take effect immediately, call force_reannounce().
requirements: The updated trackers are saved to resume data.
Handle must be valid; otherwise a system_error may be thrown.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::add_tracker
functions.description: Adds a tracker to the torrent if it’s not already present, in the tier indicated by the announce_entry.
requirements: No-op if the tracker URL already exists.
Saved in resume data.
Handle must be valid; otherwise a system_error may be thrown.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::post_trackers
functions.description: Asynchronously posts a tracker_list_alert with the torrent’s trackers.
requirements: Handle must be valid; otherwise a system_error may be thrown.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::add_url_seed
functions.description: Adds a BEP 19 URL seed to the torrent. If already present, the call has no effect. The client may download from it if the torrent is active.
requirements: url must be a valid URL string.
Handle must be valid; otherwise a system_error may be thrown.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::remove_url_seed
functions.description: Removes the specified URL seed if present.
requirements: url must match an existing URL seed to have effect.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::url_seeds
functions.description: Returns the set of BEP 19 URL seeds currently configured. URLs that fail may be removed automatically.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::add_http_seed
functions.description: Adds a BEP 17 web seed to the torrent (similar semantics to add_url_seed).
requirements: url must be a valid URL string.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::remove_http_seed
functions.description: Removes the specified BEP 17 web seed if present.
requirements: url must match an existing HTTP seed to have effect.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::http_seeds
functions.description: Returns the set of BEP 17 web seeds currently configured.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::add_extension
functions.signature: void libtorrent::torrent_handle::add_extension(std::function<std::shared_ptr<torrent_plugin>(torrent_handle const&, client_data_t)> const& ext, client_data_t userdata = client_data_t{})
functions.description: Adds an extension (torrent_plugin) instance for this torrent by invoking the supplied factory in libtorrent’s context, passing this handle and userdata.
requirements: ext must be a valid callable returning std::shared_ptr<torrent_plugin>.
The extension factory is called from libtorrent’s internal thread context.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::set_metadata
functions.description: Attempts to set the torrent’s metadata from the bencoded "info" dictionary. On success posts metadata_received_alert; on failure posts metadata_failed_alert. Returns true on success.
requirements: metadata must contain the raw info dictionary; it will be hashed and verified against the info-hash.
If metadata already exists, the function has no effect and returns false.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::is_valid
functions.description: Returns true if this handle currently refers to a torrent still alive (not removed and destructed). This call never throws and completes immediately.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::pause
functions.description: Pauses the torrent, disconnecting peers (gracefully if graceful_pause is set) and stopping new requests. Auto-managed torrents may be resumed automatically unless that flag is cleared.
requirements: Handle must be valid; otherwise a system_error may be thrown.
Use pause_flags_t (e.g., graceful_pause) to control behavior.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::resume
functions.description: Resumes a paused torrent, reconnecting peers and continuing normal operation.
requirements: Handle must be valid; otherwise a system_error may be thrown.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::flags
functions.description: Returns the current torrent state flags (torrent_flags_t).

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::set_flags
functions.description: Sets/clears all flags that are part of mask to match flags, allowing setting and clearing in one call.
requirements: The seed_mode flag can only be set via add_torrent_params and only cleared after the torrent has been added.
Handle must be valid; otherwise a system_error may be thrown.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::unset_flags
functions.description: Clears the specified flags, leaving others unchanged.
requirements: Handle must be valid; otherwise a system_error may be thrown.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::flush_cache
functions.description: Asynchronously flushes the torrent’s disk cache and closes file handles. Completion signaled via cache_flushed_alert.
requirements: By the time the alert is received, all data cached at the time of the call is guaranteed flushed (new data may be cached after).

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::force_recheck
functions.description: Forces the torrent into a full recheck of files on disk. Disconnects peers, stops announcing, queues the torrent for checking, and then resumes normal operation when done. Moves torrent to the back of the queue.
requirements: Handle must be valid; otherwise a system_error may be thrown.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::save_resume_data
functions.description: Asynchronously generates and posts resume data (add_torrent_params) via save_resume_data_alert. May post save_resume_data_failed_alert if conditions are not met (e.g., being removed, only_if_modified with no changes).
requirements: If shutting down, do not remove_torrent() before receiving save_resume_data_alert.
Flags control when to save (e.g., only_if_modified, if_* flags).
Handle must be valid; otherwise a system_error may be thrown.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::get_resume_data
functions.description: Synchronously generates and returns resume data (add_torrent_params). Blocks the caller until data is produced.
requirements: This call blocks.
Flags control what to include (e.g., save_info_dict) and whether to allow skipping for only_if_modified.
Handle must be valid; otherwise a system_error may be thrown.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::need_save_resume_data
functions.description: Returns whether any data that goes into resume data has changed since it was last saved.
requirements: This call blocks waiting for libtorrent thread response.
Meaningful only if save_resume_data_alerts are properly handled.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::queue_position
functions.description: Returns the torrent’s position in the download queue. Seeding torrents have -1.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::queue_position_up
functions.description: Moves this torrent one step closer to the front of the download queue.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::queue_position_down
functions.description: Moves this torrent one step closer to the back of the download queue.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::queue_position_top
functions.description: Moves this torrent to the front (top) of the download queue.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::queue_position_bottom
functions.description: Moves this torrent to the back (bottom) of the download queue.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::queue_position_set
functions.description: Moves this torrent to the specified queue position, shifting others to make space while maintaining their relative order.
requirements: p must be a non-negative queue position (other than -1 reserved for seeds).

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::set_ssl_certificate
functions.signature: void libtorrent::torrent_handle::set_ssl_certificate(std::string const& certificate, std::string const& private_key, std::string const& dh_params, std::string const& passphrase = "")
functions.description: Sets the SSL certificate, private key, DH parameters and optional passphrase for SSL torrents, using file paths to PEM-encoded files. Needed to connect to peers for SSL torrents.
requirements: certificate, private_key, dh_params must be paths to PEM files.
If private_key is encrypted, passphrase must be provided.
After setting, resuming the torrent is typically required for connections to proceed.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::set_ssl_certificate_buffer
functions.signature: void libtorrent::torrent_handle::set_ssl_certificate_buffer(std::string const& certificate, std::string const& private_key, std::string const& dh_params)
functions.description: Sets the SSL certificate material from in-memory PEM strings for SSL torrents.
requirements: certificate, private_key, dh_params must contain valid PEM data.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::torrent_file
functions.description: Returns a (possibly copied) torrent_info for this torrent, or nullptr if metadata is not available. Not guaranteed to be the same instance as originally added.
requirements: Do not assume piece layers/trackers/etc. match the originally added torrent_info. For saving .torrent files, prefer save_resume_data() + write_torrent_file().

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::torrent_file_with_hashes
functions.description: Returns a copy of torrent_info including piece layers (for v2 torrents) if available. More expensive than torrent_file().
requirements: Piece layers are included only if available (e.g., added from .torrent with layers or seeding).
Magnet-added torrents may lack full merkle trees until completed.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::piece_layers
functions.description: Synchronously returns piece-layer hashes for all files (empty for v1 torrents). Blocks until synchronized with libtorrent thread.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::post_piece_availability
functions.description: Asynchronously posts a piece_availability_alert with availability counts per piece.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::piece_availability
functions.description: Fills avail with the number of connected peers that have each piece. For seeds, availability is reported as 0 for all pieces.
requirements: avail will be resized or cleared and filled to number_of_pieces().

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::piece_priority
functions.description: Sets the priority of the specified piece. 0 disables downloading that piece; 1–7 are increasing priorities; default is 4.
requirements: index must be a valid piece index.
For magnet (no metadata yet) torrents, piece priorities cannot be changed (no-op).

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::prioritize_pieces
functions.description: Sets priorities for all pieces from the provided vector (one entry per piece).
requirements: pieces.size() must equal the number of pieces.
For torrents without metadata, piece priorities cannot be changed (no-op).

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::get_piece_priorities
functions.description: Returns a vector of priorities for all pieces in the torrent.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::file_priority
functions.description: Sets the priority of the specified file; internally maps to piece priorities. Changing file priorities resets piece priorities to match file priorities.
requirements: index must be a valid file index.
Cannot set priorities on torrents without metadata or on torrents that are seeds (no-op).
Applying file priorities is asynchronous; to synchronize, wait for file_prio_alert.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::prioritize_files
functions.description: Sets priorities for all files from the provided vector, resetting piece priorities accordingly.
requirements: files.size() must equal the number of files in the torrent.
Cannot set priorities on torrents without metadata or on torrents that are seeds (no-op).
Applying file priorities is asynchronous; to synchronize, wait for file_prio_alert.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::get_file_priorities
functions.description: Returns a vector of priorities for all files in the torrent.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::force_reannounce
functions.signature: void libtorrent::torrent_handle::force_reannounce(int seconds = 0, int idx = -1, reannounce_flags_t = {}) const
functions.description: Schedules a forced tracker announce in seconds from now. If idx is -1, all trackers are re-announced; otherwise only the given tracker index. By default honors tracker min_interval; ignore_min_interval can override.
requirements: seconds must be >= 0.
If min_interval has not elapsed, the forced announce may be delayed until the interval expires unless ignore_min_interval is set.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::force_dht_announce
functions.description: Immediately announces the torrent to the DHT.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::force_lsd_announce
functions.description: Immediately announces the torrent via Local Service Discovery (LSD).

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::scrape_tracker
functions.description: Sends a scrape request to a tracker (last working if idx == -1, otherwise by index). Updates num_complete/num_incomplete in torrent_status. Completion posts scrape_reply_alert or scrape_failed_alert.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::set_upload_limit
functions.description: Sets the per-torrent upload bandwidth limit in bytes/second. Global limits still apply.
requirements: limit must be >= 0 (0 typically means unlimited; see settings).

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::upload_limit
functions.description: Returns the current per-torrent upload bandwidth limit in bytes/second.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::set_download_limit
functions.description: Sets the per-torrent download bandwidth limit in bytes/second. Global limits still apply.
requirements: limit must be >= 0 (0 typically means unlimited; see settings).

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::download_limit
functions.description: Returns the current per-torrent download bandwidth limit in bytes/second.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::connect_peer
functions.signature: void libtorrent::torrent_handle::connect_peer(tcp::endpoint const& adr, peer_source_flags_t source = {}, pex_flags_t flags = pex_encryption | pex_utp | pex_holepunch) const
functions.description: Attempts to connect to a specific peer endpoint for this torrent. The source flags are ORed into the peer’s source mask; pex_flags control connection preferences (encryption, uTP, holepunch).
requirements: Handle must be valid and the torrent must not be uninitialized/queued/checking; otherwise a system_error may be thrown.
adr must specify a valid address and port.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::clear_peers
functions.description: Disconnects all peers and clears the peer list for this torrent.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::set_max_uploads
functions.description: Sets the maximum number of unchoked peers for this torrent. -1 means unlimited. Global unchoke slot limits still apply.
requirements: If set, value must be >= -1.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::max_uploads
functions.description: Returns the current per-torrent maximum number of unchoked peers.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::set_max_connections
functions.description: Sets the per-torrent maximum number of connections. -1 means unlimited. Must be at least 2 when limited.
requirements: max_connections must be -1 or >= 2.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::max_connections
functions.description: Returns the current per-torrent maximum number of connections.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::move_storage
functions.signature: void libtorrent::torrent_handle::move_storage(std::string const& save_path, move_flags_t flags = move_flags_t::always_replace_files) const
functions.description: Asynchronously moves/copies the torrent’s files to save_path. Completion posts storage_moved_alert or storage_moved_failed_alert. Behavior is controlled by move flags (always_replace_files, fail_if_exist, dont_replace).
requirements: save_path must be a valid destination path.
Operation may block other disk IO while copying (performed on disk thread).
fail_if_exist may fail with file_exists if any target file exists.
Files renamed to absolute paths are not moved.
Sparse regions may not be preserved when copying.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::rename_file
functions.signature: void libtorrent::torrent_handle::rename_file(file_index_t index, std::string const& new_name) const
functions.description: Asynchronously renames the file at index. Completion posts file_renamed_alert or file_rename_failed_alert.
requirements: index must be a valid file index.
new_name must be a valid target name/path allowed by the storage backend.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::info_hash
functions.description: Returns the info-hash for v1 torrents (or a truncated hash for v2). For the full v2 hash, use info_hashes().

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::info_hashes
functions.description: Returns the (possibly dual) info-hash set for the torrent (supports v1 and v2).

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::native_handle
functions.description: Returns a shared_ptr to the internal torrent object. Intended for plugins/alerts only. Not a stable ABI and not thread-safe to use outside libtorrent’s internal thread.
requirements: Client and library must be built with matching TORRENT_* build configuration macros.
Access must be restricted to libtorrent’s internal thread for thread safety.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::userdata
functions.description: Returns the userdata pointer associated with this torrent (from add_torrent_params).

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_handle::in_session
functions.description: Returns true if the torrent is still in the session (before remove_torrent()). This is a blocking call, unlike is_valid().

functions.name: std::hash<libtorrent::torrent_handle>::operator()
functions.description: Standard hash functor specialization delegating to libtorrent::hash_value for torrent_handle.

functions.name: libtorrent::aux::sanitize_append_path_element
functions.signature: void libtorrent::aux::sanitize_append_path_element(std::string& path, string_view element, bool force_element = false)
functions.description: Internal helper that sanitizes a single path element and appends it to an existing path string. Used to ensure safe filesystem paths (e.g., removing/normalizing dangerous components) before concatenation.
requirements: path must be a valid mutable string buffer that will receive the sanitized and appended element
element is treated as a single path element; directory separators or parent traversals (if any) may be sanitized/removed
If force_element is true, an element will be appended even if the input would otherwise be empty after sanitization
Function is internal; behavior details beyond sanitizing/append are not documented

functions.name: libtorrent::aux::verify_encoding
functions.description: Internal helper that verifies and possibly normalizes the string encoding (typically UTF-8) of target. Returns true if the string passes verification (after any in-place adjustments).
requirements: target is modified in-place; caller must be prepared for its content to change
Exact encoding rules and transformations are not documented; inferred to check/normalize UTF-8 per libtorrent conventions

functions.name: libtorrent::web_seed_entry::web_seed_entry
functions.signature: libtorrent::web_seed_entry::web_seed_entry(std::string url_, libtorrent::web_seed_entry::type_t type_, std::string auth_ = std::string(), libtorrent::web_seed_entry::headers_t extra_headers_ = libtorrent::web_seed_entry::headers_t())
functions.description: Constructs a web seed entry describing a URL seed (BEP 19) or HTTP seed (BEP 17). Optionally supplies HTTP Basic auth credentials and extra HTTP headers for requests to this seed.
requirements: url_ should be a valid HTTP/HTTPS URL understood by the corresponding seed type
type_ must be either libtorrent::web_seed_entry::url_seed or libtorrent::web_seed_entry::http_seed
auth_, if set, must be in the form "username:password" for HTTP Basic auth
extra_headers_ items are name/value string pairs to include as HTTP headers

functions.name: libtorrent::web_seed_entry::operator==
functions.description: Compares two web_seed_entry objects for equality by URL and type.
requirements: Comparison is case-sensitive and compares URL strings verbatim and type value

functions.name: libtorrent::web_seed_entry::operator<
functions.description: Strict-weak-ordering comparison for web_seed_entry. Orders first by URL lexicographically, then by type.
requirements: Intended for use in ordered containers; imposes lexicographic order on url and then on type

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::torrent_info
functions.description: Constructs torrent_info from a parsed bdecoded .torrent root node. Throws on error (when exceptions are enabled).
requirements: torrent_file must represent a valid .torrent dictionary
On malformed input, this overload throws (if exceptions are enabled)

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::~torrent_info
functions.description: Destructor. Frees storage associated with this torrent_info instance.
requirements: No specific caller requirements; object must have been properly constructed

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::operator=
functions.description: Copy assignment is explicitly deleted; torrent_info cannot be copy-assigned.
requirements: Cannot be called; attempting to copy-assign will be a compile error

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::files
functions.description: Returns the (possibly modified) file_storage describing how pieces map to files for this torrent.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid as long as *this remains alive and not modified in ways that replace the storage

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::orig_files
functions.description: Returns the original, unmodified file_storage snapshot preserved from the loaded torrent metadata. Useful for building web seed URLs.
requirements: A torrent must be loaded; otherwise semantics are unspecified

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::rename_file
functions.description: Renames a single file in the storage to a new path or name. Updates the file_storage returned by files(); orig_files() remains unchanged.
requirements: index must refer to an existing file: 0 <= index < num_files()
new_filename may be relative (under save_path) or absolute (detaches it from save_path and prevents moving with move_storage())

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::remap_files
functions.description: Replaces the file layout mapping with a new file_storage f. Intended to map torrent data to a different set of files (e.g., single large file, sector-aligned files).
requirements: f must have exactly the same total size as the current storage
Use is discouraged for v2 torrents due to tight coupling between piece and file boundaries

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::add_tracker
functions.description: Adds a tracker URL to the announce-list at the specified tier.
requirements: url should be a valid tracker URL
tier is a non-negative integer selecting priority group; lower tiers are tried before higher tiers

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::trackers
functions.description: Returns the current list of tracker announce entries, sorted by tier and order added.
requirements: Returned reference is valid while torrent_info remains alive and until the list is mutated

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::clear_trackers
functions.description: Removes all trackers from the announce-list.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::similar_torrents
functions.description: Returns info-hashes listed under the "similar" key (BEP 38) from both inside and outside the info-dict.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::collections
functions.description: Returns collection strings listed under the "collections" key (BEP 38) from both inside and outside the info-dict.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::add_url_seed
functions.signature: void libtorrent::torrent_info::add_url_seed(std::string const& url, std::string const& ext_auth = std::string(), libtorrent::web_seed_entry::headers_t const& ext_headers = libtorrent::web_seed_entry::headers_t())
functions.description: Adds a URL seed (BEP 19) to the torrent, optionally with external authorization and extra HTTP headers.
requirements: url should be a valid HTTP/HTTPS URL seed
ext_auth, if provided, is sent as the HTTP Authorization header value and overrides any credentials in the URL
ext_headers are custom HTTP headers for this seed

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::add_http_seed
functions.signature: void libtorrent::torrent_info::add_http_seed(std::string const& url, std::string const& extern_auth = std::string(), libtorrent::web_seed_entry::headers_t const& extra_headers = libtorrent::web_seed_entry::headers_t())
functions.description: Adds an HTTP seed (BEP 17) to the torrent, optionally with external authorization and extra HTTP headers.
requirements: url should be a valid HTTP/HTTPS seed URL
extern_auth, if provided, is sent as the HTTP Authorization header value and overrides any credentials in the URL
extra_headers are custom HTTP headers for this seed

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::web_seeds
functions.description: Returns all configured web seeds (both URL seeds and HTTP seeds).
requirements: Returned reference is valid while torrent_info remains alive and until the web seed list is mutated

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::set_web_seeds
functions.description: Replaces the current set of web seeds with the provided list.
requirements: seeds entries should have valid URLs and types

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::_internal_drain
functions.description: Internal: moves out and returns the current trackers, web_seeds, and nodes vectors, leaving them empty in this object.
requirements: Intended for internal use; after calling, trackers(), web_seeds(), and nodes() will be emptied in this instance

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::total_size
functions.description: Returns the total size in bytes represented by the torrent (piece_count * piece_length, accounting for the possibly smaller last piece; includes pad files).

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::piece_length
functions.description: Returns the nominal piece length in bytes.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::num_pieces
functions.description: Returns the total number of pieces in the torrent.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::blocks_per_piece
functions.description: Returns the number of blocks per typical piece (may be fewer for the last piece).

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::last_piece
functions.description: Returns the index of the last piece in the torrent.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::end_piece
functions.description: Returns the one-past-the-end piece index (i.e., last_piece() + 1).
requirements: m_files.num_pieces() must be > 0; i.e., the torrent must be loaded and non-empty (asserted internally)

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::piece_range
functions.description: Returns a range suitable for range-for iteration over all piece indices.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::info_hash
functions.description: Returns the v1 (SHA-1) info-hash of the torrent. For v2 support, use info_hashes().

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::info_hashes
functions.description: Returns the combined info_hash_t, which may hold v1 and/or v2 hashes for hybrid torrents.
requirements: Returned reference remains valid while the torrent_info object exists

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::v1
functions.description: Returns true if this torrent has v1 metadata.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::v2
functions.description: Returns true if this torrent has v2 metadata.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::num_files
functions.description: Returns the number of files in the file_storage.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::map_block
functions.signature: std::vector<file_slice> libtorrent::torrent_info::map_block(piece_index_t piece, std::int64_t offset, int size) const
functions.description: Maps a piece-relative byte range (piece, offset, size) to a set of file slices where the data belongs on disk.
requirements: is_loaded() must be true
piece must be within [0, end_piece())
offset and size must describe a valid in-piece range: 0 <= offset, 0 <= size, and offset + size <= piece_size(piece)

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::map_file
functions.signature: peer_request libtorrent::torrent_info::map_file(file_index_t file, std::int64_t offset, int size) const
functions.description: Maps a file-relative byte range to the corresponding torrent piece range (peer_request).
requirements: is_loaded() must be true
file must be a valid file index: 0 <= file < num_files()
offset and size must be within the file bounds: 0 <= offset and offset + size <= file_size(file)

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::ssl_cert
functions.description: Returns the SSL root certificate for an SSL torrent as an x509 string, or an empty string if not an SSL torrent.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::is_valid
functions.description: Returns true if a torrent is loaded (metadata resolved), false otherwise.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::priv
functions.description: Returns true if this is a private torrent (should not use DHT, etc.).

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::is_i2p
functions.description: Returns true if this torrent is considered an i2p torrent (e.g., has a .i2p tracker), which disables DHT, LSD, and non-i2p transports.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::v2_piece_hashes_verified
functions.description: Returns true if v2 piece hashes were loaded and verified from the torrent metadata.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::set_piece_layers
functions.description: Internal: sets the v2 per-file piece layer hash buffers for the torrent (SHA-256 hash list per file).
requirements: pl must contain one entry per file that has a piece layer; each buffer size must be divisible by 32 (implicit from piece_layer() docs)

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::piece_size
functions.description: Returns the exact size of the specified piece (the last piece may be smaller than piece_length()).
requirements: index must be within [0, end_piece())

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::hash_for_piece
functions.description: Returns the SHA-1 hash for a v1 piece at the specified index.
requirements: is_loaded() must be true
index must be within [0, end_piece())
Only meaningful for torrents with v1 metadata

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::hash_for_piece_ptr
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the 20-byte SHA-1 digest for the specified v1 piece. The memory is owned by the torrent_info and is not null-terminated.
requirements: index must be >= 0 and < end_piece()
is_loaded() must be true
Underlying info-section must contain piece hashes (v1 metadata)
Caller must not read past 20 bytes starting at the returned pointer

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::is_loaded
functions.description: Returns true if the torrent metadata has been loaded (i.e., num_files() > 0).

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::name
functions.description: Returns the torrent name as a UTF-8 string.
requirements: Returned reference remains valid while the torrent_info object exists

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::creation_date
functions.description: Returns the torrent creation date (POSIX time). Returns 0 if not present.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::creator
functions.description: Returns the "created by" string from the torrent, or an empty string if absent.
requirements: Returned reference remains valid while the torrent_info object exists

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::comment
functions.description: Returns the comment string from the torrent (UTF-8), or an empty string if absent.
requirements: Returned reference remains valid while the torrent_info object exists

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::nodes
functions.description: Returns the list of DHT nodes (hostname and port) included in the torrent metadata.
requirements: Returned reference remains valid while the torrent_info object exists and until mutated

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::add_node
functions.description: Adds a known DHT node (hostname and port) to the torrent metadata (used for DHT bootstrap).
requirements: node.second (port) should be a valid TCP port number in [0, 65535]
node.first should be a hostname or IP address string

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::parse_info_section
functions.signature: bool libtorrent::torrent_info::parse_info_section(bdecode_node const& info, error_code& ec, int max_pieces)
functions.description: Populates the torrent_info from a parsed info-dictionary (e.g., obtained via magnet). Applies a piece-count limit. Returns true on success; on failure, returns false and sets ec.
requirements: info must refer to a valid info-dictionary node
max_pieces limits allowable piece count; torrents exceeding this fail
ec is set on failure; object may remain partially initialized

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::info
functions.description: Looks up a key inside the info-dictionary of the loaded torrent and returns the corresponding bdecode_node; returns a null/empty node if not found.
requirements: A torrent must be loaded; otherwise the node may be empty
key is a null-terminated C-string naming the info-dict key to look up

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::info_section
functions.description: Returns a span view of the raw info section bytes of the torrent. The underlying memory is owned by torrent_info.
requirements: Returned span becomes invalid when the torrent_info is destroyed or its metadata buffer is freed/replaced
Caller must not modify the underlying bytes

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::piece_layer
functions.description: Returns the bytes of the v2 piece layer hashes for the specified file. Buffer size is divisible by 32 (SHA-256). If the file has no piece layer, returns an empty span. For small files (<= piece size), returns the root hash.
requirements: Argument must be a valid file index: 0 <= index < num_files()

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::free_piece_layers
functions.description: Clears piece layer buffers from the torrent_info (the session stores them internally once added).

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::internal_set_creator
functions.description: Internal: sets the creator string field.
requirements: Intended for internal use; string_view must remain valid only for the duration of the call (value is copied internally)

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::internal_set_creation_date
functions.description: Internal: sets the creation date field.
requirements: Intended for internal use

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_info::internal_set_comment
functions.description: Internal: sets the comment string field.
requirements: Intended for internal use; string_view must remain valid only for the duration of the call (value is copied internally)

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_priority
functions.description: Computes a symmetric priority value for a peer pair based on their endpoints. Intended to compare/connect peers; one endpoint is expected to be the local endpoint. Usage: pass two TCP endpoints (local and remote) to obtain a 32-bit rank usable for ordering or prioritization. Implementation details are not in this header.
requirements: At least one of the endpoints should represent the local endpoint (as stated in the comment).
Endpoints must be valid tcp::endpoint instances (address and port initialized).
The return value is a 32-bit priority suitable for comparisons; no stability across runs is guaranteed (unspecified).

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_peer::total_download
functions.description: Returns the total number of bytes downloaded from this peer. Exact computation is not shown here; based on struct comments it likely aggregates historical session counters with any current connection metrics. Details of units and inclusion of current connection are unknown since the implementation is not present.
requirements: The torrent_peer instance must be valid and properly constructed.
No thread-safety guarantees are documented; callers should ensure appropriate synchronization if accessed concurrently.
Return value units are bytes (inferred from return type); historical fields in the struct are in KiB, but method semantics are not fully documented here.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_peer::total_upload
functions.description: Returns the total number of bytes uploaded to this peer. Exact computation is not visible; it likely combines historic counters with any current connection metrics. Precise details are unknown in this header.
requirements: The torrent_peer instance must be valid and properly constructed.
No thread-safety guarantees are documented; callers should ensure appropriate synchronization if accessed concurrently.
Return value units are bytes (inferred from return type); historical fields in the struct are in KiB, but method semantics are not fully documented here.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_peer::rank
functions.signature: std::uint32_t libtorrent::torrent_peer::rank(libtorrent::external_ip const& external, int external_port) const
functions.description: Computes a rank (priority) value for this peer, based on our external IP/port and the peer’s address. Used to prioritize peers. The exact algorithm is not provided here.
requirements: The torrent_peer instance must be valid and properly constructed.
The external parameter must reference a valid libtorrent::external_ip object representing our external address state.
external_port should be a valid TCP port number in the range [0, 65535].
No thread-safety guarantees are documented; callers should synchronize if accessed concurrently.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_peer::address
functions.description: Returns the network address of this peer as a libtorrent::address (IPv4 or IPv6). For I2P peers, address-based comparison may not apply; use dest() for I2P destination handling.
requirements: The torrent_peer instance must be valid and properly constructed.
If the peer represents an I2P destination, the returned IP address may not be meaningful; use dest() in that case (inferred from presence of is_i2p_addr/dest()).

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_peer::dest
functions.description: Returns the destination string for this peer. Primarily applicable to I2P peers where peers are identified by destination strings. For non-I2P peers, behavior/details are not documented here and may be an empty/unspecified view.
requirements: The torrent_peer instance must be valid and properly constructed.
The returned string_view is non-owning; the underlying storage must remain valid for the duration of use by the caller.
For non-I2P peers, contents may be empty or unspecified (not documented).

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_peer::ip
functions.description: Returns the peer’s socket endpoint composed of address() and port. Useful for making connections or logging.
requirements: The torrent_peer instance must be valid and properly constructed.
port is a std::uint16_t field; its value must be a valid port in [0, 65535] to form a meaningful endpoint.
address() should return a valid IPv4/IPv6 address for non-I2P peers; for I2P peers, this endpoint may be non-meaningful (inferred).

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_peer::to_string
functions.description: Formats this peer into a human-readable string (for logging/debugging). Only available when logging is enabled at compile time (TORRENT_DISABLE_LOGGING not defined).
requirements: This function is only available if TORRENT_DISABLE_LOGGING is not defined at compile time.
The torrent_peer instance must be valid and properly constructed.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_peer::protocol
functions.description: Returns the BitTorrent protocol version (V1 or V2) this peer is marked to support, based on the protocol_v2 flag. Useful for capability-gated behavior.
requirements: The torrent_peer instance must be valid and properly constructed.
protocol_v2 flag should reflect the known capability of the peer; no additional preconditions are documented.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_peer::peer_source
functions.description: Returns the bitmask of sources from which this peer was learned, as a peer_source_flags_t, derived from the internal source field.
requirements: The torrent_peer instance must be valid and properly constructed.

functions.name: libtorrent::ipv4_peer::operator=
functions.description: Copy-assigns an ipv4_peer from another ipv4_peer, updating this object’s state to match the source. Lvalue-qualified; cannot assign to rvalues.
requirements: Both the target and source objects must be valid ipv4_peer instances.
Because the operator is lvalue-qualified (&), the left-hand side must be an lvalue (cannot assign to a temporary).
No-throw or strong exception guarantees are not documented; callers should assume standard copy-assignment semantics.

functions.name: libtorrent::peer_address_compare::operator()
functions.signature: bool libtorrent::peer_address_compare::operator()(libtorrent::torrent_peer const* lhs, libtorrent::address const& rhs) const
functions.description: Comparator: orders a torrent_peer pointer against a network address. For I2P peers, they are sorted after IP addresses. Used to maintain associative containers keyed by addresses.
requirements: lhs must point to a valid torrent_peer object.
Comparator imposes a strict weak ordering suitable for ordered containers (e.g., std::set, std::map).
Behavior involving I2P peers depends on TORRENT_USE_I2P at compile time.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_peer_equal
functions.signature: bool libtorrent::torrent_peer_equal(libtorrent::torrent_peer const* lhs, libtorrent::torrent_peer const* rhs)
functions.description: Equality predicate for torrent_peer pointers. If both are I2P, compares their dest() strings; otherwise compares IP address and port. Useful for deduplication or associative container equality checks.
requirements: lhs and rhs must point to valid torrent_peer objects.
When comparing non-I2P peers, both address() and port must match to be equal.
When exactly one is I2P and the other is not, returns false (as per implementation).

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_peer_allocator_interface::allocate_peer_entry
functions.description: Allocates and returns a torrent_peer entry of the specified peer type from an implementing allocator. Intended to construct peer objects (e.g., IPv4/IPv6/I2P) backed by an internal pool in concrete implementations.
requirements: Argument 'type' must be one of libtorrent::torrent_peer_allocator_interface::peer_type_t values (ipv4_peer_type, ipv6_peer_type, or i2p_peer_type).
May return nullptr on allocation failure or unsupported type (behavior not documented in this header).
Caller owns the returned pointer and must release it using the matching free_peer_entry() of the same allocator implementation.
Thread-safety and error semantics are not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_peer_allocator_interface::free_peer_entry
functions.description: Releases a previously allocated torrent_peer entry back to the implementing allocator.
requirements: Parameter 'p' must be a pointer previously returned by the same allocator's allocate_peer_entry().
'p' must not be nullptr (not specified in header whether nullptr is allowed; behavior unknown).
'p' must not be freed more than once; use-after-free is invalid (inferred from allocator semantics).
After this call, 'p' must not be dereferenced by the caller.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_peer_allocator::allocate_peer_entry
functions.description: Concrete allocator that allocates a torrent_peer of the given type from an internal fixed-size pool (separate pools for IPv4, IPv6, and conditionally I2P). Tracks cumulative and live allocation statistics.
requirements: Argument 'type' must be one of libtorrent::torrent_peer_allocator_interface::peer_type_t values: ipv4_peer_type, ipv6_peer_type, or i2p_peer_type (I2P only if compiled with TORRENT_USE_I2P).
May return nullptr if the pool cannot satisfy the allocation or if the type is unsupported at compile-time (unknown exact behavior).
The returned pointer must be freed with libtorrent::torrent_peer_allocator::free_peer_entry() from the same allocator instance.
No thread-safety is specified; concurrent use requirements are unknown.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_peer_allocator::free_peer_entry
functions.description: Frees a torrent_peer previously obtained from this allocator and returns it to the appropriate internal pool; updates live allocation/byte counters.
requirements: Parameter 'p' must be a pointer previously returned by libtorrent::torrent_peer_allocator::allocate_peer_entry() on the same allocator instance.
'p' must not be nullptr (acceptance of nullptr is not documented; behavior unknown).
Do not free the same pointer more than once; after this call, the pointer becomes invalid.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_peer_allocator::total_bytes
functions.description: Returns the cumulative number of bytes ever allocated by this allocator across its peer pools.
requirements: None beyond a valid libtorrent::torrent_peer_allocator instance.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_peer_allocator::total_allocations
functions.description: Returns the cumulative number of allocation operations performed by this allocator.
requirements: None beyond a valid libtorrent::torrent_peer_allocator instance.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_peer_allocator::live_bytes
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes currently live (not yet freed) across all peer pools managed by this allocator.
requirements: None beyond a valid libtorrent::torrent_peer_allocator instance.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_peer_allocator::live_allocations
functions.description: Returns the number of live (outstanding) allocations currently held by clients of this allocator.
requirements: None beyond a valid libtorrent::torrent_peer_allocator instance.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_status::torrent_status
functions.description: Default-constructs a torrent_status snapshot object. Initializes all members to their default values as defined in the header. Intended to be filled by torrent_handle::status() or by assignment/copy from another instance.
requirements: No arguments required.
Object may be used immediately after construction; members hold default/zero-initialized values until populated.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_status::torrent_status
functions.description: Copy-constructs a torrent_status from another instance, duplicating its snapshot state, including handle and all fields.
requirements: The source object must be a valid, initialized torrent_status instance.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_status::torrent_status
functions.description: Move-constructs a torrent_status from another instance, transferring its snapshot state (including handle) and leaving the source in a valid but unspecified state. Guaranteed not to throw.
requirements: The source must be an rvalue torrent_status (temporaries or std::move).
After the move, only destruction or re-assignment of the moved-from object should be relied upon; other fields are unspecified.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_status::~torrent_status
functions.description: Destroys the torrent_status object, releasing any internal resources. Safe to call when the object holds default-constructed or populated state.
requirements: The object must have been previously constructed.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_status::operator=
functions.description: Copy-assigns the snapshot state from another torrent_status into this object, replacing current contents.
requirements: Both this object and the source must be valid torrent_status instances.
Self-assignment is permitted.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_status::operator=
functions.description: Move-assigns the snapshot state from another torrent_status into this object, transferring ownership of internal state and leaving the source valid but unspecified.
requirements: The source must be an rvalue torrent_status (temporaries or std::move).
After the move, only destruction or re-assignment of the moved-from object should be relied upon; other fields are unspecified.
Self-move-assignment behavior is unspecified by the header; avoid moving from the same object.

functions.name: libtorrent::torrent_status::operator==
functions.description: Compares two torrent_status objects for referring to the same torrent. Only compares the handle field; other fields are ignored.
requirements: Both objects must be valid torrent_status instances.
Equality is determined solely by (this->handle == st.handle).

functions.name: std::hash<libtorrent::torrent_status>::operator()
functions.description: Computes a hash value for a libtorrent::torrent_status by hashing its handle (returns libtorrent::hash_value(ts.handle)). Useful for using torrent_status as keys in unordered containers.
requirements: The provided torrent_status must be valid; its handle must be hashable via libtorrent::hash_value.
No side effects; callable multiple times and expected to be stable while the handle remains unchanged.

functions.name: libtorrent::request_callback::tracker_warning
functions.signature: virtual void tracker_warning(libtorrent::tracker_request const& req, std::string const& msg) = 0;
functions.description: Pure virtual callback invoked to deliver a warning message from a tracker for a specific tracker request. Implement in a subclass to observe non-fatal tracker warnings.
requirements: Must be implemented by a derived class before instances are used.
req refers to the tracker request that triggered the warning; it must be a valid request instance provided by the library.
msg may be any UTF-8/ASCII text from the tracker; do not assume any specific format.
Implementations must be noexcept-safe or handle exceptions internally to avoid unwinding through the library callback boundary.

functions.name: libtorrent::request_callback::tracker_scrape_response
functions.signature: virtual void tracker_scrape_response(libtorrent::tracker_request const& /*req*/, int /*complete*/, int /*incomplete*/, int /*downloads*/, int /*downloaders*/) {}
functions.description: Optional callback invoked when a tracker scrape response is received. Default implementation is a no-op. Override to observe scrape statistics.
requirements: If overridden, accept the provided counters as-is; negative values indicate unsupported metrics.
Do not throw exceptions from the override to avoid breaking the calling context.

functions.name: libtorrent::request_callback::tracker_response
functions.signature: virtual void tracker_response(libtorrent::tracker_request const& req, libtorrent::address const& tracker_ip, std::list<libtorrent::address> const& ip_list, struct libtorrent::tracker_response const& response) = 0;
functions.description: Pure virtual callback invoked when a tracker announces a response, providing peer lists, tracker-provided IPs, and announce intervals. Implement to consume peers and metadata.
requirements: Must be implemented by a derived class.
req is the original announce/scrape request; treat as read-only.
tracker_ip is the address the tracker resolved to; may be unspecified if unavailable.
ip_list may contain zero or more IP addresses from headers like X-Tracker-IP; do not assume uniqueness.
response contains peers and metadata; fields may be empty or set to -1 when unknown.
Do not throw exceptions from the override.

functions.name: libtorrent::request_callback::tracker_request_error
functions.signature: virtual void tracker_request_error(libtorrent::tracker_request const& req, libtorrent::error_code const& ec, libtorrent::operation_t op, const std::string& msg, libtorrent::seconds32 retry_interval) = 0;
functions.description: Pure virtual callback invoked when a tracker request fails. Provides an error code, the operation, a human-readable message, and a suggested retry interval.
requirements: Must be implemented by a derived class.
Do not throw exceptions from the override.
retry_interval may be zero; treat it as a hint for scheduling retries, not a guarantee.
msg is informational; do not parse for control flow.

functions.name: libtorrent::request_callback::should_log
functions.description: Pure virtual query to determine whether debug logging should be emitted for this callback sink. Used to gate debug_log calls.
requirements: Must be implemented by a derived class.
Must be thread-safe with debug_log if both are used by the implementation.

functions.name: libtorrent::request_callback::debug_log
functions.signature: virtual void debug_log(const char* fmt, ...) const noexcept TORRENT_FORMAT(2,3) = 0;
functions.description: Pure virtual, printf-style debug logging hook. The TORRENT_FORMAT attribute enforces format-string checking. Intended for verbose diagnostics when should_log() is true.
requirements: Must be implemented by a derived class.
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string matching the provided variadic arguments (per TORRENT_FORMAT(2,3)).
Implementation must not throw (declared noexcept).
Only call when should_log() returns true to avoid unnecessary overhead (conventional usage).

functions.name: libtorrent::timeout_handler::timeout_handler
functions.description: Constructor that binds the timeout handler to an io_context for scheduling asynchronous deadline timers.
requirements: ios (the io_context argument) must remain valid for the lifetime of the timeout_handler instance.

functions.name: libtorrent::timeout_handler::set_timeout
functions.description: Configure both the overall completion timeout and the read inactivity timeout used by the internal deadline timer.
requirements: completion_timeout must be a non-negative number of seconds (inferred from typical semantics).
read_timeout must be a non-negative number of seconds (inferred).
Calling this replaces any previous timeout settings.

functions.name: libtorrent::timeout_handler::restart_read_timeout
functions.description: Reset the read inactivity timer baseline to the current time, extending the read timeout window.
requirements: Should be called after receiving data to prevent read timeouts (inferred from name).
Instance must not be canceled (cancelled() can be checked) to have effect.

functions.name: libtorrent::timeout_handler::cancel
functions.description: Cancel any pending timeouts and mark the handler as aborted so no further timeout callbacks will fire.
requirements: Safe to call multiple times; subsequent calls have no additional effect (typical cancel semantics).

functions.name: libtorrent::timeout_handler::cancelled
functions.description: Query whether the timeout handler has been canceled/aborted.
requirements: None.

functions.name: libtorrent::timeout_handler::on_timeout
functions.description: Pure virtual callback invoked when a timeout expires or an error occurs in the timer. Implement to handle timeout conditions.
requirements: Must be implemented by a derived class.
Implementations should inspect ec to distinguish cancellation vs. expiration.
Must not throw exceptions.

functions.name: libtorrent::timeout_handler::~timeout_handler
functions.description: Virtual destructor to allow proper cleanup via base-class pointer.
requirements: None for callers; derived classes may perform resource release.

functions.name: libtorrent::timeout_handler::get_executor
functions.description: Return the associated executor of the internal timer (propagated from the deadline_timer). Useful for initiating asynchronous operations on the same executor.
requirements: Only use the returned executor while the timeout_handler (and its underlying io_context) is alive.

functions.name: libtorrent::tracker_connection::tracker_connection
functions.signature: tracker_connection(libtorrent::tracker_manager& man, libtorrent::tracker_request req, libtorrent::io_context& ios, std::weak_ptr<libtorrent::request_callback> r);
functions.description: Construct a tracker_connection bound to a tracker_manager, a specific tracker_request, an io_context, and a weak callback sink. Base class for HTTP/UDP tracker connections.
requirements: man must outlive the connection instance.
req is copied into the connection; the caller may reuse its original after construction.
ios must remain valid for the lifetime of the connection.
r may be expired; code must handle that (handled internally).

functions.name: libtorrent::tracker_connection::requester
functions.description: Obtain a strong reference to the request_callback, if still alive. Returns an empty shared_ptr if the weak_ptr has expired.

functions.name: libtorrent::create_ut_pex_plugin
functions.description: Factory function that constructs the ut_pex extension plugin for a torrent. The ut_pex extension lets peers exchange (gossip) peer lists to improve swarm connectivity and peer discovery. Typical usage is to provide this function to libtorrent via add_torrent_params::extensions or by calling torrent_handle::add_extension(create_ut_pex_plugin). Direct invocation is possible but usually unnecessary, as the libtorrent APIs will call the factory with the appropriate torrent_handle and client_data_t.
requirements: Must be used in a build where extensions are not disabled (the declaration is available only when TORRENT_DISABLE_EXTENSIONS is not defined).
The provided torrent_handle must refer to a valid torrent associated with a running libtorrent session at the time the extension is added.
client_data_t must be provided as required by the add_extension factory signature (contents are opaque/usage unspecified by this header).
Intended to be passed to add_torrent_params::extensions or torrent_handle::add_extension(); calling context must follow those APIs’ threading and lifetime rules.

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: filesystem path strings used by stubs (save_path, file paths, directories).
# We generate portable, valid, interesting paths with variations: relative/absolute, nested, with dots,
# different separators, and sanitized to avoid traversals beyond fuzzer sandbox expectations.

_MAX_LEN = 256

def _rand_name(rng: random.Random, min_len=3, max_len=16) -> str:
    # filenames without reserved characters. include dots/underscores/dashes for variety
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_."
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # avoid leading dot to reduce hidden-file edge unless chosen
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))
    # collapse repeated separators later; ensure not empty
    return s or "file"

def _platform_abs_prefix(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose absolute path styles for POSIX or Windows
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        # POSIX style
        return "/"
    else:
        # Windows-like: C:\\ or \\?\C:\\ (keep simple)
        drive = rng.choice(string.ascii_uppercase)
        return f"{drive}:\\"

def _join_parts(parts: List[str], rng: random.Random, abs_prefix: str) -> str:
    # Mix separators occasionally
    sep_main = "/" if abs_prefix.startswith("/") else "\\"
    sep_alt = "\\" if sep_main == "/" else "/"
    seps = [sep_main] * 3 + [sep_alt]
    path = abs_prefix.rstrip("/\\")
    for i, p in enumerate(parts):
        path += rng.choice(seps) + p
    return path

def _make_nested_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    depth = rng.randint(1, 4)
    parts = []
    for i in range(depth):
        if rng.random() < 0.2 and i < depth - 1:
            # include a simple dot-dir for variety, but avoid ".."
            parts.append(".")
        else:
            parts.append(_rand_name(rng))
    # last element as file or dir suffix
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        # simulate directory by adding a trailing folder
        parts.append(_rand_name(rng))
    abs_prefix = _platform_abs_prefix(rng) if rng.random() < 0.5 else ("" if rng.random() < 0.7 else "./")
    p = _join_parts(parts, rng, abs_prefix)
    # Occasionally add extension to last
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        base, sep, last = p.rpartition("/" if "/" in p and (p.rfind("/") > p.rfind("\\")) else "\\")
        if last:
            ext = rng.choice([".dat", ".bin", ".tmp", ".part", ".torrent"]) if rng.random() < 0.5 else ""
            last = (last if not last.endswith(ext) else last) + ext
            p = (base + sep + last) if base else last
    return p[:_MAX_LEN]

def _simple_rel(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Simple relative dir or file
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return _rand_name(rng, 3, 12)
    return os.path.join(_rand_name(rng, 3, 8), _rand_name(rng, 3, 12))[:_MAX_LEN]

def _sanitize(p: str) -> str:
    # Avoid parent traversal and NULs
    p = p.replace("\x00", "_")
    parts = []
    for part in p.replace("\\", "/").split("/"):
        if part in ("..", ""):
            continue
        parts.append(part)
    if p.startswith(('/', '\\')):
        out = "/" + "/".join(parts)
    else:
        out = "/".join(parts)
    return out or "tmp"

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Build a small corpus of candidate paths; choose one to return.
    candidates = []

    # 1) Relative working dir-like path
    candidates.append(_simple_rel(rng))

    # 2) Nested path with mixed separators and optional extension
    candidates.append(_make_nested_path(rng))

    # 3) Absolute-like path
    abs_path = _join_parts([_rand_name(rng), _rand_name(rng), _rand_name(rng)], rng, _platform_abs_prefix(rng))
    candidates.append(abs_path[:_MAX_LEN])

    # 4) Dot-prefixed relative path
    candidates.append(os.path.join(".", _rand_name(rng), _rand_name(rng))[:_MAX_LEN])

    # 5) A likely temp-like directory path
    tmp_base = rng.choice(["tmp", "temp", "var", "data"]) + _rand_name(rng, 2, 4)
    candidates.append(os.path.join(tmp_base, _rand_name(rng) + ".dat")[:_MAX_LEN])

    # 6) A path ending with a directory delimiter variant
    tail = _make_nested_path(rng)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        tail = tail.rstrip("/\\") + ("/" if "/" in tail or not any(c == '\\' for c in tail) else "\\")
    candidates.append(tail[:_MAX_LEN])

    # 7) Simple file in current dir
    candidates.append(_rand_name(rng, 5, 10) + rng.choice([".bin", ".part", ".dat"]))

    # Sanitize and pick one
    sanitized = [_sanitize(c) for c in candidates]
    choice = rng.choice(sanitized)

    # Ensure non-empty and within length, and avoid trailing separators except root
    if len(choice) > _MAX_LEN:
        choice = choice[:_MAX_LEN]
    choice = choice if choice == "/" else choice.rstrip("/\\")
    if not choice:
        choice = "tmp"

    return choice.encode("utf-8")
